87	        "body": "### Issue Summary\n\n`CONTRIBUTING.md` \u252c\u00baBuilding tells every contributor to run `yarn build` before pushing, and says nothing about side effects. But `packages/prisma`'s build script is `ts-node --transpile-only ./auto-migrations.ts`, and `packages/prisma/auto-migrations.ts:34` runs **`yarn prisma migrate deploy`** against `DATABASE_URL`. Following the documented instruction with `.env` pointed at a shared, staging or teammate's database applies pending migrations to it, without asking.\n\nSeparately, the \"no database, so skip\" guard does not work. `packages/prisma/is-prisma-available-check.ts:11` returns `false` only for `Prisma.PrismaClientInitializationError` and **rethrows everything else** (`:14`). A refused TCP connection to a Postgres that is not running is not that class, so it escapes the guard, reaches `main().catch()` and exits 1 \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 and the failure reads like a code bug rather than a missing service.\n\n### Steps to Reproduce\n\n1. Have no Postgres listening on the port in your `.env`.\n2. Run `yarn build`.\n\n### Actual Results\n\nExit 1 after about 20 seconds at `@calcom/prisma#build`, with ``Invalid `prisma.$queryRaw()` invocation``.\n\nWith a database present and reachable, the build instead **migrates it** silently.\n\n### Expected Results\n\n`yarn build` should not write to a database, or `CONTRIBUTING.md` \u252c\u00baBuilding must say that it does. With no database reachable, the build should skip migrations and continue \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 which is exactly what the guard was written to do.\n\n### Technical details\n\nMeasured 2026-09-14 on macOS, Node 22.14.0, yarn 4.12.0:\n\n- bare `yarn build` \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 **exit 1 in 20s**;\n- `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1 yarn build` (the escape hatch at `packages/prisma/auto-migrations.ts:17`) \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 **exit 0 in 2m46s**, 13 turbo tasks.\n\nSo the tree itself is sound; the migration step is the only blocker.\n\n### Rough scope\n\n**Small.** Widen the `catch` in `is-prisma-available-check.ts` so connection failures count as \"unavailable\", and add one line to `CONTRIBUTING.md` \u252c\u00baBuilding. Both are a few lines, and the guard change has an obvious unit test.\n\n### Source\n\nHit while setting up the project locally for D1 on 2026-09-14; traced to the two files cited above.\n\n### Additional context\n\nIntended labels: `type: bug`, `scope: small`. Nearest existing labels: `bug`, `effort:low`. I do not have permission to apply labels to this repo, so they are recorded here until someone with triage access can add them.\n",

128	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\nWhen every slot on a booking page is taken, the page is a dead end. It renders `\"no_available_slots\": \"No available slots\"` (`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:2239`) or `\"all_booked_today\": \"All booked.\"` (`:735`), and the visitor leaves with nothing to do.\n\nTwo things are lost at that moment. The visitor has no way to signal that they wanted this host and this week, so they go and book elsewhere. And the host never learns that the demand existed \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 a fully-booked page and a page nobody visited look identical from the dashboard.\n\nMeanwhile the product already handles the other half well: bookings get cancelled and rescheduled all the time, and those freed slots currently go to whoever happens to reload the page first.\n\nThere is no waitlist anywhere in the codebase \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 `rg -ni \"waitlist|waiting.list\"` across the repo, excluding `node_modules` and lock files, returns zero matches.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\nLet a visitor join a waitlist instead of hitting the dead end:\n\n- on a fully-booked booking page, offer \"join the waitlist\" for a specific slot or for a date;\n- when a booking is cancelled or rescheduled away, notify waitlisted people in order with a **time-limited claim link**, so a slot is not held forever by someone who has stopped watching;\n- give hosts a per-event-type toggle, a cap on waitlist size, and a view of who is waiting;\n- let people leave the waitlist from the notification.\n\nThis benefits both sides: attendees stop refreshing, and hosts convert cancellations into bookings instead of into gaps.\n\n### User story\n\nAs someone trying to book a fully-booked host, I want to join a waitlist for the time I need, so that I am told when it frees up instead of having to keep checking the page.\n\n### Rough scope\n\n**XL.** It needs a new Prisma model and migration, a hook into the cancel and reschedule paths to detect a released slot, notification delivery, an expiring claim flow that has to resolve a race between claimants, host settings UI, attendee UI, and i18n \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 and it must respect `EventType.seatsPerTimeSlot` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:222`) rather than assuming one booking per slot.\n\n### Source\n\nReviewing the booking page's own empty-state strings while verifying the local setup on 2026-09-14: the product ships copy for \"all booked\" and has nothing behind it.\n\n### Additional context\n\nIntended labels: `type: feature`, `scope: xl`. Nearest existing labels: `enhancement`, `effort:high`. I do not have permission to apply labels to this repo, so they are recorded here until someone with triage access can add them.\n",

169	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\nThis fork still behaves as though Insights exists, and then does not ship it.\n\n- Migration `packages/prisma/migrations/20230329000000_add_insights_feature_flag/migration.sql` seeds a `Feature` row: `('insights', true, 'Enable insights for this instance', 'OPERATIONAL')` \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 **enabled by default**.\n- The copy ships: `\"insights\": \"Insights\"` (`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:2718`), `\"insights_subtitle\": \"View booking insights across your events\"` (`:2855`), `\"insights_no_data_found_for_filter\"` (`:2720`), and more.\n- The marketing images ship: `apps/web/public/tips/insights.jpg`, `apps/web/public/upgrade/full_insights.png`.\n\nBut there is **no insights route** \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 nothing under `apps/web/app` matches `*insights*` \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 and no insights package under `packages/`. A self-hoster reading the feature-flag list is told the feature is on, and then cannot find it anywhere in the product.\n\nBeyond the inconsistency, the underlying need is real: a host currently has no way to see how their event types are actually performing without exporting data by hand.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\nBuild an Insights page for this fork:\n\n- bookings created, completed, cancelled and no-show over a selectable date range;\n- busiest times of day and week;\n- most- and least-booked event types;\n- cancellation reasons, since the data is already stored (`Booking.cancellationReason`, `packages/prisma/schema.prisma:880`);\n- filters by user and by team.\n\nRead-only, behind the existing `insights` feature flag, reusing `packages/features/data-table` for tables rather than inventing a grid.\n\n### User story\n\nAs a host or team admin, I want a dashboard of my booking history, so that I can see which event types actually get booked and when people cancel, without exporting anything.\n\n### Rough scope\n\n**XL.** Aggregate queries over `Booking` that must not be quadratic or unindexed (`agents/rules/performance-avoid-quadratic.md`), a new repository plus service plus tRPC router obeying the layering rules in `agents/rules/architecture-circular-dependencies.md`, a new route with charts, date and team filtering, i18n, and tests. 210	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.\n  For example, \"I'm always frustrated when...\"\n-->\n\nAs a user, I may want to offer the same event in different locations, such as online or in person. Currently, an event type uses one availability schedule for all of its locations. This can be limiting because I may be available at different times depending on where the meeting takes place.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n## User Story\nAs a user, I want to assign different availability schedules to each event location so that I can offer different meeting times depending on where the meeting takes place.\n\n## User Scenario\nA user creates an event type that offers multiple locations, such as Cal Video and an in-person location. The user has different availability depending on the location.\n\nFor example, the user may be available for Cal Video Monday through Friday from 9:00 AM\u0393\u00c7\u00f45:00 PM, but only available for in-person meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 12:00 PM\u0393\u00c7\u00f44:00 PM. The user can assign a different availability schedule to each location. When someone selects a location on the booking page, they will only see available times for that specific location.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n1. Allow users to assign an availability schedule to each location within an event type.\n2. Allow different locations within the same event type to use different availability schedules.\n3. Display the availability schedule associated with each location when editing the event type.\n4. When a booker selects a location, show available time slots based on that location's assigned availability schedule.\n5. Update the available time slots if the booker changes the selected location.\n6. Continue supporting event types that use the same availability schedule for all locations.\n7. Add or update tests to verify location-specific availability and booking behavior.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Creating new types of availability schedules.\n- Changing how availability schedules themselves are created or edited.\n- Automatically assigning different schedules to locations.\n- Changing the existing meeting location options.\n\n## Open Questions\n- What schedule should be used if a location does not have a specific availability schedule assigned?\n- Should newly added locations automatically use the event type's default availability schedule?\n- What should happen if a user deletes an availability schedule that is currently assigned to a location?\n- ## Design\n\n**Decision:**  \nEach event location will reference an existing availability schedule instead of creating a separate availability system for locations.\n\n**Alternatives considered:**  \n1. Allow each location to reference an existing availability schedule.\n2. Add custom availability hours directly to each event location.\n3. Keep one availability schedule for the entire event type and filter times after a location is selected.\n\n**Rationale:**  \nUsing existing availability schedules avoids duplicating the availability system and allows users to reuse schedules they have already created. It also keeps schedule management consistent with the way availability currently works.\n\n**Consequences:**  \nThis makes it easier to reuse and manage existing schedules and keeps location availability consistent with the current scheduling system. However, the booking logic will need to determine which schedule belongs to the selected location and recalculate available time slots when the location changes.\n\n### Source:\nPersonal use \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 hit this limitation trying to offer video and in-person options with genuinely different available hours.\n\n\n\n\n---\n\n##### House rules\n\n- If this issue has a `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label, don't start coding yet. Wait until a core member approves feature request by removing this label, then you can start coding.\n  - For clarity: Non-core member issues automatically get the `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label.\n  - Your feature ideas are invaluable to us! However, they undergo review to ensure alignment with the product's direction.\n  - Follow Best Practices lined out in our [Contributor Docs](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)\n",

239	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.\n  For example, \"I'm always frustrated when...\"\n-->\n\nAs a user, I may have temporary availability changes that repeat for several weeks or months. Currently, date overrides require users to manually select the specific dates they want to change. This can become time consuming when the same availability change happens repeatedly.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\n## User Story\nAs a user, I want to create recurring availability date overrides so that I do not have to manually select each date when the same availability change repeats.\n\n## User Scenario\nA user has a temporary change in their availability that repeats for several weeks or months. Instead of manually creating an override for every individual date, the user can create one date override and choose how often it repeats.\n\nFor example, if a user is available every Saturday from 10:00 AM\u0393\u00c7\u00f42:00 PM for the next three months, they can select Saturday, set the availability time, choose to repeat the override every week, and select an end date. The system will apply that override to the matching Saturdays until the selected end date.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n1. Add a recurring option when creating a date override.\n2. Allow users to choose how often the override repeats:\n   - Every week\n   - Every other week\n3. Allow users to select an end date for the recurring override.\n4. Apply the override to the correct dates based on the selected recurrence.\n5. Ensure recurring overrides are used when calculating the user's available booking times.\n6. Keep the existing option to create a normal, non-recurring date override.\n7. Add or update tests for the recurring date override behavior.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Adding recurrence options other than every week or every other week.\n- Changing the user's normal weekly availability.\n- Automatically creating recurring overrides without the user selecting recurrence.\n- Creating a new type of availability schedule.\n## Design\n\n**Decision:**  \nRecurring date overrides will store recurrence information and use it to determine which dates the override applies to instead of requiring users to manually create each individual override.\n\n**Alternatives considered:**  \n1. Store recurrence information such as frequency, interval, and end date with the override.\n2. Immediately create a separate date override for every matching date in the recurring series.\n3. Keep the current system and require users to manually select every date.\n\n**Rationale:**  \nStoring the recurrence information keeps the recurring override connected as one logical series and avoids creating many separate overrides for a single repeating availability change.\n\n**Consequences:**  \nThis makes recurring overrides easier to represent and reduces the number of individual overrides that need to be created. However, the availability logic becomes more complex because it must determine whether a recurring override applies to a particular date.\n\n## Open Questions\n- Should users be able to edit an entire recurring series after creating it?\n- Should users be able to delete one occurrence without deleting the entire series?\n- How should a recurring override behave if another date override already exists on the same date?\n\n### Source:\nPersonal use \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 noticed while managing my own Availability schedule that a repeating date-based change required entering each date manually.\n\n---\n\n##### House rules\n\n- If this issue has a `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label, don't start coding yet. Wait until a core member approves feature request by removing this label, then you can start coding.\n  - For clarity: Non-core member issues automatically get the `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label.\n  - Your feature ideas are invaluable to us! However, they undergo review to ensure alignment with the product's direction.\n  - Follow Best Practices lined out in our [Contributor Docs](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)\n",

275	        "body": "## User Story\nAs a user, I want to customize my default landing page after logging in, so that I can reduce repetitive navigation and immediately access the area of the application I use most (such as Bookings).\n\n## User Scenario\nA user logs into the application and is frustrated by always being redirected to the hardcoded Event Types page, as they primarily use the app to check their schedule. They navigate to their account Settings menu and locate a new dropdown for the default home view. They change the selection from \"Event Types\" to \"Bookings\". The system saves this preference and now the next time the user logs in, the routing logic automatically directs them straight to the Bookings page.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n1. A dropdown menu is added to the account settings UI to allow users to change their default home view.\n2. The dropdown must include, at a minimum, the options: \"Event Types\", \"Bookings\", and \"Availability\".\n3. The selected landing page preference is successfully saved to the user's schema/profile.\n4. Upon successful login, the application's post-login routing logic redirects the user to their customized landing page instead of hardcoding the redirect to the Event Types page.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Creating new dashboard views or pages to serve as landing pages (only existing pages like Bookings, Availability, or Event Types will be supported).\n- Setting organization-wide or workspace-wide default landing pages (this is strictly an individual user preference).\n\n## Open Questions\n- Should newly created user accounts continue to default to the \"Event Types\" page before they configure this setting?",

298	        "body": "### Summary\nExpand the recurring event options to support multi-day recurrence patterns (e.g., repeating every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday) and configurable end dates. Currently, recurrence is restricted to simple weekly, monthly, or yearly intervals with a fixed count.\n\n### User story\nAs an event host, I want to configure an event to repeat on specific days of the week and set an explicit end date, so that I can accurately automate bookings for multi-day recurring schedules without manual workarounds.\n\n### Rough scope\nLarge \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 requires building an expanded recurrence selector UI (day-of-week checkboxes and end date picker), updating the recurrence data schema / RRule parsing, and modifying the booking engine's availability calculation.\n\n### Source\nPersonal scheduling use and benchmarking against Notion Calendar recurrence functionality.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.\n-->\n\nFlush out the recurring event options tab more. Have the ability to set an event to repeat on multiple days of the week and have an end date. The screenshot from Notion Calendar is attached which shows what this feature coud look like. \n\n![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2e3833b-e68c-408c-9634-38e1f94a656a)",

327	        "body": "### Summary\nAdd configurable email reminder notifications (e.g., sent 30 minutes or 24 hours prior to a scheduled meeting) for upcoming events.\n\n### User story\nAs an event host or attendee, I want to receive an automated reminder notification before an event begins.\n\n### Rough scope\nLarge \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 requires adding reminder preference controls to the event type form, updating the event schema, and integrating a background scheduling/queue service to trigger emails.\n\n### Source\nPersonal scheduling use and identifying a feature gap during the booking workflow.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.\n-->\n\nWhen creating an event, have an option to receive notifications about upcoming events. For example, maybe a user wants to be reminded of the event 30 minutes before it starts. This notification could be done through an email, but this is just an initial idea. ",

350	        "body": "### Summary\n\nDuring account creation, the username, password and email fields do NOT dynamically update the \"validity indicators\" as you type in text. This means, for instance, you can type in an invalid username, and the system gives you no indication that it is invalid until you actually go to create the account.\n\n### Rough Scope: low\nShould not require database changes; should not require new UI elements, rather changing the logic for when the indicators (which do work correctly to indicate when a field is invalid) update.\n\n### Source:\nRandomly navigating the website to check behavior.\n\n### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\nAs a user trying to create a new account, I want the account creation page to automatically inform me if my desired username, password or email is valid. In this context, valid means not taken and conforming to any rules (e.g. passwords must have at least 7 characters).\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\nI would like to see a little box to appear beneath each fillable text field (password, username, email) that says \"invalid {username, password, email}!\", similar to the one that already appears for invalid emails:\n\n<img width=\"428\" height=\"101\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b71f8415-4058-4cb9-96c3-a6a566aa21e1\" />\n\n### Describe alternatives you've considered\n\n<!--\n  Let us know about other solutions you've tried or researched.\n-->\n\n(Write your answer here.)\n\n### Additional context\n\n<!--\n  Is there anything else you can add about the proposal?\n  You might want to link to related issues here, if you haven't already.\n-->\n\n(Write your answer here.)\n\n### Requirement/Document\n\n<!--\n  Is there any type of document that could support that feature?\n-->\n\n(Share it here.)\n\n---\n\n##### House rules\n\n- If this issue has a `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label, don't start coding yet. 379	        "body": "### Summary\n\nIt can be somewhat confusing to find a specific setting (there are many settings within many subpages of settings). The intent of the feature request is to integrate AI into the search process so the average user can easily find the settings they need. There are other AI integrations through the app store; the idea is that this would be native to the platform.\n\n### Rough Scope: large\nRequires setting up an API endpoint, adding a search box, holding some sort of vector database/database for the AI to search from.\n\n### Source:\nRandomly navigating the different settings of the event types. I figured a feature like this would be useful for the average person who is NOT familiar with Cal.diy.\n\n### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.\n  For example, \"I'm always frustrated when...\"\n-->\n\nAs a new user who does not understand all of the settings yet, I want to be able to type in what I want to do with the application (e.g. if I want to require users to give a reason for cancelling, I would just type \"how do I require users to give a reason for cancelling\") and the system either walks me through how to do it, or points me to the relevant settings (the answer to the example is \"Require cancellation reason\" under the \"Advanced\" settings). Finding the exact setting I want requires digging through lots of text and makes the experience more annoying to navigate.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\nI would like to be able to give a natural language description of the task I am trying to accomplish (e.g. require users to give a reason for cancelling) into the search box, and I see either a drop-down list of potential settings that are applicable to me, or I get a walk through (text instructions) on how to activate the relevant settings.\n\n### Describe alternatives you've considered\n\n<!--\n  Let us know about other solutions you've tried or researched.\n-->\n\n(Write your answer here.)\n\n### Additional context\n\n<!--\n  Is there anything else you can add about the proposal?\n  You might want to link to related issues here, if you haven't already.\n-->\n\n(Write your answer here.)\n\n### Requirement/Document\n\n<!--\n  Is there any type of document that could support that feature?\n-->\n\n(Share it here.)\n\n---\n\n##### House rules\n\n- If this issue has a `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label, don't start coding yet. Wait until a core member approves feature request by removing this label, then you can start coding.\n  - For clarity: Non-core member issues automatically get the `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label.\n  - Your feature ideas are invaluable to us! 408	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\n#4 made it possible to **enter** an event duration as hours and minutes, and #21 implements that\nfor both entry points. But everywhere a duration is **displayed**, it is still rendered as a flat\nminute count \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 so an event you entered as \"1 hour 30 minutes\" reads back as \"90 mins\".\n\nRaised by @zachbowden reviewing #21, with screenshots: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/21#issuecomment-5684917913\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\nAnywhere a duration of 60 minutes or more is shown, render it as hours and minutes\n(\"1h 30m\" / \"1 hour 30 minutes\"), keeping the flat minute form below 60.\n\nKnown places, from that review:\n\n| Where | Code |\n|---|---|\n| Event types listing badge (`90m`) | `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeDescription.tsx:79` \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 renders `{eventType.length}m` |\n| \"Allow multiple durations\" dropdown options | `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/EventSetupTab.tsx:91` \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 `t(\"multiple_duration_mins\", { count: mins })` |\n| \"Basics\" tab subtitle in the event type editor (`90 mins`) | not yet pinned down \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 visible in the editor's left sidebar |\n\nTwo more with the same pattern, not in the original report but worth folding in:\n\n- `apps/web/modules/onboarding/components/onboarding-browser-view.tsx:164`\n- `apps/web/modules/onboarding/components/onboarding-organization-browser-view.tsx:183`\n\nboth `{event.duration} {t(\"minute_timeUnit\")}`.\n\n### Suggested approach\n\n#21 already added a pure, tested `minutesToHoursAndMinutes` helper at\n`packages/features/eventtypes/lib/duration.ts`. A `formatDuration(minutes, t)` built on top of it\nwould give every site above one implementation and one place to test, rather than five variations.\n\nNew strings go through `t()` and `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`. `hours` and `minutes`\nalready exist; a combined form (\"{{hours}}h {{minutes}}m\") likely needs adding.\n\n### Why this is separate from #4\n\n#4 asks to \"split the duration **entry**\", and that is what #21 does. Changing how durations are\ndisplayed touches different components, needs its own strings, and affects screens #4 never\nmentions \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 so it is cleaner as its own change than bolted onto that PR.",

444	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\nBookings is a flat list of Upcoming/Past/Cancelled. There is no way to see an overview of the month in the style of a calendar.\n\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\nAs a host, I want a week and month view of my bookings, so I can see how my time is actually shaped instead of reading a list.\n\n\n### Describe alternatives you've considered\n\n<!--\n  Let us know about other solutions you've tried or researched.\n-->\n\n\n\n### Additional context\n\n<!--\n  Is there anything else you can add about the proposal?\n  You might want to link to related issues here, if you haven't already.\n-->\n\nWeekly view already exists but is not enabled by default. Add monthly view and enable by default in bookings page. Personal use; every calendar tool has this and cal.diy doesn't.\n\n### Requirement/Document\n\n<!--\n  Is there any type of document that could support that feature?\n-->\n\n## User Story\nAs a host, I want a month view of my bookings next to the existing list and week views, so that I can see how my month is shaped at a glance instead of reading a list.\n\n## User Scenario\nA host on a desktop browser opens Bookings for the first time with no saved view. The page opens in Month: a seven-column grid of every week that touches the current month, starting on the host's preferred first weekday, with days from the previous and next month greyed out and today highlighted. Each day lists its bookings with start time and title, placed on the day they start in the host's selected timezone. The host clicks a booking and the existing booking details panel opens for it. The host moves to next month with the arrow, comes back with Today, and switches to Week or List with the view toggle. After reloading, the page opens on the last view the host chose.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n1. The view toggle shows List, Week and Month. `?view=calendar` still opens the existing weekly view and `?view=month` opens the month grid.\n2. A desktop user with the bookings calendar enabled, no `?view=` in the URL and no saved view opens in Month. A valid `?view=` value wins over a saved view, a saved view wins over the Month default, and an invalid value in either place is ignored.\n3. On screens 768px wide or narrower, and for users without the bookings calendar enabled, the list view is shown as before.\n4. The month grid shows every week containing a day of the month, seven days per week, starting on the user's first weekday (Sunday or Monday), for 28-, 29-, 30- and 31-day months and across December to January.\n5. A booking appears on the day it starts in the selected timezone, including bookings near midnight and on daylight-saving change days. A booking that starts on the last day of the grid and ends after midnight still appears.\n6. A month with more than 100 bookings shows all of them, and each occurrence of a recurring booking appears on its own day.\n7. Clicking a booking opens the existing details panel for that booking and does not change the month shown.\n8. While bookings load a loading message is shown, a failed request shows an error, and a month with no bookings shows \"No bookings this month\".\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Dragging bookings to reschedule, creating bookings from the grid, or any other action from the month grid. Actions stay in the details panel.\n- New calendar libraries, database changes or new booking API endpoints.\n- Turning on the bookings calendar for users who do not already have it.\n- The availability grid work in #69 to #71.\n\n## Open Questions\n- Should Month replace List as the default for new desktop users, or only be offered in the toggle? Proposed: default to Month, as the issue asks (\"enable by default\"), but keep any saved choice.\n- Should `?view=calendar` be renamed to `week`? Proposed: no, so existing links and saved preferences keep working; add `month` as a new value.\n- How should busy days with many bookings display? Proposed: the day cell scrolls, so no booking is hidden.\n- Should multi-day bookings appear on every day they cover? Proposed: no, only on the start day, for this issue.\n\n---\n\n##### House rules\n\n- If this issue has a `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label, don't start coding yet. Wait until a core member approves feature request by removing this label, then you can start coding.\n  - For clarity: Non-core member issues automatically get the `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label.\n  - Your feature ideas are invaluable to us! However, they undergo review to ensure alignment with the product's direction.\n  - Follow Best Practices lined out in our [Contributor Docs](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)\n",

516	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\nEvery booking action is one-at-a-time. Clearing a day before you travel, cancelling a week of meetings when you're ill, or marking a run of no-shows all mean opening each booking separately and repeating the same reason into each one.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.\n-->\n\nAs a host who needs to clear a day, I want to select several bookings and cancel them together with a single message to the attendees, so that I don't repeat the same action and the same explanation ten times.\n\n## User Story\nAs a host who needs to clear a day, I want to select several of my upcoming bookings and cancel them together with one shared reason, so that I don't repeat the same action and the same explanation for every booking.\n\n## User Scenario\nA host is ill and needs to clear tomorrow. On the Upcoming bookings tab they tick the checkboxes next to their three meetings for tomorrow. A bar appears showing \"3 selected\" with \"Clear selection\" and \"Cancel selected\". They click \"Cancel selected\", and a dialog lists the three bookings and asks for a cancellation reason. They type \"Sorry, I'm ill and need to cancel today\" and confirm. Each booking is cancelled one after another through the same cancellation the single \"Cancel event\" action uses, so each booking's attendees get their usual cancellation email with that reason. If one cancellation fails, the others still go through, the dialog shows how many succeeded and failed with the error for each failure, and \"Retry failed\" tries only the failed ones again.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n1. On the Upcoming tab, a checkbox appears only on bookings the signed-in user hosts that are accepted, have not ended, and whose event type allows cancelling. Other users' bookings, unconfirmed, past and cancelled bookings, and the \"Today\"/\"Next\" separator rows have no checkbox. Other tabs show no checkboxes.\n2. Clicking a checkbox selects or deselects that booking and does not open the booking details panel.\n3. \"Select all on this page\" selects every eligible booking on the current page, up to 10. Bookings on other pages are never selected.\n4. Changing page, page size, filters or status tab clears the selection.\n5. \"Cancel selected\" opens a dialog listing the selected bookings. Closing the dialog without confirming cancels nothing.\n6. The confirm button is disabled while the reason is empty or only spaces, and while a batch is running.\n7. Confirming sends one cancellation request per selected booking, one at a time, each with that booking's UID, the shared reason and a CSRF token, through the existing `/api/cancel` endpoint. It never cancels all remaining occurrences of a recurring series.\n8. If a request fails, the remaining bookings are still processed. The dialog then shows the number cancelled and the number failed, with each failed booking's error, and successful bookings are removed from the selection.\n9. \"Retry failed\" sends requests only for the bookings that failed. A booking that was cancelled successfully is never sent again.\n10. After a batch, the bookings list refreshes, and cancelling a single booking from its own menu works as before.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Bulk reschedule, bulk no-show marking and other bulk actions.\n- Cancelling a whole recurring series in one action.\n- Selecting bookings across pages or more than 10 at a time.\n- A new bulk-cancel API, database changes or changing booking statuses directly.\n- Sending one combined email to all attendees; each booking keeps its own email.\n\n## Open Questions\n- What does \"cancel them together with a single message to the attendees\" mean? Proposed: one shared reason, delivered in each booking's normal cancellation email, so attendees of different bookings never see each other.\n- Should a batch be capped? Proposed: 10 bookings, because `/api/cancel` allows 10 cancellations per user per minute. A rate-limit error is shown like any other failure and can be retried.\n- Should bookings that need extra cancellation input (such as a no-show fee acknowledgement or an internal note) be included? Proposed: hosts are exempt from the no-show fee and the list's cancel action never asks for an internal note, so host-owned upcoming bookings need nothing beyond the reason. Anything else stays out of bulk selection.\n- Should this also be available in the calendar views? Proposed: no, the list view only.\n\n---\n\n##### House rules\n\n- If this issue has a `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label, don't start coding yet. Wait until a core member approves feature request by removing this label, then you can start coding.\n  - For clarity: Non-core member issues automatically get the `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label.\n  - Your feature ideas are invaluable to us! However, they undergo review to ensure alignment with the product's direction.\n  - Follow Best Practices lined out in our [Contributor Docs](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)\n",

545	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\nCancelling a booking is immediate and irreversible. A misclick currently means manually rebooking and re-notifying the attendee.\n\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\nAs a host, I want a short window to undo a booking cancellation, so an accidental click doesn't force me to redo the whole booking.\n\n\n\n### Additional context\n\nTimed \"soft-cancel\" state, a toast with an undo action, and a background job to finalize the cancellation after the grace period expires.\n\n\n---\n\n##### House rules\n\n- If this issue has a `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label, don't start coding yet. 597	        "body": "## User Story\nAs an event host, I want to configure weekly recurring events to repeat on specific days (e.g., Tuesday and Thursday).\n\n## User Scenario\nAn event host configures a weekly recurring event, selecting specific days (e.g., Tuesday and Thursday) from a new toggle row. When a booker schedules the event, they only see availability for those selected days. \n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n1. When setting an event to repeat weekly, a new row of buttons (Sunday through Saturday) appears, allowing the host to select specific days.\n2. The system requires at least one day to be selected and prevents users from unchecking every day.\n3. The selected days are successfully saved to the event's settings so they apply to all future bookings.\n4. Automated tests must ensure the calendar correctly generates the schedule based on the chosen days.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Implementing specific end dates (\"Ends: Never / On [date]\")\u0393\u00c7\u00f6the system will continue using a maximum occurrence count.\n- Day-of-week selection for monthly or yearly recurrence intervals.\n- Updating the `GoogleCalendarService` sync logic to support the new day selection (to be handled in a follow-up issue).\n\n## Open Question\n- Does the \"maximum of N events\" limit refer to individual meetings or total weeks (e.g., does a max of 8 on a Tue/Thu schedule mean 4 weeks or 8 weeks)?\n\n<img width=\"784\" height=\"678\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18ad2b61-e9e0-4a36-9db7-21184856c7a1\" />",

620	        "body": "### Summary\nExpand recurring event options to support configurable end conditions, including an explicit end date. Currently, recurrence is restricted to simple intervals with a fixed count.\n\n### User story\nAs an event host, I want to set an explicit end date for recurring events, so that I can automatically stop recurring availability after a designated date.\n\n### Rough scope\nMedium \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 requires building the \"Ends\" UI section with an end-date picker, updating the recurrence data schema. \n\n### Source\nIdea taken from Notion Calendar\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\nAdd an \"Ends\" configuration section to the recurrence modal with three distinct options based on the Notion Calendar reference\n- **Never**: Event recurs indefinitely[cite: 2].\n- **On [date]**: Date picker field allowing the host to select a specific termination date\n- **After [X] times**: Input field to cap recurrence by occurrence count\n\n<img width=\"784\" height=\"678\" alt=\"Image\" src=\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7271c92-83e7-4a9f-bb56-af60fca2bfa0\" />",

696	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.\n  For example, \"I'm always frustrated when...\"\n-->\n\nOnce the visual grid exists, users need a way to switch between the existing text-field input method and the new visual grid. Both modes need to coexist so that users who prefer text entry are not forced onto the new UI.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.\n-->\n\nAdd a clearly labeled toggle control (e.g. a segmented button reading \"Text\" / \"Visual\") to the availability settings page. Activating it swaps which input mode is visible. Only one mode is shown at a time. The toggle persists within the session.\n\n### Describe alternatives you've considered\n\n<!--\n  Let us know about other solutions you've tried or researched.\n-->\n\nA permanent side-by-side layout showing both modes simultaneously was considered, but it would be too visually heavy and confusing. A one-time onboarding prompt to pick a default mode was considered, but a persistent in-page toggle is simpler and more discoverable.\n\n### Additional context\n\n<!--\n  Is there anything else you can add about the proposal?\n  You might want to link to related issues here, if you haven't already.\n-->\n\nDepends on Issue #69 (grid component must exist to be toggled in). Issue #72 (state sync) will make switching between modes lossless \u0393\u00c7\u00f6 this issue only handles the visibility toggle, not data consistency. The existing text-field UI must remain completely unmodified.",

725	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.\n  For example, \"I'm always frustrated when...\"\n-->\n\nWith both a visual grid and text fields present on the page, changes made in one mode must be reflected in the other. Without a shared data model and sync logic, switching modes would cause the user to lose their work or see inconsistent availability data.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.\n-->\n\nDefine a single shared availability data model (e.g. an array of `{ day, startTime, endTime }` intervals) that both the grid and text-field components read from and write to. When a user selects cells in the grid, the text field ranges update automatically. When a user edits the text fields, the corresponding grid cells update. Non-contiguous time blocks must be correctly represented in both views.\n\n### Describe alternatives you've considered\n\n<!--\n  Let us know about other solutions you've tried or researched.\n-->\n\nKeeping two separate state trees and running a one-time conversion on toggle was considered, but risks data loss if the conversion has edge cases. A single source of truth with two-way bindings is more robust, though it requires careful handling of the differing representations (cell-based vs. range-based).\n\n### Additional context\n\n<!--\n  Is there anything else you can add about the proposal?\n  You might want to link to related issues here, if you haven't already.\n-->\n\nDepends on Issues #69 #70 #71. This is the most logic-heavy frontend issue. Issue #73 (DB integration) depends on the clean shared state produced here. Pay particular attention to edge cases: non-contiguous blocks, overnight ranges, and rounding when converting between cell-based and time-range representations.\n\n### Requirement/Document\n\n<!--\n  Is there any type of document that could support that feature?\n-->\n\nExisting availability data format in Cal.diy codebase (check current API payload for the save endpoint)\n\n---",

754	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.\n  For example, \"I'm always frustrated when...\"\n-->\n\nEven with a working visual grid and synced state, availability set via the new UI will not persist if the save/load flow is not updated to handle the shared data model. The database integration must be verified to work correctly regardless of which input mode the user was in when they saved.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\n<!--\n  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.\n-->\n\nVerify and update the save and load flow so that the shared availability state from Issue #72 is correctly written to and read from the database. On save, the API payload must be identical in format whether the user used the grid or text-field mode. On load, the fetched data must correctly populate both the grid and the text fields.\n\n### Describe alternatives you've considered\n\n<!--\n  Let us know about other solutions you've tried or researched.\n-->\n\nIntroducing a separate API endpoint specifically for grid-mode saves was considered, but keeping a single endpoint and data format is simpler, less error-prone, and avoids divergence in the backend.\n\n### Additional context\n\n<!--\n  Is there anything else you can add about the proposal?\n  You might want to link to related issues here, if you haven't already.\n-->\n\nDepends on Issue #71 (shared state must be stable before wiring to the DB). This is primarily a backend and integration issue and can be picked up in parallel with late-stage frontend work on Issue #71. Regression testing of the existing text-field save/load path is required.\n\n### Requirement/Document\n\n<!--\n  Is there any type of document that could support that feature?\n-->\n\n- Existing availability save/load API endpoint in Cal.diy\n- Current database schema for availability/schedule records\n\n---",

783	        "body": "### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\nSince #70, the weekly availability grid supports drag-to-select with mouse and touch. On touch devices, a finger on any day cell **always** starts a selection, because the cells use `touch-action: none` so the browser doesn't scroll while dragging.\n\nOn a phone the grid fills most of the screen. A user who puts a finger on the grid to **scroll** (the page, or the grid's own 600px scroll area) selects or deselects time slots by accident. Scrolling currently only works by dragging on the hour-label column or the day header, which users aren't likely to discover. We made this decision to constrain the scope of earlier PRs, but this issue arose.\n\nAs an event host on a phone, I'm frustrated when I try to scroll through my week and end up changing my availability instead.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\nUse **long-press to start a drag on touch input**, the way Google Calendar's mobile app works:\n\n- **Swipe** on the grid: scrolls normally (page or grid), with no selection.\n- **Press and hold** a cell for about 350ms without moving: the starting cell highlights to show a drag has started. Dragging then selects or deselects exactly as in #70: the starting cell's state sets the mode, the drag stays in that day's column, and the grid auto-scrolls near its edges.\n- **Mouse and pen:** unchanged, the drag starts immediately on press.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n1. On touch devices, a quick swipe starting on a grid cell scrolls and never changes the selection.\n2. On touch devices, holding a cell for about 350ms, then dragging, selects or deselects slots with the same behavior as #70, including auto-scroll.\n3. Once a long-press drag has started, the page and grid don't scroll under the finger, except for the grid's own edge auto-scroll.\n4. A long press doesn't open the browser's context menu, the iOS callout, or a text selection.\n5. Mouse behavior is unchanged.\n6. Automated tests cover the hold threshold, cancelling on movement, and mouse versus touch behavior.\n\nImplementation notes (from the #70 design):\n- **Where:** the logic belongs in `packages/features/schedules/hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag.ts`.\n- **Starting the timer:** on a touch `pointerdown`, start a timer instead of a drag. Cancel it if the finger moves more than about 8px first, or if the browser takes over scrolling (it fires `pointercancel`).\n- **Blocking scroll once dragging:** add a native `touchmove` listener with `{ passive: false }` that calls `preventDefault()`. React's touch handlers are passive and can't do this.\n- **Cell styles:** change `touch-none` to `touch-pan-y` on day cells in `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx` so swipes scroll, and suppress the long-press menu (`onContextMenu` \u0393\u00e5\u00c6 `preventDefault`, `-webkit-touch-callout: none`).\n- **Testing:** use Vitest fake timers for the threshold logic. Real scrolling can't be simulated in jsdom, so it needs a manual check on a device or in Chrome DevTools touch emulation.\n\n### Describe alternatives you've considered\n\n- **Keep the current behavior** (cells select, labels scroll). This shipped in #70 because it's simple, but it's prone to accidental selection and the scroll area is hard to discover.\n- **An \"Edit\" toggle** that turns on drag mode, with scrolling everywhere otherwise. Clear, but it adds an extra tap and UI state every time.\n- **Two-finger scroll and one-finger select.** Not a common pattern, and hard to discover.\n- **Dragging only after a horizontal or vertical movement threshold.** That conflicts with vertical scrolling, because drags in this grid are vertical too.\n\nLong-press matches a pattern users already know from calendar apps, so it seems the most intuitive.\n\n### Additional context\n\n- Builds on #70 (drag-to-select). PRs: #<PR #90 >, #<PR #91 >, #<PR #92 >.\n- Related: #71 (grid/list toggle). The grid isn't visible to users until that lands, so this is a usability fix before release rather than an urgent bug.\n- Out of scope: keyboard-based selection, and any change to mouse behavior.\n\n### Requirement/Document\n\n---\n\n##### House rules\n\n- If this issue has a `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label, don't start coding yet. Wait until a core member approves feature request by removing this label, then you can start coding.\n  - For clarity: Non-core member issues automatically get the `\u2261\u0192\u00dc\u00bf needs approval` label.\n  - Your feature ideas are invaluable to us! However, they undergo review to ensure alignment with the product's direction.\n  - Follow Best Practices lined out in our [Contributor Docs](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)",

819	        "body": "\n### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\nPR #85 (closes #6) lets a host set a leave time and a return time on an out-of-office entry. The booking page now removes the slots inside that window, but it does that the way it removes a calendar event: the slots are gone, and nothing says why. A whole-day entry shows the \"away\" panel with the reason, the emoji, the public note and, when a redirect user is set, a \"Book with <name>\" button. A partial-day entry shows none of these. PR #85 names this as a known limit (\"Partial-day entries do not show the \"away\" badge or a redirect on the booking page\") and describes \"alternative 1\" as the path to fix it.\n\n### Describe the solution you would like\n\nBuild alternative 1 from PR #85: teach the per-day out-of-office map about time ranges. Slots inside a partial-day window stay in the slot list, marked `away` with the entry's reason, emoji, note and redirect user, the same data a whole-day entry carries. The booker then renders one \"away\" panel at the place in the day where the window falls, between the slots before it and the slots after it. Away slots stay unbookable, as they are for whole days today.\n\n### User Story\n\nAs an attendee who opens a host's booking page, I want to see that the host is away for part of the day, and book with their redirect user if one is set, so that I know why some times are missing and where to book instead.\n\n### User Scenario\n\nA host works 09:00 to 17:00 and has a partial-day entry from 14:00 to 16:00 with the reason \"Doctor\" and a public note. An attendee opens the booking page for that day. Slots from 09:00 run up to the slot that ends at 14:00. Below them is the away panel with the emoji, the reason and the note. Below the panel, slots resume at 16:00. If the entry has a redirect user, the panel also shows \"Book with <name>\", and the button opens that user's booking page on the same date.\n\n### Acceptance Criteria\n\n1. For a partial-day entry, every slot that overlaps the window is returned with `away: true` and the entry's `fromUser`, `toUser`, `reason`, `emoji`, and the note when `showNotePublicly` is on. Slots that do not overlap the window have no `away` flag.\n2. A slot marked away for a partial-day entry cannot be booked. Booking it returns the same error as booking inside a whole-day entry.\n3. On the booking page, a day with a partial-day window shows the bookable slots before the window, one away panel, and the bookable slots after the window, in that order. This holds when the window is at the start of the day, in the middle, or at the end.\n4. When the entry has a redirect user, the away panel shows \"Book with <name>\", and clicking it opens that user's booking page on the same date, as it does for a whole-day entry.\n5. A partial-day entry that covers all of the host's working hours on a day renders that day exactly as a whole-day entry does, in the time list and in the date picker.\n6. Whole-day entries, holidays and calendar busy times render and block exactly as before. Existing tests for them pass unchanged.\n7. API v2 slot responses do not change. Away slots stay filtered out of them (`slots-output.service.ts:49` and `:119` already do this).\n8. Unit tests cover criteria 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6, including a window on a DST change day in America/New_York.\n\n### Out of Scope\n\n- Setting a redirect user from the out-of-office form. The redirect switch is disabled in this fork (`hasTeamPlan = false`, `CreateOrEditOutOfOfficeModal.tsx:190`, used at `:483`). This issue only renders a redirect that is already stored.\n- Partial-day entries through API v2, which still stores whole days (PR #85, Known limits).\n- Team and round-robin events. Their availability uses `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`getAggregatedAvailability.ts:43` and `:65`), so whole-day entries show no away panel there either.\n- Changes to the out-of-office form or list from PR #85.\n\n### Open Questions\n\n- Which slots count as \"inside\" the window? A 30-minute event at 13:45 overlaps a 14:00 leave time. Criterion 1 says any overlap marks the slot away. The other option is to drop overlapping slots and mark only the slots fully inside the window. A window shorter than one slot interval (for example 14:10 to 14:20) may otherwise produce no away slot and so no panel.\n- What does the panel say for a 2-hour entry? Today it says the host is away with no times. Should a partial-day panel show the leave and return times (\"Away 2:00 PM to 4:00 PM\")? That needs a new string in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` and the times in the attendee's timezone, not the host's.\n- Two partial-day entries on one day (for example 10:00 to 11:00 and 14:00 to 15:00): two panels, or one? The per-day map holds one entry per date today, so this decides the shape of the data.\n- Timezone edges. The map is keyed by the host's date (`slots.ts:189-192` formats the slot in `datesOutOfOfficeTimeZone`). An attendee several hours away can see a host's evening window on their next day. Is it enough that the panel sits between the right slots in the attendee's view, or must the panel also say the host's local times?\n- The redirect cannot be set from the UI or from API v2 in this fork today. Is criterion 4 worth keeping if it can be shown only with a unit test and a hand-edited `OutOfOfficeEntry.toUserId` row?\n\n### Technical Notes (from reading the code, to be confirmed while implementing)\n\nLine numbers are from `origin/main` at `cc65a9670f`.\n\n- **Where partial entries leave the map today.** `UserAvailabilityService.calculateOutOfOfficeRanges` returns early for any entry that fails `isWholeDayOutOfOffice` (`packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts:748`). The predicate is at `packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.ts:228`. The partial entries go to `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` instead (`date-ranges.ts:248`, called at `getUserAvailability.ts:482`).\n- **Why the slots vanish.** The partial ranges are appended to the busy times (`getUserAvailability.ts:651-657`) and subtracted from both `dateRanges` and `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`:659-660`). A whole-day entry is different: it stays in `dateRanges`, so its slots are generated and then marked away, and it is removed only from `oooExcludedDateRanges` through `groupedOOO` (`date-ranges.ts:297-300` and `:354-361`). To get away slots, a partial window must follow the same split: subtract it from `oooExcludedDateRanges` only, and keep it in `dateRanges`.\n- **Booking stays blocked.** `ensureAvailableUsers` checks a booking against `oooExcludedDateRanges` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/ensureAvailableUsers.ts:220`), so once the window is removed there, a booking inside it is still rejected. Criterion 2 needs a test for this.\n- **Slot marking is date-level.** `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` looks up `datesOutOfOffice[YYYY-MM-DD]` and marks every slot on that date (`packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts:187-221`). It needs a time check for partial entries. `IOutOfOfficeData` (`getUserAvailability.ts:209`) maps a date to one entry, so the type must carry the window (for example optional `start` and `end`, or a list per date). See the open question on two entries in one day.\n- **The booker assumes away means a whole day.** `AvailableTimes` shows the panel when every slot is away, or when only the first or only the last slot is away, and it hides every away slot (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.tsx:266-293`). A mid-day window has neither its first nor its last slot away, so no panel renders. It must render the panel at the first away slot of each run. `AvailableTimeSlots` decides that a day is away from its first slot only (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:206`, comment \"since OOO is date-level\"), which hides the time-format toggle when a window starts the day.\n- **The redirect.** The \"Book with\" button is in `OutOfOfficeInSlots.tsx`, which calls `router.push` to `/${toUser.username}` with the date. It already works from the slot data, so criterion 4 needs only the data in criterion 1.\n- **Other readers of `away`.** `DatePicker.tsx:256-269` marks a day as away only when every slot is away, which gives criterion 5 for free. `useNonEmptyScheduleDays.ts:13` and the weekly view `Empty.tsx:66` also read the flag. Check that they do not change for a partial window.\n- **Test that must change.** PR #85 added `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`, which asserts that a partial-day entry \"stays off the away map\". This issue reverses that on purpose. Update the case, do not delete it.\n- **DST.** Keep the `wallClockToTimeZone` parse from PR #85 (`date-ranges.ts:241-246`) for the window edges. `.tz(zone, true)` returns the wrong offset near a DST change.\n\n### Additional context\n\nEstimate: medium (`effort:medium`). The likely files are `getUserAvailability.ts`, `date-ranges.ts`, `slots.ts`, `AvailableTimes.tsx`, `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx`, plus `slots.test.ts`, `date-ranges.test.ts`, `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`, and a new test for `AvailableTimes`. That is about 5 code files and 4 test files, under the 10-file limit in `AGENTS.md`. The slot engine part reuses a pattern that whole-day entries already use, which keeps it medium. The booker change is the part that could grow, because no unit test covers `AvailableTimes` today (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/` has tests only for `Booker`, `BookingDetailsSheet` and `DatePicker`). If the diff passes 500 lines, split it: engine and slots first, booker second.\n\n### Requirement/Document\n\n- PR #85, sections \"Known limits\" and \"Design\", alternative 1: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/85\n- Issue #6: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/issues/6",
