## #5 — Ability to set event theme

- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** The work spans the database (new columns need approval, or the existing `eventTypeColor` JSON gets extended), the event type editor UI, and the booker's styling via `use-brand-colors.tsx`, for about 6–8 files. The logic itself is simple: hex validation, a contrast check, and conditionally applying CSS variables to one event type's booking page. The existing `eventTypeColor` pattern (storage, toggle, contrast warning strings) gives a template, which keeps this from going higher, but open questions about light/dark theme conflicts add some design work.
- **Summary:** Hosts want to set a custom background and text color for an individual event type's public booking page. The setting sits under the layout setting, is off by default, accepts only valid hex values, and warns when the two colors fail a contrast check. Background images, gradients, fonts, team-level themes and email styling are explicitly out of scope.

## #11 — Require a reason when a booking is rescheduled

- **Estimated difficulty: 4/10.** It needs a new Prisma enum and column plus a migration, a dropdown in the Advanced tab, validation on the reschedule path, and tests, so it touches the schema, the event type UI and the booking backend. The full pattern already exists end to end for cancellation reasons (`CancellationReasonRequirement`, `handleCancelBooking.ts`), so most of the work is a parallel copy of known-good code. The main risk is finding every reschedule entry point (attendee-initiated vs. host "request reschedule") so that the validation can't be bypassed.
- **Summary:** Event types can already require a cancellation reason, but a reschedule reason is always optional, so hosts lose accountability when bookings are moved. The issue proposes a `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum with the same four values as the cancellation setting, a settings dropdown next to the cancellation one, and server-side rejection of empty reasons. It was deliberately deferred from the cancellation-reason feature and is scoped as a medium, mostly mechanical change.

## #12 — `yarn build` silently migrates the database `DATABASE_URL` points at

- **Estimated difficulty: 2/10.** The fix touches two files: widening the `catch` in `is-prisma-available-check.ts` and adding a warning line to `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The only subtle part is recognizing connection-refused errors (e.g. Prisma's `P1001`-style errors) as "unavailable" without hiding real failures. A small unit test for the guard is straightforward to write.
- **Summary:** The documented `yarn build` step runs `prisma migrate deploy` against whatever database `DATABASE_URL` points at, so it can silently migrate a shared or staging database. Separately, the "no database, skip migrations" guard only catches `PrismaClientInitializationError`, so a refused connection crashes the build with a misleading error. The proposed fix makes connection failures count as "unavailable" and documents the migration side effect.

## #13 — Add a waitlist for fully-booked time slots

- **Estimated difficulty: 9/10.** This touches nearly every layer: a new Prisma model and migration, hooks in the cancel and reschedule paths, notification delivery, host settings UI, attendee-facing UI on the booking page, and i18n. The logic is hard because the time-limited claim links need race resolution between claimants, and the feature has to respect `seatsPerTimeSlot` instead of assuming one booking per slot. It would need to be split into several PRs to stay within the repo's size limits.
- **Summary:** When every slot is booked, the booking page is a dead end, so visitors leave and hosts never learn that the demand existed. The proposal lets visitors join a waitlist for a slot or date, notifies them in order with an expiring claim link when a booking is cancelled or rescheduled, and lets them leave the waitlist from the notification. Hosts get a per-event-type toggle, a size cap, and a view of who is waiting.

## #14 — Add an Insights dashboard for booking history

- **Estimated difficulty: 8/10.** It needs a new repository, service and tRPC router following the layering rules, a new App Router route, charts, date and team filters, i18n and tests, so it is many files across many packages. The aggregate queries over `Booking` must be indexed and non-quadratic to scale. A chart library may also be a new dependency, which needs approval first.
- **Summary:** The fork still seeds an enabled `insights` feature flag and ships Insights strings and images, but the code behind it was removed, so the advertised feature does not exist. The issue asks for a read-only Insights page showing booking counts by status, busiest times, most- and least-booked event types, and cancellation reasons. It would sit behind the existing feature flag, reuse `packages/features/data-table`, and support filtering by user and team.

## #17 — Allow different availability schedules for each event location

- **Estimated difficulty: 8/10.** Locations are stored as JSON on `EventType`, so linking each one to a schedule needs a schema or JSON-shape change, editor UI, and changes to slot calculation, which then has to take the selected location as input. The booker must re-fetch slots when the location changes, and booking-time validation must also check the location's schedule, or bookings could get around it. The core availability engine is sensitive, and team or round-robin events with multiple hosts add edge cases.
- **Summary:** Event types currently use one availability schedule for all locations, even though a host may be available at different times for video calls than for in-person meetings. The proposal lets each location reference an existing availability schedule, so bookers only see times valid for the location they selected. The existing single-schedule behavior must keep working, and open questions remain about fallbacks and deleted schedules.

## #18 — Add recurring options for availability date overrides

- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** Storing recurrence (frequency, interval, end date) on overrides needs a schema change, plus updates to the override dialog UI and the availability calculation that expands overrides into date ranges. The availability logic has to decide whether a recurring override applies to a given date, correctly across timezones and DST. Unresolved questions about editing whole series, deleting single occurrences, and conflicts with one-off overrides could significantly expand the scope.
- **Summary:** Date overrides must currently be created one date at a time, which is tedious when the same change repeats for weeks or months. The proposal adds a recurring option (every week or every other week) with an end date, stored as one logical series instead of many separate overrides. Recurring overrides must feed into booking availability, and normal one-off overrides must keep working.

## #19 — Allow users to set a custom default landing page after login

- **Estimated difficulty: 3/10.** It needs a stored preference (a new `User` column, which needs schema approval, or a field in user metadata), a dropdown in account settings, a tRPC input change, and an update to the post-login redirect. That is about 4–6 files with simple logic. The main care point is precedence, since an explicit `callbackUrl` should still win over the saved default.
- **Summary:** After login, users are always sent to Event Types, even if they mostly use Bookings or Availability. The issue adds a settings dropdown (Event Types, Bookings and Availability at minimum) that saves a per-user default landing page. Post-login routing then sends the user to that page, while org-wide defaults and new pages are out of scope.

## #23 — Add multi-day recurrence and end date options to recurring events

- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** This changes the recurrence UI, the `recurringEvent` data shape and RRule generation, and the code that creates and checks every occurrence of a recurring booking, so it affects the editor, the booker and the booking engine. Calendar integrations and emails that consume the recurrence rule also need to stay consistent. Much of this scope has since been split into #63 (day-of-week) and #64 (end conditions), so this issue mostly works as an umbrella.
- **Summary:** Recurring events currently support only simple weekly, monthly or yearly intervals with a fixed occurrence count. The issue asks to support repeating on several days of the week (e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri) and an explicit end date, modeled on Notion Calendar's recurrence picker. It needs an expanded recurrence selector, schema/RRule updates, and changes to the booking engine's availability calculation.

## #24 — Send automated email reminder notifications for upcoming events

- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** This fork has no workflows module (`packages/features/ee/workflows` is absent), so it needs new scheduling infrastructure (a delayed job via the tasker/Trigger.dev pattern or a cron), plus reminder settings, schema changes and a new email template. Reminders must be cancelled or rescheduled whenever the booking changes, which adds hooks in several booking paths. Sending at the right time across timezones and with retries adds reliability concerns.
- **Summary:** Hosts and attendees get no automatic reminder before an upcoming event. The issue proposes a configurable reminder (e.g. 30 minutes or 24 hours before) set on the event type and delivered by email at first. It needs event type form controls, a schema update, and a background scheduling or queue service to send the emails.

## #29 — Add dynamic feedback of invalid fields during account creation

- **Estimated difficulty: 3/10.** This is a frontend change, mostly in the signup form: switching validation to run on change or blur and showing the existing error indicators sooner. Password and email format checks are local, but "username taken" needs a debounced async availability check against an existing or new endpoint. No database changes are needed, and only about 1–3 files.
- **Summary:** On the signup page, invalid usernames, passwords and emails are only flagged when the user submits the form. The issue asks for live validation as the user types, with an "invalid …" message under each field like the one already shown for emails. Valid means both well-formed (e.g. password rules) and not already taken.

## #33 — Add AI search support for navigating settings

- **Estimated difficulty: 8/10.** It needs a new dependency (an LLM or embedding provider, which needs approval), an API endpoint, a searchable index of every settings page and option, and a search UI with results or walkthroughs. Self-hosted instances add configuration, API-key handling, cost and graceful fallback when AI is off. The index must also stay in sync as settings change, and LLM answers need guarding against pointing users at settings that don't exist.
- **Summary:** Settings are spread across many subpages, which makes specific options hard to find for new users. The proposal adds a native natural-language search box where users describe a goal (e.g. "require a reason for cancelling"). The system then either lists the relevant settings or gives step-by-step instructions to enable them.

## #35 — Display durations of 60 minutes or more as hours and minutes

- **Estimated difficulty: 3/10.** The logic is trivial: a `formatDuration(minutes, t)` helper built on the existing, tested `minutesToHoursAndMinutes`. It does touch about 5 display sites (event type badge, multiple-durations dropdown, editor subtitle, two onboarding views), plus a new i18n string and tests. One call site (the "Basics" subtitle) still needs to be found.
- **Summary:** Durations can now be entered as hours and minutes (#21), but they are still displayed as flat minute counts like "90 mins". The issue asks that every duration of 60 minutes or more display as hours and minutes, while shorter durations stay as minutes. It lists the known call sites and suggests one shared, tested formatter.

## #50 — Add a calendar view for bookings

- **Estimated difficulty: 6/10.** Mostly a frontend change: a new month-grid component, a three-way view toggle, URL vs. saved-view precedence, and default-view logic for desktop only, for about 6–8 files. Placing bookings on the correct day in the selected timezone (midnight, DST, recurring occurrences) and loading more than 100 bookings per month take careful logic and testing. No schema or API changes are needed, which keeps it out of the high range.
- **Summary:** Bookings are shown only as a flat list, and the existing weekly calendar view is not on by default. The issue adds a month view (a 7-column grid starting on the user's first weekday) alongside List and Week, and makes Month the default for desktop users without a saved view. Clicking a booking opens the existing details panel, and dragging or creating bookings from the grid is out of scope.

## #51 — Add a rebook feature

- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** The "Book again" button alone is small (about a 2/10), because the booker already accepts prefilled name and email through URL parameters. The "People" view raises it: a new page plus a query that groups past attendees by email with counts and last-meeting dates. The issue has no acceptance criteria, so the scope has to be decided before implementation.
- **Summary:** Once a booking ends, there is no quick way to schedule the same person again without retyping their details. The issue proposes a "Book again" action on past bookings that pre-fills the attendee. It also proposes a People view showing who you've met, how often and when last, with one-click scheduling.

## #52 — Add bulk actions to the bookings list

- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** It is frontend-only and reuses the existing `/api/cancel` endpoint, but touches the bookings data table (a checkbox column with eligibility rules), selection state, a selection bar and a confirmation dialog. The batch logic needs sequential requests, a 10-item cap matching the rate limit, partial-failure reporting and "retry failed only" behavior. About 5–7 files including tests.
- **Summary:** Every booking action is one at a time, so clearing a day means opening and cancelling each booking separately. The issue adds checkboxes on eligible upcoming bookings, a selection bar, and a "Cancel selected" dialog with one shared reason that is sent through each booking's normal cancellation email. Failures don't stop the batch, and other bulk actions, cross-page selection and new APIs are out of scope.

## #57 — Grace period to undo a cancellation

- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** It needs a new soft-cancel state (a schema change), an undo toast, and a background job to finalize the cancellation after the grace period. Cancellation has many side effects (attendee emails, calendar event deletion, webhooks, refunds), and they must all be delayed until the cancellation is final, which means restructuring a critical path. Whether the slot is open or held during the grace period is another subtle decision.
- **Summary:** Cancelling a booking takes effect immediately and can't be reversed, so a misclick forces the host to rebook and re-notify the attendee. The issue proposes a short grace period during which the cancellation can be undone from a toast. A background job finalizes the cancellation once the window expires.

## #59 — Selecting use different email at verification page makes username unavailable

- **Estimated difficulty: 4/10.** The fix is probably small: let signup reclaim a username held by an unverified, abandoned account, or clean that account up when the user chooses "use a different email". It needs reproduction and careful conditions so a verified user's username can never be taken over. About 2–4 files plus a test.
- **Summary:** After signing up, choosing "Use a different email" on the verification page leaves the original unverified account in place. That account keeps holding the username, so trying it again shows an "account already exists" error. The bug report is short and gives only the two steps above to reproduce.

## #63 — Day-of-Week Recurrence Selection

- **Estimated difficulty: 6/10.** It adds a day-of-week field to the `recurringEvent` JSON (RRule already supports `byweekday`), a row of day toggles in the recurrence UI, and changes to how occurrence dates are generated and booked. Occurrence generation, the booker's display of recurring dates, and the meaning of the occurrence count all need to stay consistent. Google Calendar sync is deferred, but the RRule must still not break other integrations.
- **Summary:** Hosts can't make a weekly recurring event repeat on specific days such as Tuesday and Thursday. The issue adds a Sunday–Saturday toggle row for weekly recurrence that requires at least one day, saves the selection, and limits booker availability to those days. End dates, monthly/yearly day selection and Google Calendar sync updates are out of scope.

## #64 — Configurable Recurrence End Conditions

- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** It adds an "Ends" section (Never / On date / After N times) to the recurrence UI and an `until` field to the recurrence data, which RRule already supports. "Never" is harder than it looks, because recurring bookings are created as individual rows, so an infinite series needs a cap or a different model. The issue is light on acceptance criteria, which adds some scope uncertainty.
- **Summary:** Recurring events can currently end only after a fixed number of occurrences. The issue adds an "Ends" option with three choices: never, on a specific date, or after a set number of occurrences, modeled on Notion Calendar. It needs the new UI section and an updated recurrence data schema.

## #67 — Website setting to force admin users to enable 2FA

- **Estimated difficulty: 3/10.** Admin 2FA is already enforced in production: `next-auth-options.ts` downgrades admins without 2FA to `INACTIVE_ADMIN`, and `AdminPasswordBanner` prompts them. Most of the work is a toggle (for example a `Feature` flag row with a migration and an admin settings switch) and turning the banner into a non-dismissable prompt when it's on. That is a few files across auth and admin settings, with simple logic.
- **Summary:** Instance admins want to require two-factor authentication for every admin account to reduce the risk of compromised credentials. The proposal adds a toggle on the site configuration page that enforces 2FA for admins. When it's on, admins without 2FA see a non-dismissable prompt at their next login.

## #68 — Website setting to force all users to enable 2FA

- **Estimated difficulty: 6/10.** Unlike #67, there's no existing enforcement for regular users, so it needs a session flag, app-wide gating (e.g. middleware or a shell guard) that blocks use until 2FA is set up, and a required 2FA step in signup. It touches the instance settings, the auth/session layer, the shell UI and the onboarding flow. Edge cases include SSO/OAuth users and API access, and lockout risk makes thorough testing important.
- **Summary:** Admins want to require two-factor authentication for every user on the instance, not just administrators. The proposal adds a site-wide toggle that shows existing users a non-dismissable 2FA setup prompt at their next login. New accounts must complete 2FA setup during signup while the setting is on.

## #71 — Add Toggle to Switch Between Text-Field and Calendar Grid Modes (Subissue of #32)

- **Estimated difficulty: 2/10.** This is a visibility toggle (a "Text / Visual" segmented control) in one component (`AvailabilitySettings.tsx`), with session-level persistence and new i18n strings. It deliberately does not handle data consistency, which is #72. The only dependency is that the grid component from #69 exists.
- **Summary:** Once the visual availability grid exists, users need a way to switch between it and the existing text-field inputs. The issue adds a clearly labeled toggle on the availability page that shows one mode at a time and remembers the choice for the session. The existing text-field UI must remain completely unchanged.

## #72 — Sync State Between Calendar Grid and Text-Field Inputs (Subissue of #32)

- **Estimated difficulty: 6/10.** It touches only a few frontend files, but it is the most logic-heavy part of the epic: two-way conversion between cell-based grid state and range-based intervals in one shared source of truth. Non-contiguous blocks, overnight ranges and rounding to the grid's cell size are all edge cases that can lose data. It has to work with the existing form state and needs thorough unit tests on the conversion functions.
- **Summary:** With both a grid and text fields on the page, edits in one mode must show up in the other, or users lose work when switching. The issue defines one shared availability model (e.g. `{ day, startTime, endTime }` intervals) that both components read from and write to. Particular care is needed for non-contiguous blocks, overnight ranges, and rounding between cells and time ranges.

## #73 — Integrate Visual Availability State with the Database (Subissue of #32)

- **Estimated difficulty: 4/10.** Because it keeps the existing save endpoint and payload format, this is mostly verification: the grid must produce identical payloads, and loaded data must fill both views. The work is mostly regression testing of the text-field save/load path plus small fixes in the form's serialization. The text says it depends on #71, but the shared state it relies on comes from #72, so that dependency should be clarified.
- **Summary:** Availability set in the new grid will not persist unless the save/load flow handles the shared data model. The issue requires the API payload to be identical whether the user saved from grid or text mode, and loaded data to fill both views correctly. A separate grid-specific endpoint was rejected in favor of one endpoint and one data format.

## #93 — Add long-press to start drag on touch devices in the weekly availability grid

- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** The change lives in about 3 files (`useWeeklyGridDrag.ts`, `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx`, tests), but low-level pointer-event handling is fiddly. It needs a hold timer cancelled by movement or `pointercancel`, a non-passive native `touchmove` listener to block scrolling once dragging, and suppression of the iOS callout and context menu. jsdom can't simulate real scrolling, so it also needs manual testing on a device.
- **Summary:** On touch devices, any finger on a grid cell starts a selection, so users trying to scroll accidentally change their availability. The issue adopts Google Calendar's pattern: swipes scroll normally, and a press-and-hold of about 350ms starts the existing drag-to-select behavior. Mouse and pen behavior stays the same, and tests cover the hold threshold and movement cancellation.

## #104 — Show the away badge and redirect for partial-day out-of-office entries

- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** It touches the core availability engine (`getUserAvailability.ts`, `date-ranges.ts`, `slots.ts`), changes the `IOutOfOfficeData` shape to carry time windows, and reworks the booker components so the away panel can appear mid-day. That is about 5 code files plus 4 test files, close to the PR limit, and the issue itself suggests splitting engine and booker work. DST handling, keeping bookings blocked inside the window, and the open question about multiple entries per day all add risk.
- **Summary:** PR #85 added partial-day out-of-office entries, but their slots simply disappear, without the "away" panel, reason, note or redirect button that whole-day entries show. The issue keeps slots inside the window in the list, marked `away` with the entry's details, and renders one away panel between the slots before and after the window. Away slots must stay unbookable, and whole-day entries, holidays and API v2 responses must not change.

When carrying out an approved implementation plan, do only one step at a time and stop after it, summarizing what changed. Do not continue to the next step until the user says so.

**Why:** The user wants to run tests and make a commit after each step themselves (stated while planning Issue #70, 2026-10-08).

**How to apply:** After finishing a step, report the changes and the suggested test command/commit message, then wait. Related: [[user-runs-e2e-and-dev-server-verification]].
---
name: type-check-ci-windows-broken
description: "yarn type-check:ci is broken on this machine (Windows); use yarn turbo run type-check --filter=... --force instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  pinned: false
  originSessionId: 6834d160-5c47-4479-b701-c4cdb11f19b9
  modified: 2026-09-17T15:18:26.813Z
---

In the cal.diy repo, on this user's Windows machine, `yarn type-check:ci --force` reliably fails with `Error: spawn tsc ENOENT` for every package it touches (confirmed identically for `@calcom/app-store`, `@calcom/ui`, and `@calcom/web`). This is not caused by any particular branch or code change — it reproduces the same way regardless of what files were edited.

The root cause is that each package's `type-check:ci` script runs through `tsc-absolute` (a wrapper that rewrites TypeScript's reported paths to absolute paths), which internally calls Node's `child_process.spawn('tsc', [...])` directly rather than through a cross-platform-safe spawner. On Windows, the installed binary is actually `tsc.cmd`, and `child_process.spawn()` without `shell: true` does not resolve `.cmd`/`.bat` extensions the way a real shell does, so the spawn fails to find `tsc` at all.

The plain `type-check` script (without `:ci`) runs `tsc --pretty --noEmit` directly via `yarn`, which correctly resolves the `.cmd` shim, and reports the same underlying type errors — it just skips the absolute-path rewriting convenience. So on this machine, prefer:

```bash
yarn turbo run type-check --filter=<package> --force
```

over `yarn type-check:ci --force`, when verifying type safety in this repo. This has been confirmed to actually run and pass on this machine, whereas `type-check:ci` cannot be used at all until the underlying `tsc-absolute`/Windows spawn issue is fixed upstream or worked around in the repo's tooling.
---
name: user-runs-e2e-and-dev-server-verification
description: "In cal.diy, the user runs e2e tests and dev-server/browser verification themselves rather than having Claude run them"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  pinned: false
  originSessionId: 6834d160-5c47-4479-b701-c4cdb11f19b9
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:36:01.195Z
---

In the cal.diy repo, the user prefers to run Playwright e2e tests, `yarn dev`-backed manual browser checks, and similar verification steps themselves, then report the results back for Claude to interpret and act on — rather than Claude running those commands directly. This came up explicitly ("Please do NOT push or create a PR yet. I will manually run the tests / verification step") and held for the rest of a long session: every e2e run, biome check, and type-check was executed by the user in their own terminal, with Claude only proposing which commands to run and then diagnosing the output they pasted back.

Lighter-weight checks that don't need a running dev server or database (e.g. reading files, `git status`, `git diff`, quick greps) are still fine for Claude to run directly. But for this project, default to proposing e2e/dev-server/full-build verification commands and waiting for the user to run them and share results, rather than running `yarn e2e`, `yarn dev`, or similar directly — unless the user asks Claude to run them.

# Setup Notes — Phase 1 (repo discovery)

Recorded 2026-10-26 by Claude Code. Read-only discovery; nothing was changed in the repo except this file.

## Stack

- **Language:** TypeScript (strict), some JS. Not Go, so the Go-to-UML mapping note does not apply.
- **Framework:** Next.js (App Router in `apps/web/app/`, plus Pages-style modules), tRPC, Prisma/PostgreSQL, NextAuth, Tailwind. Yarn 4.12 + Turbo monorepo.
- **Build:** `yarn build` (`turbo run build --filter=@calcom/web...`). Warning: it runs `prisma migrate deploy` against `DATABASE_URL` (issue #12); use `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1 yarn build` when needed.
- **Tests:** Vitest (`vitest.config.mts`, `vitest.workspace.ts`).
  - All unit tests: `TZ=UTC yarn test`
  - One file: `TZ=UTC yarn vitest run <path>` (use the Bash tool; `TZ=UTC` prefix is POSIX syntax)
  - E2E: Playwright, `yarn e2e` — the user runs these themselves (see memory).
- **Type check:** `yarn type-check:ci --force` is broken on this Windows machine (`spawn tsc ENOENT`). Use `yarn turbo run type-check --filter=<package> --force`.
- **Lint/format:** Biome (`biome.json`): `yarn biome check --write <paths>`; `yarn lint` runs via turbo.

## CI (GitHub Actions)

- `.github/workflows/pr.yml` runs on `pull_request_target` and fans out to lint, type-check, unit tests, API v2 unit tests, security audit, builds, e2e.
- Code PRs (e.g. #110) actually run **Linters, Type Checks, Tests / Unit, Tests / API v2 Unit**. E2E and production builds are skipped (no `ready-for-e2e` label).
- **Security Audit fails** on PR #110 and makes the `required` check fail. This looks pre-existing (not caused by that PR); `/preflight` should report the individual checks rather than only `required`.
- Docs-only PRs skip nearly every job.
- `Validate PR title` enforces conventional-commit titles.

## Repository

- **Owner/name:** `CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy`; **default branch:** `main`.
- **Blob URL pattern:** `https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/blob/main/<path>`. Links only resolve once the file is merged to `main`. Before that, use the branch name in place of `main`.
- **Milestones:** `Sprint 1` (#1, still open: 2 open / 14 closed), `Sprint 2` (#2: 6 open / 0 closed).
- **Release tags:** `v6.2.0-csci435-s0`, `v6.2.0-csci435-s1`, so the Sprint 2 tag is `v6.2.0-csci435-s2`.
- **`gh`:** works. Logged in as `dchan01-wm`, scopes `repo, read:org, workflow, gist`. `gh issue list --limit 3` returned #112, #111, #104.

## Existing templates and docs

- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`: upstream Cal.diy template ("What does this PR do?", "Mandatory Tasks", "How should this be tested?"). It does **not** include the course's Closes/What/Why/Test strategy/Tech Debt structure. `/pr-draft` should follow the course reference, not this template.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md` and `bug_report.md`: upstream templates. The course's verbatim User Story and OB/EB/S2R templates differ and take precedence for D2.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: upstream contributor guide.
- `CLAUDE.md` **is a git symlink to `AGENTS.md`**, a tracked upstream file shared with the whole team. Adding my personal guardrails there would change it for everyone and show up in diffs. See "Decisions needed".
- `agents/` holds the upstream engineering rules (`agents/rules/`), command reference and knowledge base.

## Where Claude config lives

- `.claude/skills` → git symlink to `agents/skills/` (tracked; holds upstream skills `calcom-api`, `vercel-react-best-practices`, `web-design-guidelines`).
- `.claude/rules` → git symlink to `agents/rules/`.
- `.claude/` is listed in `.git/info/exclude` (local only, not committed). So `.claude/work/` and `.claude/course/` are private to this machine. Anything placed under `.claude/skills/` actually lands in tracked `agents/skills/`.
- `~/.claude/skills/` does not exist yet.

## Branch naming used so far

- Course convention used by me and most teammates: `feat/issue-N-slug`, `fix/issue-N-slug` (e.g. `feat/issue-70-drag-to-select-interaction`, `fix/issue-45-copy-link-toast-translation`).
- Split work uses suffixes: `feat/issue-70-a-drag-logic`, `feat/issue-70-b-drag-hook`.
- Docs: `docs/dchan01-wm_AI_logs_sprint1v2`, `docs/dchan01-wm_sprint2_checkin`.
- Some teammates use GitHub's auto names (`105-add-mid-sprint-check-in`) or no issue number (`feat/reschedule-reason-backend`).

## AI logs

- `ai-logs/sprint{0,1}/dchan01-wm/` exist with names following `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<slug>.md`.
- `ai-logs/sprint2/` exists but is **empty** (no `dchan01-wm/` folder yet). The reference requires the folder to exist even if no AI was used.
- `.specstory/history/` has 12 files named `YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SSZ-<first-words>.md`. **Timestamps are UTC.** A session started in the evening Eastern time is stamped the next day (e.g. this session: `2026-10-26_23-42-24Z`). `/log-sync` must decide whether the log date is the UTC date or the local date. See "Decisions needed".
- Some SpecStory files share a start timestamp (e.g. `2026-10-08_01-35-56Z-PR-69.md` and `2026-10-08_01-35-56Z-hey-claude-let-s.md`). `/log-sync` should surface these instead of assuming they are distinct sessions.
- `.specstory` is in `.gitignore`.

## Decisions needed (raise at later checkpoints)

1. **Guardrails location:** `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` is shared and upstream. Options: (a) `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, which Claude Code loads as project memory and which is excluded from git, so personal; (b) `CLAUDE.local.md`; (c) append to `AGENTS.md`, which is team-wide and needs a PR.
2. **Skills location:** project-level `.claude/skills/` really means tracked `agents/skills/`, next to upstream skills and shared via PR. Personal `~/.claude/skills/` stays private.
3. **Log date:** use the UTC date from the SpecStory filename, or convert to local time (America/New_York)?

```text
1	# Cal.diy — Student Setup Guide (Windows-friendly)
2	
3	How to get this project running locally, tested with seed data, with unit + E2E tests — the exact path verified on Windows 11 (2026-07-16).
4	
5	For anything not covered here (integrations, Docker deployment, env-var reference), see the [main README](./README.md).
6	
7	## What you need
8	
9	| Tool | Version we verified | Notes |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| Node.js | v24.x (repo requires >= 18) | |
12	| Yarn | 4.12.0 via Corepack | `yarn --version` inside the repo must say 4.12.0 |
13	| Docker Desktop | any recent | **Only needed for PostgreSQL + Mailhog.** The app itself runs natively. No local Postgres install required. |
14	| Git Bash | ships with Git for Windows | Run the setup commands below in Git Bash, not PowerShell |
15	
16	Clone under a path with **no spaces or apostrophes** (e.g. `C:\dev\...`) — shell scripts in this monorepo break otherwise.
17	
18	> 💡 **New to Next.js?** Cal.diy's frontend and API routes are built with [Next.js 14](https://nextjs.org/docs). The [Next.js Getting Started tutorial](https://nextjs.org/learn) covers the App Router, server components, and API routes — the three things you'll encounter most.
19	
20	> 💡 **New to Prisma?** The database schema lives in `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, and all queries go through the [Prisma Client](https://www.prisma.io/docs/getting-started). The [Prisma quickstart](https://www.prisma.io/docs/getting-started/quickstart-sqlite) explains the schema → migration → query workflow.
21	
22	> 📖 **Architecture overview:** [docs.cal.com](https://docs.cal.com) has developer guides covering the monorepo layout, booking flows, and API design. Read the *Contributing* section before picking a task.
23	
24	## Setup (first time)
25	
26	```bash
27	# 1. Clone (Windows: symlinks flag matters) and install
28	git clone -c core.symlinks=true https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy.git
29	cd cal.diy
30	yarn
31	
32	# 2. Environment file
33	cp .env.example .env
34	```
35	
36	Edit `.env` and set these two (generate values with the commands shown):
37	
38	```bash
39	openssl rand -base64 32   # -> NEXTAUTH_SECRET
40	openssl rand -base64 24   # -> CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY
41	```
42	
43	```bash
44	# 3. WINDOWS FIX — packages/prisma/.env is a broken symlink on most Windows clones
45	#    (it will be a tiny text file containing "../../.env"). Replace it with a real copy:
46	rm packages/prisma/.env && cp .env packages/prisma/.env
47	#    Re-do this copy whenever you change the root .env.
48	
49	# 4. Database (Docker): starts Postgres 18 on port 5450, migrates, seeds
50	yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-up
51	yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-deploy
52	yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-seed
53	
54	# 5. Mailhog (emails during dev/E2E) — http://localhost:8025
55	cd packages/emails && docker compose up -d && cd ../..
56	
57	# 6. Run the app
58	yarn dev
59	```
60	
61	App: **http://localhost:3000** — seeded logins:
62	
63	| Email | Password |
64	|---|---|
65	| `pro@example.com` | `pro` |
66	| `free@example.com` | `free` |
67	| `admin@example.com` | `ADMINadmin2022!` |
68	
69	Browse the database with `yarn db-studio` (Prisma Studio, port 5555).
70	
71	## Running tests
72	
73	### Unit tests (Vitest, ~2 min)
74	
75	```bash
76	NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E="" TZ=UTC yarn test
77	```
78	
79	**Why the `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=""` prefix:** if your `.env` has `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1` (needed for E2E), 7 unit tests fail by design — E2E mode intentionally bypasses SSRF localhost-blocking and forces feature rollouts to 100%. Blank it for unit runs.
80	
81	**Verified Windows baseline (2026-07-16): 4049 passed, 58 skipped.** Two files fail on Windows only (`\` path separators — they pass on Linux/CI): `apps/web/test/lib/next-config.test.ts` and `apps/web/test/lib/pagesAndRewritePaths.test.ts`. Safe to ignore.
82	
83	### E2E tests (Playwright)
84	
85	One-time: `npx playwright install` (downloads browsers) and set in `.env`: `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1`, `E2E_TEST_MAILHOG_ENABLED=1`.
86	
87	Two Windows realities to work around:
88	
89	1. **Don't run the full suite against `yarn dev`** — the dev-mode server hangs under parallel test load (verified: 120s navigation timeouts, then total unresponsiveness). Use a production build.
90	2. **Playwright can't auto-start the server on Windows** — the `webServer` command in `playwright.config.ts` uses Unix inline-env syntax (`NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 yarn ...`) that cmd.exe can't parse (`Process from config.webServer was not able to start`). Start the server yourself in Git Bash; Playwright then reuses it (`reuseExistingServer` is on locally).
91	
92	```bash
93	# Terminal 1 — build once, then serve the production app (stop yarn dev first)
94	export NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"
95	yarn build          # if it fails once on sprite.svg/Biome, just run it again (see gotchas)
96	yarn workspace @calcom/web copy-app-store-static
97	NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 yarn workspace @calcom/web start -p 3000
98	
99	# Terminal 2 — re-seed and run the suite (headless, throttled workers)
100	yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-seed
101	PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 yarn playwright test --project=@calcom/web --workers=4
102	```
103	
104	**Verified Windows baseline (2026-07-16): 243 passed, 3 failed, 27 skipped in ~6 min** (273 total). Known failures:
105	- `icons.e2e.ts` — no `win32` screenshot baseline exists in the repo (Linux-only snapshots); environment artifact, not a bug.
106	- 2 `booking-seats.e2e.ts` reschedule tests — timeouts/element-not-found; rerun individually before treating as real regressions.
107	
108	While developing, run a single spec instead of the whole suite:
109	`PLAYWRIGHT_HEADLESS=1 yarn e2e apps/web/playwright/login.e2e.ts`
110	
111	## Gotchas we actually hit (in order)
112	
113	1. **Port conflicts** — cal.diy needs 3000 (app), 5450 (Postgres), 8025/1025 (Mailhog). Check with `netstat -ano | findstr "3000 5450 8025"` and stop whatever holds them (for us it was another project's Docker container: `docker stop <name>`).
114	2. **`packages/prisma/.env` broken symlink** — every Prisma command fails with `unexpected character / in variable name` until you replace it with a real copy (step 3 above).
115	3. **`yarn build` fails once with a Biome error on `sprite.svg`** (`No files were processed in the specified paths`) — a CRLF/LF line-ending artifact of the Windows checkout. The failing step already rewrote the file, so **just run `yarn build` again**; it passes on the second run.
116	4. **Build memory** — export `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"` (or 8192 on 16 GB machines) before `yarn build`/`yarn dev`.
117	5. **`NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1` breaks unit tests** — see the unit-test section above.
118	6. **Playwright webServer fails to start on Windows** — see the E2E section above.
119

121	
122	```bash
123	yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-up   # if the Postgres container isn't running
124	yarn dev                              # http://localhost:3000
125	```
126	
127	Reset the database to a clean seeded state anytime: `yarn workspace @calcom/prisma db-reset` (nukes the Docker volume, re-migrates, re-seeds).
128	
129	## Contributing workflow
130	
131	All team members have write access to this repository, so the team uses a **branch-based** workflow — not forks. Here is the background and the commands.
132	
133	**Why not forks?** Forking is the standard model for contributing to open-source projects where you _don't_ have write access: you fork to your own GitHub account, clone your fork, and open a PR from your fork back to the original. You will encounter this when contributing to the upstream project. But for your course team — where everyone has write access to the shared repo — it just adds confusion: two clones on your machine, two remotes to keep in sync, merge conflicts that are harder to reason about.
134	
135	**Branch-based workflow** is what most professional teams use internally. You clone the shared repo once, create a short-lived branch for each issue, push the branch back to the same repo, and open a PR from that branch into `main`. One clone, one remote, full PR workflow.
136	
137	### For each issue you work on
138	
139	```bash
140	# One-time setup: clone the team repo (skip if already done)
141	git clone https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy.git
142	cd cal.diy
143	
144	# Before starting each issue: make sure you are on a fresh main
145	git checkout main
146	git pull origin main
147	
148	# Create a branch named for the issue
149	git checkout -b feat/issue-17-dark-mode      # new feature
150	git checkout -b fix/issue-42-toast-dismiss   # bug fix
151	
152	# ... make your changes, run tests ...
153	
154	# Stage and commit
155	git add <the files you changed>
156	git commit -m "feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)"
157	
158	# Push the branch to the team repo
159	git push origin feat/issue-17-dark-mode
160	```
161	
162	After pushing, GitHub shows a **"Compare & pull request"** banner on the repository page. Click it to open a PR from your branch into `main`. Fill in the description (what changed and why), reference the issue (`Closes #17`), and request a review from a teammate.
163	
164	**Branch naming:**
165	
166	| Prefix | Use for |
167	|---|---|
168	| `feat/issue-<N>-short-description` | new features |
169	| `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` | bug fixes |
170	| `chore/short-description` | docs, config, dependency updates |
171	
172	> ⚠️ **`main` is protected — direct pushes are blocked.** All changes go through a reviewed PR. If you accidentally commit to `main` locally, move your changes to a branch before pushing:
173	>
174	> ```bash
175	> git checkout -b fix/issue-42-my-fix   # create branch from your current state
176	> git checkout main
177	> git reset --hard origin/main          # revert local main to match remote
178	> ```
179	
180	**After your PR is merged**, delete the branch to keep the repo tidy:
181	
182	```bash
183	git checkout main
184	git pull origin main
185	git branch -d feat/issue-17-dark-mode
186	```

````python
"""Read-only extraction of user prompts from AI logs for the Phase 2 usage analysis.

Opens every log read-only, never writes to the log folders. Output goes to the path given as argv[2].
Usage: python -I extract_prompts.py <repo_root> <out_file>
"""

import hashlib
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

repo = Path(sys.argv[1])
out_path = Path(sys.argv[2])

SOURCES = [
    repo / "ai-logs" / "sprint0" / "dchan01-wm",
    repo / "ai-logs" / "sprint1" / "dchan01-wm",
    repo / ".specstory" / "history",
]

SPEC_MARKER = re.compile(r"^_\*\*(User|Agent(?: - sidechain)?)\s*\(([^)]*)\)\*\*_\s*$", re.M)
WEB_MARKER = re.compile(r"^## (User|Assistant):\s*$", re.M)

# Tool calls, tool results and collapsible blocks are noise for intent analysis.
NOISE = [
    re.compile(r"<tool-use\b.*?</tool-use>", re.S),
    re.compile(r"<details\b.*?</details>", re.S),
    re.compile(r"<think>.*?</think>", re.S),
]

CORRECTION = re.compile(
    r"\b(no[,.!]|nope|wrong|incorrect|that's not|thats not|not what i|didn't ask|did not ask|"
    r"revert|undo|instead|again|still (fail|broken|not|doesn)|doesn't work|does not work|"
    r"you (forgot|missed|didn't|did not)|why did you|stop|don't|do not|actually|mistake|"
    r"broke|broken|same error|try again)\b",
    re.I,
)
QUESTION = re.compile(r"\b(why|what does|what is|how does|how do|explain|relate|what happens|what would)\b", re.I)


def strip_noise(text: str) -> str:
    for pattern in NOISE:
        text = pattern.sub(" [tool block] ", text)
    return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", text).strip()


def split_specstory(text: str):
    turns = []
    matches = list(SPEC_MARKER.finditer(text))
    for i, m in enumerate(matches):
        end = matches[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(matches) else len(text)
        role = "user" if m.group(1) == "User" else ("sidechain" if "sidechain" in m.group(1) else "agent")
        turns.append((role, m.group(2), text[m.end():end]))
    return turns


def split_web(text: str):
    turns = []
    matches = list(WEB_MARKER.finditer(text))
    for i, m in enumerate(matches):
        end = matches[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(matches) else len(text)
        role = "user" if m.group(1) == "User" else "agent"
        turns.append((role, "", text[m.end():end]))
    return turns


def clip(text: str, limit: int, tail: bool = False) -> str:
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    return ("…" + text[-limit:]) if tail else (text[:limit] + f"… [+{len(text) - limit} chars]")


seen_files: dict[str, str] = {}
seen_prompts: set[str] = set()
records = []
validation = []

for folder in SOURCES:
    for path in sorted(folder.glob("*.md")):
        raw = path.read_bytes()
        digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
        rel = path.relative_to(repo).as_posix()
        if digest in seen_files:
            validation.append(f"| {rel} | duplicate of {seen_files[digest]} | – | – |")
            continue
        seen_files[digest] = rel
        text = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        is_spec = "Generated by SpecStory" in text[:300]
        turns = split_specstory(text) if is_spec else split_web(text)
        expected = len(re.findall(r"^_\*\*User", text, re.M)) if is_spec else len(re.findall(r"^## User:\s*$", text, re.M))
        found = sum(1 for t in turns if t[0] == "user")
        new_here = 0
        for idx, (role, ts, body) in enumerate(turns):
            if role != "user":
                continue
            prompt = body.strip()
            key = ts + "|" + re.sub(r"\s+", " ", prompt)[:300]
            if key in seen_prompts:
                continue
            seen_prompts.add(key)
            new_here += 1
            prev_agent = next((strip_noise(t[2]) for t in reversed(turns[:idx]) if t[0] == "agent" and strip_noise(t[2]).replace("[tool block]", "").strip()), "")
            next_agent = next((strip_noise(t[2]) for t in turns[idx + 1:] if t[0] == "agent" and strip_noise(t[2]).replace("[tool block]", "").strip()), "")
            flags = []
            if CORRECTION.search(prompt):
                flags.append("CORRECTION?")
            if QUESTION.search(prompt):
                flags.append("QUESTION")
            if "[Request interrupted" in prompt:
                flags.append("INTERRUPT")
            records.append((rel, ts, idx, prompt, prev_agent, next_agent, flags))
        status = "OK" if found == expected else "MISMATCH"
        validation.append(f"| {rel} | {status} | {found}/{expected} | {new_here} new |")

with out_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as out:
    out.write("# Extracted user prompts (read-only extraction)\n\n## Validation (turns found / marker count)\n\n")
    out.write("| File | Status | Found/Expected | Unique prompts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n")
    out.write("\n".join(validation) + "\n\n")
    out.write(f"Total unique prompts: {len(records)}\n\n---\n\n")
    for n, (rel, ts, idx, prompt, prev_agent, next_agent, flags) in enumerate(records, 1):
        out.write(f"## P{n} · {rel} · {ts or 'turn ' + str(idx)} · {' '.join(flags)}\n\n")
        if prev_agent:
            out.write("**Preceding AI (tail):**\n```\n" + clip(prev_agent, 500, tail=True) + "\n```\n")
        out.write("**USER:**\n```\n" + clip(prompt, 3000) + "\n```\n")
        if next_agent:
            out.write("**Following AI (head):**\n```\n" + clip(next_agent, 600) + "\n```\n")
        out.write("\n")

print(f"wrote {out_path} ({out_path.stat().st_size} bytes), {len(records)} prompts")

````

2667	- Added the `EventTypeFavorite` join model with composite primary key `(userId, eventTypeId)`, index on `eventTypeId`, and cascade delete constraints linking to `User` and `EventType`. Generated an additive migration script w/ Prisma.
2668	- Created `EventTypeFavoriteRepository` with duplicate-safe `create` (`createMany` + `skipDuplicates`), safe `delete` (`deleteMany`), and `findEventTypeIdsByUserId` (returning a sorted `number[]` array).
2669	- Registered `EVENT_TYPE_FAVORITE_REPOSITORY` and module tokens using unique `Symbol()` keys, set up the module loader recipe, and exposed the public `getEventTypeFavoriteRepository()` getter.
2670	- Added Vitest unit test suite covering argument validation, error suppression, and data transformations.
2671	
2672	## Why
2673	To support starring event types, the application needs a dedicated, reliable data layer that tracks favorites per user without altering shared event data, crashing on duplicate actions, or coupling database logic directly to API routes.
2674	
2675	---
2676	
2677	## Design Decision
2678	
2679	### Decision
2680	Chose to implement a dedicated `EventTypeFavorite` join table instead of adding columns to the existing `EventType` table.
2681	
2682	### Alternatives Considered
2683	1. **Adding an `isFavorite` boolean column to `EventType`**:
2684	   - *Flaw*: An `EventType` record is shared across a team. Marking a boolean flag on the event itself would mark it as a favorite for all team members rather than per individual user.
2685	2. **Adding a `positionBeforeFavorite` integer column to `EventType`**:
2686	   - *Flaw*: Attempting to store an item's previous position to restore upon unfavoriting still requires a database migration, but introduces stale ranking bugs: if other items are reordered while an event is starred, restoring the old rank creates position collisions.
2687	
2688	### Rationale
2689	A separate junction table (`userId`, `eventTypeId`, `createdAt`) cleanly scopes favorites to individual users, enforces uniqueness through a composite primary key, automatically cleans up dangling records via cascade deletes, and separates UI display tiers from persistent list ranks.
2690	
2691	---
2692	
2693	## How It Was Tested
2694	- *Unit tests using Vitest and `prismaMock` to verify repository methods and query arguments without needing a running database instance.
2695	- **Cases Covered**:
2696	  - `create`: Confirms `skipDuplicates: true` is passed to handle duplicate requests.
2697	  - `delete`: Confirms `deleteMany` targets both `userId` and `eventTypeId` and resolves cleanly when records do not exist.
2698	  - `findEventTypeIdsByUserId`: Confirms queries filter by user, sort newest-first by `createdAt`, and transform database rows into a flat array of numbers.
2699	- **CI / Verification**: Local unit tests pass cleanly (`pnpm test`) Migration verified locally via Prisma shadow database.

3037	## Context
3038	Availability is entered today as text-field time ranges (`ScheduleComponent` → `DayRanges` → `TimeRangeField`). Issue #32 adds a When2Meet / Google Calendar style grid that users can drag across, with a toggle between the two input modes. **This PR only builds the grid as a visual element**: it renders the current availability. Drag (#70), the toggle (#71), and two-way sync and persistence (#73) come later.
3039	
3040	Decisions from discussion:
3041	- **Slot precision matches the text fields (15 minutes).** The grid has 96 rows per day, with a label on each hour. The text fields and the grid should look like mirror images of the same data.
3042	- **Only one mode is visible at a time.** The grid takes the place of the text-field Schedule inside the same card. It doesn't sit beside it or stack with it. The toggle button is #71's job.

3044	## Design
3045	
3046	### 1. Shared slot interval
3047	`INCREMENT` in `packages/features/schedules/components/ScheduleComponent.tsx:569` isn't exported. Move it into a small constants file that both components import, so the grid and the dropdowns can't drift apart:
3048	- `packages/features/schedules/lib/constants.ts`: export `AVAILABILITY_SLOT_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (same env var and the same default of 15).
3049	- Change `ScheduleComponent.tsx` to import it. Behavior stays the same.
3050	
3051	### 2. Pure conversion util (the basis for #70 and #73)
3052	`packages/features/schedules/lib/weekly-grid.ts`:
3053	- `getSlotsPerDay(intervalMinutes)`: returns 1440 / interval.
3054	- `scheduleToSlotGrid(schedule: TimeRange[][], intervalMinutes): boolean[][]`. It returns 7 rows (Sunday = index 0, matching the form) of `slotsPerDay` booleans.
3055	  - A slot is selected if it falls inside any range, using the **UTC** hour and minute from `start`/`end`. That's how the form stores times (see `useOptions` in `ScheduleComponent`).
3056	  - An `end` at 23:59 fills the last slot.
3057	  - Use native `Date` / `getUTCHours`, not Day.js, because this runs in a loop.
3058	  - Cost is O(ranges + slots) per day: compute the start and end indices for each range, then fill that span.
3059	- `resolveSlotInterval(interval)`: returns `interval` if it is a positive integer that divides 60 evenly (5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 60), otherwise 15. The conversion and the grid both call it, so a bad env value never breaks the layout.
3060	- The reverse function (`slotGridToSchedule`, which merges adjacent slots into ranges) goes in this same file in #70. It's not part of this PR.
3061

3414	### Summary
3415	Add mouse drag and touch interaction to the weekly availability grid component so users can click-and-drag across time slots to rapidly select or deselect available blocks of time.
3416	### User story
3417	As an event host, I want to click and drag across time blocks on the availability grid, so that I can quickly configure or clear my open schedule without clicking every single slot individually.
3418	### Rough scope
3419	Medium — requires attaching mouse (`mousedown`, `mouseenter`, `mouseup`) and touch event handlers to the grid, managing active drag state with real-time cell highlighting, dynamically determining select vs. deselect mode from the initial cell, and suppressing default text selection during drags. (Excludes synchronization with text inputs and backend/DB persistence).
3420	### Source
3421	Feature enhancement for the availability grid component and scheduling workflow optimization.
3422	### Describe the solution you'd like
3423	Implement responsive click-and-drag interaction across the weekly availability grid with immediate visual feedback:
3424	
3425	### Acceptance criteria:
3426	- Clicking and dragging across grid cells selects them.
3427	- The interaction mode (select vs. deselect) is determined by the state of the initial cell: starting on an unselected cell selects dragged cells; starting on an already-selected cell deselects them ("reverse drag").
3428	- Selection highlights update visually in real time as the user drags.
3429	- Drag interactions are fully supported on touch devices (mobile/tablet).
3430	- Releasing the drag (`mouseup` / `touchend`) commits the new selection to state.
3431	- Accidental text selection and browser drag-and-drop artifacts are prevented during drag actions (e.g., `user-select: none`).
3432	### Out of scope:
3433	- Synchronizing selected blocks with text fields.
3434	- Saving availability data to the database or making API mutation calls.

3448	
3449	## Proposed approach
3450

3836	## The idea in one sentence
3837	A pull request shows the difference between its branch and its **base** branch. Stacking means pointing each PR's base at the **previous PR's branch** instead of `main`, so each PR shows only its own piece.

Here is the full skill list, with the Phase 2 additions folded in. I've put `/checks` in Tier 1 because `/pr-draft` and `/preflight` depend on it. Frontmatter, inputs and outputs come in Phase 3.

## Rules every skill follows
- **Drafts only.** Nothing is pushed, posted, merged, approved, tagged or released without your "yes" in the current conversation.
- **Templates:** fill the repo's original GitHub template first, then add every field the course requires. Course templates marked "verbatim" keep their exact wording.
- **Code claims** cite `file:line` and are marked as verified or unverified.
- **Rules** say where they come from: the course, the team, or `AGENTS.md`.
- **Commands** come with a one-line note on what they do, use Git Bash syntax, and follow `setup-notes.md`.
- **Your questions** are answered in the main conversation, never handed off to background agents.

## Tier 1: needed before Oct 29

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/log-sync` | Copies new SpecStory sessions into `ai-logs/sprint2/dchan01-wm/`. Names them `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<slug>.md` using the **local** date. It proposes slugs for your approval and creates attachment folders. It flags: sessions not yet copied, logs saved partway through a session, files with the same timestamp, and claude.ai logs that mention attached files but have no attachments folder. It never changes a log's contents. |
| `/log-comment <N>` | Finds your logs for issue N and asks your role (Implementation / Code review / Testing / Other). It drafts the **verbatim** AI Assistance comment, with a full GitHub link to each file (never a folder link), and checks that each linked file exists. If no AI was used, it drafts the "No AI used." version. It posts only on your yes. |
| `/preflight <N>` | Checks an issue and its PRs against the grading checklist and gives a pass/fail table with fixes. It checks:<br>• **spec:** template, at least 3 testable criteria, a teammate's spec-review comment<br>• **design:** at least 2 alternatives<br>• **PR:** `Closes #N`, what/why/how tested, test strategy, Tech Debt section<br>• **CI:** each check reported separately<br>• **reviews:** a rubric comment from someone other than the author<br>• your AI Assistance comment with working links<br>• the milestone. |
| `/pr-draft <N>` | Builds the PR description from the issue, your work-folder notes and the diff against `main`. It starts from `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and adds the course fields and the Tech Debt section, with no AI log links. Before drafting it:<br>• checks the diff size; if over 500 lines or 10 files, it suggests a stacked-PR split with the commands explained line by line<br>• checks your branch is up to date with `main`<br>• lists exactly which files to commit and which to leave out (e.g. the `schema.prisma` line-ending change, `.specstory/`). |
| `/uml <N>` | Asks whether you want Mermaid or PlantUML. It builds a class diagram and a sequence diagram showing existing and new/modified code, with a legend and notes on the key design decisions, and renders them to PNG if it can. It creates the verbatim Q&A file `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<N>-dchan01-wm.md`. The answers are left for you; hints are allowed if clearly marked for deletion. It records what it generated, so you can answer the AI-use question honestly. |
| `/checks` *(new)* | Runs the standard local verification: Biome on the changed files only, the type-check for the affected packages, and the related unit tests with the right environment settings. It compares results against `main` rather than the outdated `students.md` numbers, and explains each command in one line. It never runs e2e tests or the dev server; it lists those commands for you to run. |

## Tier 2: core development workflow

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/estimate <N> [--hypothesis "…"]` | Finds the relevant code and works out what else depends on it, then writes `impact.md`: files and systems touched, estimated size, risks, test impact, and a story-point **suggestion** for planning poker. It suggests splitting the issue if it looks large. If you give a hypothesis (code you located yourself), it checks that first, before showing its own findings. |
| `/spec <N>` | Uses `impact.md` to draft the issue body: the original issue template first, then the verbatim User Story or OB/EB/S2R sections. It checks that each acceptance criterion has a clear pass/fail and that the story meets INVEST, flags open questions, and reminds you a teammate must review the spec before you code. |
| `/design <N>` | Proposes design decisions in Decision / Alternatives (at least 2 concrete) / Rationale / Consequences form. It presents the alternatives neutrally and lets you choose, then writes `design.md`. |
| `/implement <N>` | Won't start without a spec and a design, and warns if no teammate has reviewed the spec. It creates the `feat/` or `fix/issue-N-slug` branch once you confirm, writes `plan.md` and waits for your approval. Then it does **one step at a time** and stops after each. Each step report covers:<br>• what changed, why, the assumptions made, how it relates to existing code, and what could go wrong<br>• the tests added or updated, plus results from `/checks`<br>• the exact files to commit and a suggested commit message<br>• the running diff size<br>• a reminder to check the VS Code Problems panel. |
| `/explain [target] [--plain]` | Explains a file, function, commit or "last change" in your usual format: file by file with snippets, what changed and why, assumptions, how it relates to existing code (with `file:line`), edge cases, and what could break. `--plain` gives a plain-language version. |
| `/review-pr <PR#>` | Before forming any opinion, it fetches the PR description, the linked issue, related sibling or parent issues, and the comments. It explains the systems involved and how the change interacts with existing code, and checks acceptance-criteria coverage and whether the tests are meaningful. It traces every suspected bug before listing it (Confirmed / Unverified) and suggests manual verification steps (Mailhog, the seeded test users). It drafts the verbatim rubric with Notes filled and **Scores blank** for you, and reminds you to post it on your first review pass. |

## Tier 3: sprint housekeeping

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/address-review <PR#>` | Goes through reviewer comments one at a time: explains the concern, proposes a fix or a reasoned reply, and waits for your decision on each. |
| `/backlog` | Lists open issues and Sprint 1 carryovers. It flags issues missing specs or estimates, suggests sub-issue splits, and drafts carryover or skip comments. |
| `/checkin` | Drafts `docs/sprint2/checkin/dchan01-wm.md` from your PRs and notes. "Learned" and "would do differently" are left as prompts for you to answer. |
| `/sprint-report` | Gathers the report tables: issues (owner, points, status), PRs (author, reviewer, status), your session count and tools, and links to your diagrams and check-in. Narrative sections are left for the team. |
| `/release-notes` | Drafts the release description from merged Sprint 2 PRs and suggests the tag `v6.2.0-csci435-s2`. It never creates the tag without your yes. |

**That's 17 skills in total:** the 16 from your prompt plus `/checks`.

I answered from the portion of the page shown. The content was truncated before its end, so some details may be incomplete.

## 1. Where skills live and how they're named

The docs list these locations ("Choose where skills load"):

| Location | Path | Loads in |
| :- | :- | :- |
| Enterprise | `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` in the managed settings directory | All users on machines where your organization deploys it |
| Personal | `~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` | All your projects on this machine |
| Project | `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` | Sessions in this repository |
| Nested | `<subdir>/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` | Sessions started in or below `<subdir>` |
| Additional directory | `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` in a directory passed with `--add-dir` | That session |
| Plugin | `<plugin>/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` | Wherever the plugin is enabled, as `/plugin-name:skill-name` |

Legacy files in `.claude/commands/` still work. The docs state: "A file at `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create `/deploy`."

Naming, from "How a skill gets its command name":
- Personal/project skill: "Frontmatter `name` or the directory name" (e.g., `.claude/skills/deploy-staging/SKILL.md` → `/deploy-staging`).
- Nested, on a name clash: "Subdirectory path relative to the working directory, then the skill directory name." Example: `apps/web/.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` → `/apps/web:deploy`.
- Added directory, on a clash (v2.1.309+): `../cli/.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md` with `--add-dir ../cli` → `/cli:verify`.
- Plugin skill: "Frontmatter `name` or the directory name, namespaced by plugin." Example: `my-plugin/skills/review/SKILL.md` → `/my-plugin:review`.
- Commands subdirectory: "`.claude/commands/frontend/component.md` → `/frontend:component`."

**Grouping:** The docs describe grouping through plugin namespaces and through `.claude/commands/` subdirectories, which become colon-separated prefixes. For `.claude/skills/`, a path prefix appears only when a nested skill's name clashes with another. The docs don't describe a general "dev:" prefix feature or a way to group skills into folders.

## 2. Frontmatter fields

"Configure a skill with YAML frontmatter between `---` markers at the top of `SKILL.md`." All fields are optional, and "Only `description` is recommended." The field names must match exactly, and "Claude Code ignores a field it doesn't recognize without reporting an error."

| Field | Description (from the docs) |
| :- | :- |
| `name` | "Command name shown in the `/` menu. Defaults to the directory name." |
| `description` | "What the skill does and when to use it. Claude uses this to decide when to apply the skill." The combined description and `when_to_use` is truncated at 1,536 characters in the listing. |
| `when_to_use` | "Additional context for when Claude should invoke the skill, such as trigger phrases or example requests." |
| `argument-hint` | "Hint shown during autocomplete... Example: `[issue-number]`." |
| `arguments` | "Named positional arguments for `$name` substitution." |
| `disable-model-invocation` | "Set to `true` to prevent Claude from automatically loading this skill." Also blocks preloading into subagents. Default `false`. |
| `user-invocable` | "Set to `false` when only Claude should invoke the skill." Default `true`. |
| `allowed-tools` | "Tools Claude can use without asking permission during the turn that invokes this skill." Space- or comma-separated, or a YAML list. |
| `disallowed-tools` | "Tools removed from Claude's available pool while this skill is active." |
| `model` | "Model to use when this skill is active." Applies for the current turn only. `inherit` keeps the active model. |
| `effort` | "Effort level when this skill is active": `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`. |
| `context` | "Set to `fork` to run in a forked subagent context." |
| `agent` | "Which subagent type to use when `context: fork` is set." |
| `background` | "Only applies with `context: fork`. Set to `false` to wait for the forked subagent's result." Default `true`. |
| `hooks` | Hooks registered when the skill is invoked and kept for the session. |
| `paths` | "Glob patterns that limit when this skill is activated." |
| `shell` | "Shell to use for `` !`command` `` and ` ```! ` blocks": `bash` (default) or `powershell`. |
| `metadata`, `license`, `compatibility` | Spec fields that Claude Code accepts but doesn't act on. |

Example:

```yaml
---
name: deep-research
description: Research a topic thoroughly
context: fork
agent: Explore
---
```

## 3. Arguments

- `$ARGUMENTS`: "All arguments passed when invoking the skill." If no placeholder receives an argument, Claude Code appends `ARGUMENTS: <value>`.
- `$ARGUMENTS[N]` or `$N`: "Access a specific argument by 0-based index."
- `$name`: "Named argument declared in the `arguments` frontmatter list."

"Indexed arguments use shell-style quoting, so wrap multi-word values in quotes." For example, `/my-skill "hello world" second` makes `$0` expand to `hello world`. To write a literal dollar sign, "escape it with a backslash: `\$1.00`."

```yaml
---
name: migrate-component
description: Migrate a component from one language to another
---

Migrate the $0 component from $1 to $2.
```

Running `/migrate-component SearchBar JavaScript TypeScript` substitutes the three values.

## 4. Dynamic context injection

"The `` !`<command>` `` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude. The command output replaces the placeholder."

```markdown
## Current changes

!`git diff HEAD`
```

The inline form must start a line or follow whitespace. "For multi-line commands, use a fenced code block opened with ` ```! `." If a command fails, "a failed command aborts the entire skill invocation." Setting `"disableSkillShellExecution": true` replaces these commands with `[shell command execution disabled by policy]`.

## 5. Supporting files

Yes. "Skills can include multiple files in their directory":

```text
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md (required - overview and navigation)
├── reference.md (detailed API docs - loaded when needed)
├── examples.md (usage examples - loaded when needed)
└── scripts/
    └── helper.py (utility script - executed, not loaded)
```

Reference them from `SKILL.md` with links such as `- For complete API details, see [reference.md](reference.md)`. Scripts can be run via `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, which "expands to the directory containing the skill's SKILL.md file." The docs also advise: "Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines."

## 6. Name format limits

The page doesn't give a full allowed-character list. It doesn't mention underscores or hyphens as restricted. It does list characters Claude Code refuses in a command name or frontmatter `name`:

- A zero-width space or a control character
- A private-use or unassigned character
- A character that changes text direction
- A blank other than one plain space between words, or a space at the start or end
- `<` or `>`

Colons are used as separators in the namespaced forms (`/plugin-name:skill-name`, `/apps/web:deploy`). A frontmatter `name` that already has the plugin prefix isn't prefixed again on v2.1.246 or later, so `name: my-plugin:fancy` becomes `/my-plugin:fancy`. The reserved names are `synced` (as a skill folder name) and `anthropic-skills`, plus anything starting with `anthropic-skills:`. The docs' examples use lowercase, hyphenated names, such as `deploy-staging`.
