When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, or managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, true from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) is ignored (false there still applies).",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "allowMachLookup": {
              "description": "macOS only: Additional XPC/Mach service names to allow looking up. Supports trailing-wildcard prefix matching (e.g., \"com.apple.coresimulator.*\"). Needed for tools that communicate via XPC such as the iOS Simulator or Playwright. Merged across settings sources. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, or managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, values from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "httpProxyPort": {
              "description": "Local TCP port of your own HTTP proxy for sandboxed traffic, used instead of the proxy Claude Code runs. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, network.deniedDomains or a WebFetch(domain:…) deny rule, when managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, or when managed, --settings or user settings set network.strictAllowlist: true, values from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. With network.allowManagedDomainsOnly, only managed settings may set it.",
              "type": "number"
            },
            "socksProxyPort": {
              "description": "Local TCP port of your own SOCKS5 proxy for sandboxed traffic, used instead of the proxy Claude Code runs. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, network.deniedDomains or a WebFetch(domain:…) deny rule, when managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, or when managed, --settings or user settings set network.strictAllowlist: true, values from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. With network.allowManagedDomainsOnly, only managed settings may set it.",
              "type": "number"
            },
            "tlsTerminate": {
              "description": "[EXPERIMENTAL] Enable in-process TLS termination so the per-request filter can see HTTPS request bodies. Provide a CA cert+key, or omit both to have sandbox-runtime generate an ephemeral one for the session. On native Windows an ephemeral CA cannot pass the sandbox trust check, so omitting the paths uses a persistent CA managed by the sandbox runtime (set up and trusted via /sandbox install); configured paths are passed to the sandbox runtime verbatim, which rejects a bad or incomplete pair at sandbox initialization. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "caCertPath": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "minLength": 1
                },
                "caKeyPath": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "minLength": 1
                }
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "filesystem": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "allowWrite": {
              "description": "Additional paths to allow writing within the sandbox. Merged with paths from Edit(...) allow permission rules. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, or managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, values from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. When managed settings or a --settings file set filesystem.denyRead, a Read(…) deny rule or a credentials.files entry (deny or mask), a value from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) under or equal to a denied path, or spelled as a glob or a network path (UNC or automount), is ignored. A value inside a directory sandboxed commands can already write is re-checked before every command and dropped once it has been re-pointed into a denied read path.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "denyWrite": {
              "description": "Additional paths to deny writing within the sandbox. Merged with paths from Edit(...) deny permission rules.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "denyRead": {
              "description": "Additional paths to deny reading within the sandbox. Merged with paths from Read(...) deny permission rules.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "allowRead": {
              "description": "Paths to re-allow reading within denyRead regions. Takes precedence over denyRead for matching paths. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, filesystem.denyRead, a Read(…) deny rule or a credentials.files entry (deny or mask), or managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, a value from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) that would re-open a path managed, --settings or user settings deny reading is ignored, as is one spelled as a glob or a network path (UNC or automount); one carving out of the project's own denyRead still applies. A value inside a directory sandboxed commands can write is re-checked before every command and dropped once it has been re-pointed into a denied path.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "allowManagedReadPathsOnly": {
              "description": "When true (set in managed settings), only allowRead paths from policySettings are used.",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "disabled": {
              "description": "macOS and Linux/WSL only: skip filesystem isolation entirely while keeping network and seccomp isolation. Ignored on native Windows, where the sandboxed process runs as a separate user with no inherent rights, so skipping the filesystem rules would withhold every access grant rather than loosen them — filesystem isolation stays on there. Sandboxed commands get unrestricted read/write access to the host filesystem; network egress is still confined to network.allowedDomains. Intended for deployments whose goal is egress control rather than filesystem containment. Does not change Bash prompting: sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed is independent and still defaults to true, so set it to false to keep prompting for sandboxed commands. Drops the read protection from filesystem.denyRead and credentials.files deny entries for sandboxed commands, since both are enforced by the filesystem layer this turns off; credentials.files mask entries (sentinel binds) and credentials.envVars deny/mask are unaffected. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. If managed settings configure sandbox.filesystem at all, or list any sandbox.credentials.files deny entry, only managed settings can set this: an admin who deployed filesystem restrictions must not have them switched off by a user-writable file. (sandbox.credentials.envVars and credentials.files mask entries do not pin it — env scrubbing and sentinel binds are independent of the filesystem layer and survive this setting.) When unset, filesystem isolation stays on.",
              "type": "boolean"
            }
          }
        },
        "credentials": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "files": {
              "description": "Credential files or directories to protect. `deny` blocks reads inside the sandbox; `mask` substitutes a sentinel inside the sandbox (whole-file, or per-`extract` capture) and injects the real value at the proxy. On macOS and Windows `mask` degrades to `deny`.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "path": {
                    "description": "Path to a credential file or directory. Same resolution as sandbox.filesystem.* paths: absolute, ~ expanded, or relative to the settings file root (project root for project settings, ~/.claude for user settings).",
                    "type": "string",
                    "minLength": 1
                  },
                  "mode": {
                    "description": "Access mode for this path. `deny` blocks reads inside the sandbox; `mask` shows sandboxed commands a sentinel-substituted copy (whole-file, or only the spans captured by `extract`) and the host proxy swaps sentinel→real on egress to `injectHosts`. On macOS and Windows `mask` currently degrades to `deny`.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "deny",
                      "mask"
                    ]
                  },
                  "extract": {
                    "description": "Optional regex for structured masking when mode is `mask`. Applied globally to the file; capture group 1 of each match is a credential value, and only those captured spans are replaced with sentinels — the rest of the file is preserved so a tool that parses it (.netrc, JSON, YAML) still succeeds. Without `extract`, the entire file content is replaced with one sentinel (whole-file masking, suited to single-secret files). If the regex matches nothing, behavior is governed by `onExtractNoMatch` (default `warn`). Accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "onExtractNoMatch": {
                    "description": "What to do when `extract` matches nothing in the file — or, with `decode`, when no candidate survives verification. `warn` (default) emits a stderr warning and leaves the file readable as-is inside the sandbox (fail-open, for credentials that may be legitimately absent); `deny` degrades the entry to mode `deny` so the file is unreadable (fail-closed) — under `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` it is treated as `error`, since read-denies are dropped in that mode; `error` aborts at sandbox setup so nothing runs until the config is fixed. Only meaningful when mode is `mask` and `extract` or `decode` is set; accepted but ignored otherwise.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "warn",
                      "deny",
                      "error"
                    ]
                  },
                  "decode": {
                    "description": "Optional encoded-credential format for `mask` mode. `jwt`: candidates are located with a built-in JWT regex (or the explicit `extract` pattern, if set), verified to actually be JWTs before masking, and replaced with a structurally valid fake JWT so client-side token parsing inside the sandbox keeps working. If no candidate verifies, behavior is governed by `onExtractNoMatch` (default `warn`). Accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "jwt"
                    ]
                  },
                  "maskClaims": {
                    "description": "Names of top-level payload claims to mask inside each decoded value, instead of replacing the whole token. Each named claim present with a string value gets its own sentinel and the token is rebuilt around the modified payload; all other claims are preserved so a tool that decodes the token and reads a non-secret claim keeps working. Requires `decode`. If no named claim matches in any verified token, behavior is governed by `onExtractNoMatch` (default `warn`). Only meaningful when mode is `mask`; accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  },
                  "maskDuplicates": {
                    "description": "If true, verbatim occurrences of each captured credential value outside the regex-matched spans are also replaced with the corresponding sentinel — for a secret repeated where the regex does not reach (e.g. pasted into a comment). Matches raw substrings, so short or common values may corrupt unrelated content; intended for long, high-entropy secrets. Defaults to false. Only meaningful when mode is `mask` and `extract` or `decode` is set; accepted but ignored otherwise.",
                    "type": "boolean"
                  },
                  "injectHosts": {
                    "description": "Optional narrowing of where the proxy substitutes this credential. Only meaningful when mode is `mask`; accepted but ignored for `deny`. If unset, defaults to `network.allowedDomains` — the credential is injected at every reachable host. Each entry must be reachable via `network.allowedDomains` (sandbox-runtime validates this).",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "path",
                  "mode"
                ]
              }
            },
            "envVars": {
              "description": "Environment variables to protect. `deny` unsets the variable for sandboxed commands; `mask` substitutes a sentinel inside the sandbox and injects the real value at the proxy.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "name": {
                    "description": "Environment variable name.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$"
                  },
                  "mode": {
                    "description": "Access mode for this environment variable. `deny` unsets the variable for sandboxed commands; `mask` shows sandboxed commands a sentinel value and the host proxy swaps sentinel→real on egress to `injectHosts`.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "deny",
                      "mask"
                    ]
                  },
                  "extract": {
                    "description": "Optional regex for structured masking when mode is `mask`. Applied globally to the value; capture group 1 of each match is a credential value, and only those captured spans are replaced with sentinels — the rest of the value is preserved so a tool that parses it (a `DATABASE_URL` connection string, a composite `KEY:SECRET` pair) still succeeds inside the sandbox. Without `extract`, the entire value is replaced with one sentinel (whole-value masking, suited to bare tokens). If the regex matches nothing, behavior is governed by `onExtractNoMatch` (default `warn`). Cannot be combined with `decode` (the decode path never consults it). Accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "onExtractNoMatch": {
                    "description": "What to do when `extract` matches nothing in the value. `warn` (default) emits a stderr warning and lets the variable pass through unmasked (fail-open, for credentials that may be legitimately absent); `deny` unsets the variable inside the sandbox (fail-closed); `error` aborts at sandbox setup so nothing runs until the config is fixed. Only meaningful when mode is `mask` and `extract` is set without `decode`. On a mask entry with `decode`, the runtime takes the decode path and never consults this field, so a fail-closed setting cannot be honored — `deny` and `error` are rejected there; only `warn` is accepted. In all other shapes the field is accepted but ignored.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "warn",
                      "deny",
                      "error"
                    ]
                  },
                  "decode": {
                    "description": "Optional encoded-credential format for `mask` mode. `jwt`: the variable's whole value is verified to actually be a JWT and replaced with a structurally valid fake JWT so client-side token parsing inside the sandbox keeps working; the proxy swaps the whole fake token on egress. If the value does not verify, the variable is left unmasked with a stderr warning (fail-open). Cannot be combined with `extract` — the decode path never consults it. Accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "jwt"
                    ]
                  },
                  "maskClaims": {
                    "description": "Names of top-level payload claims to mask inside the decoded value, instead of replacing the whole token. Each named claim present with a string value gets its own sentinel and the token is rebuilt around the modified payload; all other claims are preserved so claim-reading clients keep working. Requires `decode`. If no named claim matches, the variable is left unmasked with a stderr warning (fail-open). Only meaningful when mode is `mask`; accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  },
                  "injectHosts": {
                    "description": "Optional narrowing of where the proxy substitutes this credential. Only meaningful when mode is `mask`; accepted but ignored for `deny`. If unset, defaults to `network.allowedDomains` — the credential is injected at every reachable host. Each entry must be reachable via `network.allowedDomains` (sandbox-runtime validates this).",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "name",
                  "mode"
                ]
              }
            },
            "allowPlaintextInject": {
              "description": "Allow sentinel→real substitution on the plain-HTTP proxy path. Defaults to false: without TLS termination the upstream identity is unverified and the credential travels in cleartext. Set only for trusted-network test fixtures. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "awsPairs": {
              "description": "Explicit groupings of masked env vars into AWS credential pairs for SigV4 re-signing, for non-standard variable names. The conventional AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN trio is paired automatically when masked. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. A member is only usable when its env var is forwarded as a whole-value `mask` entry (an entry carrying `extract` or `decode` does not qualify — re-signing needs the whole real value). A pair whose key id or secret member is unusable never re-signs: it is dropped, unless it names a conventional AWS variable, in which case it is forwarded as an inert suppressor so implicit auto-pairing stays overridden. A pair whose ONLY unusable member is the session token still re-signs, without an x-amz-security-token (temporary-credential requests fail upstream until the entry is fixed).",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "accessKeyIdVar": {
                    "description": "Name of the masked env var holding the AWS access key id.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$"
                  },
                  "secretAccessKeyVar": {
                    "description": "Name of the masked env var holding the AWS secret access key.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$"
                  },
                  "sessionTokenVar": {
                    "description": "Optional name of the masked env var holding the AWS session token (temporary credentials). When set, the proxy sends the real token as x-amz-security-token on re-signed requests and adds it to the signed header set if the client did not.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "accessKeyIdVar",
                  "secretAccessKeyVar"
                ]
              }
            },
            "sigv4": {
              "description": "Policies for AWS SigV4 request shapes the proxy cannot re-sign (streaming, presigned, sigv4a) when they reference a masked credential pair: `deny` (default) or `passthrough`. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "streaming": {
                  "description": "Policy for aws-chunked streaming uploads (x-amz-content-sha256: STREAMING-*): per-chunk signatures chain off the seed signature, so re-signing would require rewriting the body. `deny` (default) fails closed with a 403; `passthrough` forwards the request unre-signed (the upstream will reject its signature).",
                  "type": "string",
                  "enum": [
                    "deny",
                    "passthrough"
                  ]
                },
                "presigned": {
                  "description": "Policy for presigned URLs (X-Amz-Algorithm/X-Amz-Signature in the query, no Authorization header): the signature lives in the URL itself. `deny` (default) or `passthrough`.",
                  "type": "string",
                  "enum": [
                    "deny",
                    "passthrough"
                  ]
                },
                "sigv4a": {
                  "description": "Policy for SigV4A (AWS4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256) asymmetric signatures: there is no shared-key HMAC to recompute. `deny` (default) or `passthrough`.",
                  "type": "string",
                  "enum": [
                    "deny",
                    "passthrough"
                  ]
                }
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "ignoreViolations": {
          "description": "Sandbox violations to leave unreported: a map of command patterns (\"*\" for every command) to the filesystem paths whose violations are ignored. Merged across settings sources. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, or managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, values from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
          "type": "object",
          "propertyNames": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          }
        },
        "enableWeakerNestedSandbox": {
          "description": "Linux only: Run without the fresh /proc mount, for hosts such as unprivileged Docker containers that cannot create one. **Reduces security** — the host /proc stays readable by sandboxed commands. Default: false. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, or managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, true from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) is ignored (false there still applies).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "allowNestedUserNamespaces": {
          "description": "Linux/WSL only: Let sandboxed commands create user namespaces of their own, which the sandbox refuses by default. Needed by tools that sandbox themselves that way, such as Chromium's and Electron's sandbox, a nested bubblewrap, and `unshare`. **Removes code-execution isolation** — in any folder a hostile command may write, it can then bypass filesystem.denyWrite, filesystem.denyRead, credentials.files entries and the paths the sandbox always write-protects (such as .claude/settings.json, git hooks and git config), and so plant code that later runs outside the sandbox; while autoAllowBashIfSandboxed is on, the command that plants it needs no approval. Default: false. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings — true from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) is ignored (false there still applies).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enableWeakerNetworkIsolation": {
          "description": "macOS only: Allow access to com.apple.trustd.agent in the sandbox. Needed for Go-based CLI tools (gh, gcloud, terraform, etc.) to verify TLS certificates when using httpProxyPort with a MITM proxy and custom CA. **Reduces security** — opens a potential data exfiltration vector through the trustd service. Default: false. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, or managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, true from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) is ignored (false there still applies).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "allowAppleEvents": {
          "description": "macOS only: Allow sandboxed commands to send Apple Events (and look up the appleeventsd Mach service). Needed for `open`, `osascript`, and browser-based auth flows that open URLs. **Removes code-execution isolation** — sandboxed commands can launch other applications unsandboxed with no user prompt, and can script running apps (e.g. Terminal) subject to the user's per-app TCC automation consent. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. Default: false",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excludedCommands": {
          "description": "Command patterns (Bash permission-rule syntax) that always run outside the sandbox. A convenience, not a security boundary: excluded commands still go through the permission flow. Merged across settings sources. When managed settings or a --settings file set allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, or managed settings set network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: true, values from project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "ripgrep": {
          "description": "Custom ripgrep configuration for bundled ripgrep support. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "command": {
              "type": "string"
            },
            "args": {
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "command"
          ]
        },
        "bwrapPath": {
          "description": "Linux/WSL only: Absolute path to the bwrap (bubblewrap) binary. Overrides auto-detection via PATH. Only honored from admin-controlled managed settings.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "socatPath": {
          "description": "Linux/WSL only: Absolute path to the socat binary used for the sandbox network proxy. Overrides auto-detection via PATH. Only honored from admin-controlled managed settings.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "additionalProperties": {}
    },
    "feedbackSurveyRate": {
      "description": "Probability (0–1) that the session quality survey appears when eligible. 0.05 is a reasonable starting point.",
      "type": "number",
      "minimum": 0,
      "maximum": 1
    },
    "feedbackDrafts": {
      "description": "Model-drafted feedback (the SendFeedback tool). \"notify\" (default) shows a one-line notice when a draft is queued; \"quiet\" shows only the footer counter; \"off\" disables the tool entirely so drafts are never queued.",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "notify",
        "quiet",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "spinnerTipsEnabled": {
      "description": "Whether to show tips in the spinner",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "spinnerVerbs": {
      "description": "Customize spinner verbs. mode: \"append\" adds verbs to defaults, \"replace\" uses only your verbs.",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "mode": {
          "type": "string",
          "enum": [
            "append",
            "replace"
          ]
        },
        "verbs": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        }
      },

        "verbs"
      ]

    "spinnerTipsOverride": {
      "description": "Add your organization's own tips to the spinner tip rotation. tips: strings or {id, text, cooldownSessions?, priority?} objects; tipsFile: a JSON file of the same; label: prefix shown before your tips; excludeDefault: if true, only show your tips (default: false).",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "excludeDefault": {
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "tips": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "anyOf": [
              {
                "type": "string"
              },
              {
                "description": "{ id: stable id (letters, digits, \".\", \"_\", \"-\"; max 64), text: the tip (max 500 characters, one line), cooldownSessions?: sessions to wait before showing it again (default 0), priority?: tie-break weight among never-shown tips (default 0) }",
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {},
                "additionalProperties": {}
              }
            ]
          }
        },
        "tipsFile": {
          "description": "Absolute or ~/ local path to a JSON file holding an array of tips (same shapes as `tips`); honored from user, --settings and on-disk managed settings only. Read once per CLI process (restart to pick up edits).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "label": {
          "description": "Prefix shown before your tips in the spinner (default \"Tip\")",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "additionalProperties": {}
    },
    "syntaxHighlightingDisabled": {
      "description": "Whether to disable syntax highlighting in diffs",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "maxProseWidth": {
      "description": "Maximum width, in terminal columns, of the prose in Claude's responses (paragraphs, headings, lists, blockquotes). In a wider terminal the prose wraps at this width while tables and code blocks keep the full width; only the display wraps, the response text itself gains no line breaks. Minimum 40. Unset (the default) uses the full terminal width.",
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 40,
      "maximum": 9007199254740991
    },
    "spellcheck": {
      "description": "Underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using an installed aspell, hunspell or ispell (off unless \"enabled\" is true; does nothing if none is installed). Read from user, flag and managed settings only (the whole block from the highest-precedence of those applies); ignored in project .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json.",
      "type": "object",

## Proposed deny rules for `.claude/settings.local.json`

The file doesn't exist yet. Because it sits inside `.claude/`, which is already excluded, it never reaches GitHub. A deny rule blocks a command outright, even if you or a skill's settings would otherwise allow it. Every pattern below would be added twice, once as `Bash(…)` and once as `PowerShell(…)`, since I can use either shell here. A trailing ` *` matches the command with or without arguments.

| Group | Patterns |
|---|---|
| **History and commits** | `git commit *`, `git add *`, `git rm *`, `git mv *`, `git revert *`, `git cherry-pick *`, `git am *` |
| **Remote** | `git push *`, `git pull *` |
| **Branches and working tree** | `git branch *`, `git checkout *`, `git switch *`, `git restore *`, `git stash *`, `git merge *`, `git rebase *`, `git reset *`, `git clean *`, `git tag *` |
| **gh PRs** | `gh pr create *`, `merge`, `review`, `comment`, `edit`, `close`, `reopen`, `ready`, `checkout` |
| **gh issues** | `gh issue create *`, `comment`, `edit`, `close`, `reopen`, `delete`, `transfer`, `lock`, `develop` |
| **gh repo and other** | `gh release *`, `gh label *`, `gh secret *`, `gh variable *`, `gh workflow run *`, `gh run rerun *`, `gh run cancel *`, `gh repo create/delete/edit/fork/sync/rename/archive *` |
| **gh api writes** | `gh api *-X *`, `gh api *--method *`, `gh api *-f *`, `gh api *-F *`, `gh api *--field *`, `gh api *--raw-field *`, `gh api *--input *` |

**Two changes from the proposal:**
- **`git branch *` is blocked completely.** Listing branches and creating them start the same way, so they can't be told apart by pattern. Skills will read the current branch with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` instead.
- **`git add` and `git checkout` are added.** You said you commit by hand, and switching branches would change your working tree under you.

**Side effects:**
- `gh api -X GET` is also blocked. Skills use plain `gh api <path>`, which is already a read.
- `git fetch`, `status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `rev-parse`, `ls-files` and `cat-file` stay allowed.

**Limitation:** these rules match how a command starts, so they're a safety net, not a guarantee. A command routed another way would get past them, such as `git -C <dir> push` or `bash -c "git push"`. The skill rules separately forbid these, and any command not already allowed still asks you first.

Should I save this list as shown? Once saved, I'll create `skill-rules.md` and `current-sprint.md`, move the catalog, and set up the guardrails file.

# How Claude remembers your project

> Give Claude persistent instructions with CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md files, and let Claude accumulate learnings automatically with auto memory.

Each Claude Code session begins with a fresh context window. Two mechanisms carry knowledge across sessions:

* **CLAUDE.md files**: instructions you write to give Claude persistent context. Claude can also read a repository's [`AGENTS.md` files](#agents-md) in place of CLAUDE.md
* **Auto memory**: notes Claude writes itself based on your corrections and preferences

This page covers how to:

* [Write and organize CLAUDE.md files](#claude-md-files)
* [Use an existing AGENTS.md](#agents-md) as your project instructions
* [Scope rules to specific file types](#organize-rules-with-claude/rules/) with `.claude/rules/`
* [Configure auto memory](#auto-memory) so Claude takes notes automatically
* [Troubleshoot](#troubleshoot-memory-issues) when instructions aren't being followed

## CLAUDE.md vs auto memory

Claude Code has two complementary memory systems. Both are loaded at the start of every conversation. Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a [PreToolUse hook](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md) instead. The more specific and concise your instructions, the more consistently Claude follows them.

| | CLAUDE.md files | Auto memory |
| :- | :- | :- |
| **Who writes it** | You | Claude |
| **What it contains** | Instructions and rules | Learnings and patterns |
| **Scope** | Project, user, or org | Per repository, shared across worktrees |
| **Loaded into** | Every session | Every session (first 200 lines or 25KB) |
...

These rules override anything else in a skill. If a step seems to need breaking one, stop and ask.

   - a draft commit message;

378	
379	Log every project-related AI session as a full transcript, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`, in `ai-logs/sprint2/<your-github-username>/` — never in a teammate's folder.

381	**What to log.** Writing, debugging or reviewing code; understanding the codebase or an issue; drafting issues, PR descriptions or docs; design discussions. Unproductive sessions count too. Not required: purely academic questions, unrelated research, or clarifying assignment instructions. When in doubt, log it.
382	
383	**File name parts.** Date = the day the session started (`2026-10-15`). Tool = identifier below. Slug = brief, lowercase, hyphens (`issue-42-auth-fix`).

385	| Tool | Identifier | How to capture |

```mjs
// Read-only scan for /log-sync. Never writes, moves or edits any file.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/log-scan.mjs [extra-dir-with-web-exports]
//
// Compares SpecStory sessions in .specstory/history/ with the logs already in
// ai-logs/sprint*/<user>/ and prints a markdown report.
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, basename } from "node:path";

const CONFIG = ".claude/course/current-sprint.md";
const HISTORY = ".specstory/history";

function configValue(text, key) {
  const row = text.split("\n").find((l) => l.startsWith(`| ${key} |`));
  if (!row) throw new Error(`"${key}" row missing from ${CONFIG}`);
  return row.split("|")[2].trim().replace(/`/g, "");
}

const config = readFileSync(CONFIG, "utf8");
const [sprintFrom, sprintTo] = configValue(config, "Dates").split(" to ");
const timeZone = configValue(config, "Time zone");
const user = configValue(config, "GitHub user");
const destDir = configValue(config, "AI log folder").replace(/\/$/, "");

// SpecStory names files by UTC start time; the course wants the local start date.
function localDate(utcStamp) {
  const m = utcStamp.match(/^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})_(\d{2})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})Z/);
  if (!m) return null;
  const d = new Date(Date.UTC(+m[1], +m[2] - 1, +m[3], +m[4], +m[5], +m[6]));
  const fmt = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", { timeZone, year: "numeric", month: "2-digit", day: "2-digit", hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit", hour12: false });
  const p = Object.fromEntries(fmt.formatToParts(d).map((x) => [x.type, x.value]));
  return { date: `${p.year}-${p.month}-${p.day}`, time: `${p.hour}:${p.minute}` };
}

function firstPrompt(text) {
  const m = text.match(/_\*\*User[^\n]*\*\*_\s*\n+([\s\S]*?)(?:\n---|\n_\*\*Agent)/);
  if (!m) return "";
  return m[1].replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().slice(0, 140);
}

const norm = (s) => s.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");

// Every existing log of this user, in any sprint folder.
const logs = [];
for (const sprint of existsSync("ai-logs") ? readdirSync("ai-logs") : []) {
  const dir = join("ai-logs", sprint, user);
  if (!existsSync(dir) || !statSync(dir).isDirectory()) continue;
  for (const f of readdirSync(dir)) {
    if (f.endsWith(".md")) logs.push({ path: `${dir}/${f}`.replace(/\\/g, "/"), text: readFileSync(join(dir, f), "utf8") });
  }
}

const sessions = readdirSync(HISTORY).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".md")).sort().map((f) => {
  const path = `${HISTORY}/${f}`;
  const text = readFileSync(path, "utf8");
  const st = statSync(path);
  return { file: f, path, text, size: st.size, mtime: st.mtime, local: localDate(f), utcDate: f.slice(0, 10) };
});

function status(s) {
  for (const log of logs) {
    if (log.text === s.text) return { kind: "copied", log: log.path };
    if (norm(log.text) === norm(s.text)) return { kind: "copied (line endings differ)", log: log.path };
  }
  for (const log of logs) {
    const a = norm(log.text), b = norm(s.text);
    if (a.length > 200 && b.length > a.length && b.startsWith(a)) return { kind: "STALE COPY", log: log.path };
  }
  return { kind: "not copied", log: "" };
}

const now = Date.now();
const out = [];
out.push(`# log-sync scan (read-only)`, "");
out.push(`Sprint window ${sprintFrom} to ${sprintTo} (${timeZone}); destination \`${destDir}/\`.`, "");
out.push("| # | SpecStory file | Local start | UTC date | In sprint | Size | Status | Existing log | First prompt |");
out.push("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|");

const flags = [];
sessions.forEach((s, i) => {
  const st = status(s);
  const inSprint = s.local && s.local.date >= sprintFrom && s.local.date <= sprintTo;
  s.status = st;
  out.push(`| ${i + 1} | \`${s.file}\` | ${s.local ? `${s.local.date} ${s.local.time}` : "?"} | ${s.utcDate} | ${inSprint ? "yes" : "no"} | ${Math.round(s.size / 1024)} KB | ${st.kind} | ${st.log ? `\`${basename(st.log)}\`` : ""} | ${firstPrompt(s.text).replace(/\|/g, "\\|")} |`);
  if (st.kind === "STALE COPY") flags.push(`- **Stale copy:** \`${st.log}\` is an earlier, shorter version of \`${s.file}\` (the session continued after it was copied).`);
  if (s.local && s.local.date !== s.utcDate) flags.push(`- **Date differs:** \`${s.file}\` started ${s.local.date} local but ${s.utcDate} UTC; course names use the local date.`);
  if (now - s.mtime.getTime() < 30 * 60 * 1000) flags.push(`- **Possibly still running:** \`${s.file}\` changed in the last 30 minutes. Copy it after the session ends (run \`specstory sync\` first).`);
});

// Same UTC timestamp: either a manual copy (identical) or two sessions.
const byStamp = {};
for (const s of sessions) (byStamp[s.file.slice(0, 20)] ??= []).push(s);
for (const group of Object.values(byStamp)) {
  if (group.length < 2) continue;
  const names = group.map((s) => `\`${s.file}\``).join(", ");
  const identical = group.every((s) => s.text === group[0].text);
  flags.push(identical
    ? `- **Duplicate files:** ${names} are byte-identical (a manual copy). Copy only one.`
    : `- **Same timestamp, different content:** ${names}. Check whether one is a renamed or continued session before copying both.`);
}

// claude-web exports that mention attached files but have no attachments folder.
const extra = process.argv[2];
const webLogs = logs.filter((l) => basename(l.path).includes("_claude-web_"));
if (extra && existsSync(extra)) {
  for (const f of readdirSync(extra).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".md"))) webLogs.push({ path: join(extra, f), text: readFileSync(join(extra, f), "utf8") });
}
for (const l of webLogs) {
  const files = [...l.text.matchAll(/^> File: *(.+)$/gm)].map((m) => m[1].trim());
  if (files.length && !existsSync(l.path.replace(/\.md$/, ""))) {
    flags.push(`- **Missing attachments folder:** \`${l.path}\` mentions ${files.length} attached file(s) (${files.slice(0, 3).join(", ")}${files.length > 3 ? ", …" : ""}) but \`${basename(l.path, ".md")}/\` does not exist.`);
  }
}

out.push("", "## Flags", "", flags.length ? flags.join("\n") : "None.");
console.log(out.join("\n"));

```

`/log-sync` is built. You can try it now; if it isn't in the `/` menu yet, restarting Claude Code should pick it up.

It has two parts:
- **The script**, `.claude/course/scripts/log-scan.mjs`, only reads files and prints a report.
- **The skill file**, `agents/skills/log-sync/SKILL.md`, uses that report to walk you through copying logs.

The skill doesn't show up in `git status`; your exclude file matches it.

## How the script works, block by block

1. **Reading the sprint settings (`configValue`).** It reads the sprint dates, time zone, your GitHub username and the log folder from `current-sprint.md`. Nothing about Sprint 2 is hard-coded. If a setting is missing, the script stops with an error naming it.

2. **Converting to your local date (`localDate`).** SpecStory names files by UTC start time, like `2026-10-08_01-35-56Z`. This block turns that into a real date and formats it in `America/New_York`. That's how it knows the session started Oct 7 at 9:35 PM your time.

3. **Getting the first prompt (`firstPrompt`).** It finds the first `_**User …**_` block and keeps about 140 characters. That gives the skill something to base the slug on without reading the whole log.

4. **Comparing text (`norm`).** It turns Windows line endings (`\r\n`) into `\n` before comparing. Git on Windows changes line endings when you commit and check out, so a log you committed earlier doesn't match its source byte for byte.

5. **Collecting existing logs.** It reads every `.md` file in `ai-logs/sprint*/dchan01-wm/`, across all sprints. A session copied into an earlier sprint's folder still counts as copied.

6. **Collecting sessions.** For each SpecStory file it records the text, size, last-modified time, local start date and UTC date.

7. **Deciding each file's status (`status`).** It checks in this order:
   - **older snapshot:** the session is the start of a longer session file, so only the longer one needs copying;
   - **copied:** an existing log matches exactly, or matches except for line endings;
   - **STALE COPY:** an existing log is a shorter start of this session, meaning it was copied before the session ended;
   - otherwise **not copied**.

8. **Building the table and flags.** It prints one table row per session and adds a flag when:
   - an existing log is a stale copy;
   - the local and UTC dates differ;
   - the file changed in the last 30 minutes, so the session may still be running.

9. **Same-timestamp check.** It groups files by their timestamp. Identical files are flagged as a manual copy. Different files with the same timestamp are flagged, unless one is already marked as an older snapshot.

10. **Attachment check.** It looks at your `claude-web` logs, plus a folder of web exports if you pass one. Any log with a `> File:` line but no matching attachments folder is flagged.

## How the skill works

- **Before I see anything:** the skill automatically loads the rules, the sprint settings and a fresh scan.
- **Step 1, report:** I tell you what to copy and what needs a decision. Nothing is touched.
- **Step 2, names:** I propose `<local date>_claude-code_<slug>.md` names and **stop until you approve**.
- **Step 3, copy:** I copy each file exactly with `cp`, then confirm the copy matches with `cmp`.
- **Step 4, hand-off:** I give you the `git add`/`commit`/`push` commands to run yourself, and remind you to run `/log-comment`.

Only the scan, `ls` and `cmp` run without asking; `cp` always asks.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-28 23:39:29Z)**_

## Where `/log-sync` reads Claude web exports from

Before your message, the skill only checked web logs already in `ai-logs/` for missing attachment folders. It never picked up new exports, so I added that.

- **Where it looks:** files named `Claude-*.md` in the **repo root**, where you saved this one. If you keep exports somewhere else, such as Downloads, run `/log-sync "C:/Users/dylan/Downloads"` and it checks that folder too.
- **What it reads:** the exporter's header instead of a SpecStory file name:
  - `# title`
  - `**Created:**`, already in your local time, so it becomes the log date (`10/26/2026 11:07:28` → `2026-10-26`)
  - `**Updated:**`
  - `**Link:** …/chat/<id>`
  - the first `## User:` prompt, used to suggest a slug
  - any `> File:` lines, which are attachments
- **How it tells if an export is already copied:** comparing contents wouldn't work, because the `Exported:` time changes every time you download. Instead it matches the **chat ID in the link** against your existing `_claude-web_` logs. If the new export has a later `Updated` time, the old copy is marked stale.
- **How it copies:** byte for byte with `cp`, then checked with `cmp`, the same as SpecStory logs. The header and contents are never touched, which fits the course rules for web logs.

**Test on your file.** The scan reads it correctly:

| | |
|---|---|
| Title | Sprint 2 task index and documentation |
| Created | 2026-10-26 11:07, inside the sprint |
| Status | not copied |
| Attachments | `AI Log.pdf`, `Sprint1.pdf`, `Sprint2.pdf` |

It would be copied as `ai-logs/sprint2/dchan01-wm/2026-10-26_claude-web_<slug>.md`, for example with the slug `sprint2-task-index`. The three PDFs go in a folder of the same name minus `.md`. The export doesn't contain the PDFs themselves, so the skill will ask you where they are.

**Earlier sprints left alone.** The scan now shows only current-sprint flags, plus a one-line count of the 10 hidden earlier-sprint flags. Adding `--all` lists those.

**One thing to watch:** while `Claude-*.md` files sit in the repo root, they show up as untracked in `git status`, so they're easy to commit by accident. The skill will remind you, but you could also add `/Claude-*.md` to `.git/info/exclude`. Should I add that line?

You can test `/log-sync` now. It will report this export plus the still-running session, propose names, and stop for your approval before copying anything.

Choice: how should we display lines for different intervals within the grid (e.g. the default is every 15 minutes, pulled from the text fields)?

Decision: the interval is settable by a ENV variable (not the decision, this is existing behavior), so we need to account for different intervals. I decided to set 15 minutes as the default, and only allow intervals that evenly divide into one hour (e.g. 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 minutes).

Two alternatives:
Option 1: only accept 15 minute intervals
Option 2: accept any interval that evenly divides 1440 = 24 hours * 60 minutes

Rationale: Option 1 could introduce a lack of parity between the text field and the grid. If the interval is set to, for instance, 20, the text fields would give drop down options in intervals of 20 minutes (and only accept values in intervals of 20 mins). If the interval was a constant 15 minutes for the grid, we would desync from the text fields. We want to maintain parity between the two: they should display the exact same information just in two different formats. Option 2 could introduce boundaries that do not align with the hours (e.g. an interval of 40 minutes would skip over 1AM). That would make the UI visually confusing since there would be an hour line at 1AM, but it would not actually be a boundary of a block of time you can select.

The current idea maintains parity with the text fields, and makes sure hours are actually boundaries.

Consequences: parity will be maintained between the text fields and the grid (since the same interval is used for both methods). But now we also have to incorporate the logic for rendering different amounts of lines (intervals) per hour, as opposed to using a fixed 15 minute interval.

```mjs
// Read-only helper for /log-comment. Never writes, moves or edits any file.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/log-find.mjs <issue#> [pr# ...] [--ref <branch>]
//
// Lists the current sprint's logs that mention the issue or its PRs, and whether each
// log (and its attachments folder) exists on GitHub at <branch> (default: main).
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, existsSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const CONFIG = ".claude/course/current-sprint.md";
const config = readFileSync(CONFIG, "utf8");
const configValue = (key) => {
  const row = config.split("\n").find((l) => l.startsWith(`| ${key} |`));
  if (!row) throw new Error(`"${key}" row missing from ${CONFIG}`);
  return row.split("|")[2].trim().replace(/`/g, "");
};
const logDir = configValue("AI log folder").replace(/\/$/, "");
const repo = configValue("GitHub repo").split(" ")[0];

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const refAt = args.indexOf("--ref");
const ref = refAt >= 0 ? args[refAt + 1] : "main";
const numbers = args.filter((a, i) => /^\d+$/.test(a) && i !== refAt + 1);
if (!numbers.length) {
  console.error("Usage: log-find.mjs <issue#> [pr# ...] [--ref <branch>]");
  process.exit(1);
}
const [issue, ...prs] = numbers;

// "#104", "issue 104", "issue-104", "PR 110", "pr-110", "pull/110" all count as a mention.
const pattern = (n) => new RegExp(`(#|\\bissues?[ -]?|\\bprs?[ -]?|pull/)${n}\\b`, "gi");
const terms = [{ label: `issue #${issue}`, re: pattern(issue) }, ...prs.map((p) => ({ label: `PR #${p}`, re: pattern(p) }))];

// Is the path present in the remote branch? Reads only the local copy of origin (run `git fetch` first).
function onRemote(path) {
  try {
    execFileSync("git", ["cat-file", "-e", `origin/${ref}:${path}`], { stdio: "ignore" });
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

if (!existsSync(logDir)) {
  console.log(`Log folder \`${logDir}/\` does not exist yet.`);
  process.exit(0);
}

const rows = [];
for (const f of readdirSync(logDir).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".md")).sort()) {
  const path = `${logDir}/${f}`;
  const text = readFileSync(join(logDir, f), "utf8");
  const hits = terms.map((t) => ({ label: t.label, count: (text.match(t.re) || []).length })).filter((h) => h.count);
  const attachDir = path.replace(/\.md$/, "");
  const hasAttach = existsSync(attachDir) && statSync(attachDir).isDirectory();
  rows.push({ f, path, hits, hasAttach, attachDir, tool: (f.match(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}_([^_]+)_/) || [])[1] ?? "?" });
}

const url = (p) => `https://github.com/${repo}/blob/${ref}/${p.split("/").map(encodeURIComponent).join("/")}`;
const out = [`# log-find for issue #${issue}${prs.length ? ` (PRs ${prs.map((p) => `#${p}`).join(", ")})` : ""}`, ""];
out.push(`Folder \`${logDir}/\`; links point at branch \`${ref}\` (checked against \`origin/${ref}\`; run \`git fetch\` first for fresh results).`, "");
out.push("| Log | Tool | Mentions | On GitHub | Attachments | Full URL |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|");
const sorted = [...rows].sort((a, b) => b.hits.length - a.hits.length);
for (const r of sorted) {
  const mentions = r.hits.length ? r.hits.map((h) => `${h.label} ×${h.count}`).join(", ") : "none";
  const attach = r.hasAttach ? (onRemote(r.attachDir) ? "folder (on GitHub)" : "folder (NOT on GitHub)") : "";
  out.push(`| \`${r.f}\` | ${r.tool} | ${mentions} | ${onRemote(r.path) ? "yes" : "**no**"} | ${attach} | ${url(r.path)} |`);
}
if (!rows.length) out.push("| (no logs yet) | | | | | |");
out.push("", "A log with no mentions can still belong to this issue (e.g. it refers to the issue by its title); ask the user.");
console.log(out.join("\n"));

```

argument-hint: "<issue#> [pr# ...]"
disable-model-invocation: true

## Rules
!`cat .claude/course/skill-rules.md`

!`cat .claude/course/current-sprint.md`

## Your task

Arguments given to this skill: "$ARGUMENTS". The first number is the issue; any others are PRs. If there is no issue number, ask for one and stop.

Draft the user's **AI Assistance comment** (deliverable D5) for that issue. Take the template, word for word, from the "AI Assistance comment" section of the sprint reference file named in the config. **You never post it.** You write a draft file and the user pastes it into GitHub.

Why this matters (course, "must improve" list): every issue or PR that involved AI needs a comment linking **directly to each log file**. A folder link, a link to another issue's log, or a broken link gets no credit. The comment may go on the issue **or** the PR. Each contributor posts their own.

### Step 1 — Gather (read-only)
1. `gh issue view <N> --json number,title,state,url,milestone,assignees,closedByPullRequestsReferences,comments`
2. Linked PRs: those in `closedByPullRequestsReferences`, plus any PR numbers given as arguments, plus `gh pr list --state all --search "<N> in:body" --json number,title,author,headRefName,state,url`.
3. For the issue and each linked PR, check whether the user (GitHub user in the config) **already has an AI Assistance comment** (a comment starting with `### AI Assistance`). For PRs use `gh pr view <PR> --json comments,author`.
4. `git fetch origin` (updates the local copy of the remote; changes nothing on GitHub), then `node .claude/course/scripts/log-find.mjs <N> <PR numbers…>`. It lists the sprint's logs, how often each mentions the issue or its PRs, whether each log is on `main` on GitHub, and the full URL.

### Step 2 — Ask (stop and wait)
Show briefly: the issue title, the linked PRs, any existing AI Assistance comment of the user's (and where), and the log-find table. Then ask, in one message:
1. **Which logs belong in the comment?** Pre-select the logs that mention the issue or its PRs; the user adds or removes. If none apply, offer the **"No AI used."** version.
2. **Role(s) in this issue:** Implementation / Code review / Testing / Other (several are allowed, e.g. "Implementation / Testing").
3. **Where will you post it:** the issue or a PR? If the user already has a comment, recommend **editing that one** to add rows (the course wants one comment per contributor per issue).

### Step 3 — Draft
For each chosen log, draft the "What AI helped with" cell: a short phrase (under ~15 words) based on **the user's own prompts** in that log (`grep` the `_**User` / `## User:` turns; don't paraphrase the AI's answers). Mark the cells as drafts for the user to edit.

`/log-comment` is built, and git ignores it like the other course skills. It has two parts, like `/log-sync`: a read-only helper script and the skill file.

## The helper: `.claude/course/scripts/log-find.mjs`

1. **Settings.** It reads your log folder and the repo name from `current-sprint.md`, so nothing about Sprint 2 is hard-coded.
2. **Arguments.** `<issue#> [pr# …]`, plus two options:
   - `--ref <branch>` sets which branch the links point to (default `main`);
   - `--dir <folder>` checks another sprint's log folder instead of the current one.

   My first version dropped the issue number when there was no `--ref`, and the first test caught it. It's fixed.
3. **Finding mentions.** It counts mentions such as `#104`, `issue 104`, `issue-104`, `PR 110`, `pr-110` and `pull/110`.
4. **Is the log on GitHub?** It runs `git cat-file -e origin/main:<path>`, which checks your local copy of `main` from the last `git fetch`. It doesn't contact GitHub and changes nothing.
5. **Output.** A table with each log's tool, mention counts, whether it's on `main`, whether an attachments folder exists and is pushed, and the full `blob/main/…` URL. Logs that mention the issue come first.

**Test:** run on Sprint 1 issue #69, it put `2026-10-08_claude-code_implement-pr-69-and-70.md` at the top with 28 mentions. That's the log your actual comment on #69 links to.

## The skill: four steps

1. **Gather (read-only):**
   - the issue and the PRs linked to it;
   - whether you already have an `### AI Assistance` comment on the issue or any of those PRs;
   - then `git fetch` and the helper's table.
2. **Ask, then stop:**
   - which logs to include (the ones that mention the issue are pre-selected);
   - your role(s);
   - whether to post on the issue or a PR. If you already have a comment, it recommends editing it to add rows.
3. **Draft:**
   - It fills in the template exactly as worded in the sprint reference, with full URLs.
   - The "What AI helped with" text is based on **your prompts** in each log, marked as a draft for you to edit.
   - It adds an Attachments line only for logs that have attachments.
   - The draft goes to `.claude/work/issue-<N>/ai-comment.md`.
4. **Link check and hand-off:**
   - If a log isn't on `main` yet, it warns you to post after your logs PR merges. It won't link to a feature branch, because those links break once the branch is deleted.
   - It shows the markdown ready to paste.
   - It also gives an optional `gh issue comment … --body-file` command, which only you run.

// `git cat-file`; never writes to git, GitHub, or any file.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/preflight.mjs <issue#> [pr# ...]
// Run `git fetch origin` first so the log-link checks see what is on GitHub.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const CONFIG = ".claude/course/current-sprint.md";
const config = readFileSync(CONFIG, "utf8");
const configValue = (key) => {
  const row = config.split("\n").find((l) => l.startsWith(`| ${key} |`));
  if (!row) throw new Error(`"${key}" row missing from ${CONFIG}`);
  return row.split("|")[2].trim().replace(/`/g, "");
};
const repo = configValue("GitHub repo").split(" ")[0];
const me = configValue("GitHub user");
const milestone = configValue("Milestone");
const sprintEnd = configValue("Dates").split(" to ")[1];

const [issueNo, ...extraPrs] = process.argv.slice(2).filter((a) => /^\d+$/.test(a));
if (!issueNo) {
  console.error("Usage: preflight.mjs <issue#> [pr# ...]");
  process.exit(1);
}

// `gh pr checks` exits non-zero when a check fails, but its JSON is still on stdout.
function gh(args) {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(execFileSync("gh", [...args, "--repo", repo], { encoding: "utf8", stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] }));
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.stdout) return JSON.parse(e.stdout);
    throw e;
  }
}
const onRemote = (ref, path) => {
  try {
    execFileSync("git", ["cat-file", "-e", `origin/${ref}:${path}`], { stdio: "ignore" });
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
};

const rows = [];
const add = (area, check, result, evidence = "", fix = "") => rows.push({ area, check, result, evidence, fix });
const esc = (s) => String(s).replace(/\|/g, "\\|").replace(/\n/g, " ");

// Text of a markdown section: from a heading/label matching `title` to the next heading.
function section(text, title) {
  const lines = text.split(/\r?\n/);
  const start = lines.findIndex((l) => new RegExp(`^\\s*(#{1,6}\\s*|\\*\\*)?${title}`, "i").test(l));
  if (start < 0) return null;
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((l) => /^\s*#{1,6}\s/.test(l));
  return (end < 0 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end)).join("\n");
}
const listItems = (text) => text.split(/\r?\n/).filter((l) => /^\s*(\d+[.)]|[-*+]\s|- \[[ x]\])/i.test(l) && l.replace(/^\s*(\d+[.)]|[-*+]|- \[[ x]\])\s*/, "").trim().length > 3);

// ---------- Issue ----------
const issue = gh(["issue", "view", issueNo, "--json", "number,title,body,state,url,milestone,assignees,author,comments,closedByPullRequestsReferences"]);
const body = issue.body || "";
const issueComments = issue.comments || [];
const owners = issue.assignees.map((a) => a.login);

add("Issue", "Milestone", issue.milestone?.title === milestone ? "PASS" : "FAIL", issue.milestone?.title ?? "none", `Attach the issue to \`${milestone}\`.`);
add("Issue", "Exactly one owner", owners.length === 1 ? "PASS" : "FAIL", owners.join(", ") || "none", "Assign exactly one owner.");

const isBug = /observed behavio/i.test(body);
const required = isBug
  ? ["Observed Behavior", "Expected Behavior", "Steps to Reproduce", "Additional Information"]
  : ["User Story", "User Scenario", "Acceptance Criteria", "Out of Scope", "Open Questions"];
const missing = required.filter((h) => section(body, h) === null);
add("Spec (D2)", `${isBug ? "Bug" : "Feature"} template sections`, missing.length ? "FAIL" : "PASS", missing.length ? `missing: ${missing.join(", ")}` : "all present", "Add the missing course template sections to the issue body (`/plan-spec`).");
if (!isBug) {
  const ac = listItems(section(body, "Acceptance Criteria") ?? "");
  add("Spec (D2)", "≥3 acceptance criteria", ac.length >= 3 ? "PASS" : "FAIL", `${ac.length} found`, "Each criterion needs a clear pass/fail outcome; minimum 3.");
  const story = section(body, "User Story") ?? "";
  add("Spec (D2)", "User story form (As a / I want / so that)", /as an? .+i want .+so that/is.test(story) ? "PASS" : "CHECK", "", "Use \"As a [user], I want [goal] so that [benefit].\"");
}
const originalHeads = isBug
  ? ["Issue Summary", "Steps to Reproduce", "Actual Results", "Expected Results", "Technical details", "Evidence"]
  : ["Is your proposal related to a problem", "Describe the solution you'd like", "Describe alternatives you've considered", "Additional context", "Requirement/Document"];
const origMissing = originalHeads.filter((h) => section(body, h.replace(/[?'/]/g, ".")) === null);
add("Spec (D2)", "Original GitHub issue template (your preference, not graded)", origMissing.length ? "INFO" : "PASS", origMissing.length ? `missing: ${origMissing.join(", ")}` : "all present");

// A teammate (not the owner) must confirm the spec is clear enough to implement.
const reviewers = issueComments.filter((c) => !owners.includes(c.author.login) && c.author.login !== me && /spec|clear|implement|acceptance|criteria|lgtm|looks good|approve/i.test(c.body));
add("Spec (D2)", "Teammate spec-review comment", reviewers.length ? "CHECK" : "FAIL",
  reviewers.length ? reviewers.map((c) => `@${c.author.login}: "${c.body.slice(0, 80)}"`).join("; ") : "no comment from a teammate about the spec",
  reviewers.length ? "Confirm the comment really reviews the spec." : "Ask a teammate to comment that the spec is clear enough to implement.");

// ---------- Linked PRs ----------
const prNumbers = new Set([...issue.closedByPullRequestsReferences.map((p) => p.number), ...extraPrs.map(Number)]);
const linkRe = new RegExp(`(closes|closed|fixes|fixed|resolves|resolved)\\s+#${issueNo}\\b`, "i");
for (const p of gh(["pr", "list", "--state", "all", "--search", `${issueNo} in:body`, "--json", "number,body", "--limit", "30"])) {
  if (linkRe.test(p.body || "")) prNumbers.add(p.number);
}
const prs = [...prNumbers].sort((a, b) => a - b).map((n) => gh(["pr", "view", String(n), "--json",
  "number,title,body,url,state,isDraft,author,baseRefName,headRefName,additions,deletions,changedFiles,files,comments,reviews,mergedBy,mergedAt"]));
if (!prs.length) add("PR (D4)", "Linked PR", "FAIL", "no PR links this issue", `Open a PR with \`Closes #${issueNo}\` (\`/pr-draft\`).`);

// ---------- Design (D3): issue body, issue comments, or PR description ----------
const designSources = [{ where: "issue body", text: body }, ...issueComments.map((c) => ({ where: `issue comment by @${c.author.login}`, text: c.body })), ...prs.map((p) => ({ where: `PR #${p.number}`, text: p.body || "" }))];
let design = null;
for (const s of designSources) {
  const at = s.text.search(/alternative/i);
  if (at < 0) continue;
  const after = s.text.slice(at).split(/\n\s*(\*\*)?(rationale|consequences?)\b/i)[0];
  const options = Math.max(listItems(after).length, (after.match(/\boption\s*([0-9]|[A-Z]\b)/gi) || []).length);
  const complete = /rationale/i.test(s.text) && /consequence/i.test(s.text) && /decision/i.test(s.text);
  if (!design || options > design.options) design = { where: s.where, options, complete };
}
add("Design (D3)", "Decision with ≥2 concrete alternatives",
  design ? (design.options >= 2 && design.complete ? "PASS" : "CHECK") : "FAIL",
  design ? `${design.where}: ${design.options} alternative(s) found${design.complete ? "" : "; Decision/Rationale/Consequences not all labelled"}` : "no design decision found",
  "Add Decision / Alternatives (2+) / Rationale / Consequences (`/plan-design`).");

// ---------- AI Assistance comment (D5): on the issue or any linked PR ----------
const aiComments = [
  ...issueComments.filter((c) => c.author.login === me && /^\s*#{1,6}\s*AI Assistance/im.test(c.body)).map((c) => ({ where: `issue #${issueNo}`, body: c.body })),
  ...prs.flatMap((p) => p.comments.filter((c) => c.author.login === me && /^\s*#{1,6}\s*AI Assistance/im.test(c.body)).map((c) => ({ where: `PR #${p.number}`, body: c.body }))),
];
add("AI logs (D5)", "Your AI Assistance comment", aiComments.length ? "PASS" : "FAIL", aiComments.map((c) => c.where).join(", ") || "none on the issue or its PRs", `Run \`/log-comment ${issueNo}\` and post it.`);
for (const c of aiComments) {
  if (/no ai used/i.test(c.body)) continue;
  for (const m of c.body.matchAll(/\]\(([^)]+)\)/g)) {
    const link = m[1];
    const blob = link.match(new RegExp(`^https://github\\.com/${repo}/(blob|tree)/([^/]+)/(.+)$`));
    const isAttachLine = c.body.split("\n").find((l) => l.includes(link))?.includes("Attachments");
    if (!blob) {
      add("AI logs (D5)", "Log link is a full URL", "FAIL", `${c.where}: ${link}`, "Use https://github.com/<repo>/blob/main/<path>; relative links break in comments.");
      continue;
    }
    const path = decodeURIComponent(blob[3]);
    if (!path.endsWith(".md") && !isAttachLine) add("AI logs (D5)", "Links go to a log file, not a folder", "FAIL", `${c.where}: ${path}`, "Link each log file directly.");
    const ok = onRemote(blob[2], path);
    add("AI logs (D5)", `Link resolves: ${path.split("/").pop()}`, ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", `${c.where}, branch \`${blob[2]}\``, ok ? "" : "File not on that branch on GitHub (not pushed/merged, renamed, or the branch was deleted). Point it at main once merged.");
  }
}

// ---------- Each PR (D4) ----------
const isCode = (f) => !/\.(md|mdx|txt|pdf|png|jpe?g|svg|lock)$|(^|\/)(ai-logs|docs)\/|yarn\.lock|\.generated\./.test(f);
for (const p of prs) {
  const a = `PR #${p.number}`;
  const pb = p.body || "";
  add(a, "Author", p.author.login === me ? "INFO" : "INFO", `@${p.author.login}, ${p.state.toLowerCase()}${p.isDraft ? " (draft)" : ""}, ${p.headRefName} → ${p.baseRefName}`);
  add(a, `\`Closes #${issueNo}\``, linkRe.test(pb) ? "PASS" : "FAIL", "", `Add \`Closes #${issueNo}\` to the description.`);
  const parts = [["What changed", /what (changed|does this pr do)/i], ["Why", /^\s*(#{1,6}\s*|\*\*)why/im], ["How it was tested", /how (it was|should this be) tested/i], ["Test strategy", /test strategy/i], ["CI / manual verification", /ci\b|manual verification/i]];
  const absent = parts.filter(([, re]) => !re.test(pb)).map(([n]) => n);
  add(a, "What / why / how tested / test strategy / CI-or-manual", absent.length ? "FAIL" : "PASS", absent.length ? `missing: ${absent.join(", ")}` : "all present", "Fill these in (`/pr-draft`).");
  const td = section(pb, "Tech Debt");
  const tdOk = td !== null && /\*\*Introduced:?\*\*/i.test(td) && /\*\*Encountered:?\*\*/i.test(td);
  add(a, "Tech Debt section (Introduced / Encountered)", tdOk ? "PASS" : "FAIL", td === null ? "no `## Tech Debt` section" : tdOk ? "" : "Introduced or Encountered missing", "Add the verbatim Tech Debt section; \"None.\" is valid.");
  const origParts = ["What does this PR do", "Mandatory Tasks", "How should this be tested"].filter((h) => !new RegExp(h, "i").test(pb));
  add(a, "Original PR template (your preference, not graded)", origParts.length ? "INFO" : "PASS", origParts.length ? `missing: ${origParts.join(", ")}` : "all present");
  add(a, "Conventional-commit title", /^(feat|fix|refactor|chore|docs|test|perf|build|ci|style|revert)(\([^)]+\))?!?: /.test(p.title) ? "PASS" : "FAIL", p.title, "e.g. `feat(scope): …` (AGENTS.md; CI validates PR titles).");

  const codeFiles = p.files.filter((f) => isCode(f.path));
  const codeLines = codeFiles.reduce((n, f) => n + f.additions + f.deletions, 0);
  add(a, "Size ≤500 code lines and ≤10 code files", codeLines <= 500 && codeFiles.length <= 10 ? "PASS" : "CHECK", `${codeLines} lines in ${codeFiles.length} code files (excludes docs, logs, lock files)`, "AGENTS.md (team rule): split large PRs.");
  const tests = p.files.filter((f) => /\.(test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/.test(f.path));
  if (codeFiles.length) add(a, "Tests added or updated", tests.length ? "PASS" : "CHECK", tests.map((f) => f.path.split("/").pop()).join(", ") || "no test files changed", "Every behavioral change needs new or updated tests (course).");

  const checks = gh(["pr", "checks", String(p.number), "--json", "name,bucket"]);
  const failed = checks.filter((c) => c.bucket === "fail");
  const notes = failed.map((c) => c.name === "required" ? "required (fails by design when E2E is skipped, agents/rules/ci-check-failures.md)" : c.name);
  add(a, "CI", failed.length ? "CHECK" : "PASS", `${checks.filter((c) => c.bucket === "pass").length} passed, ${failed.length} failed${failed.length ? `: ${notes.join("; ")}` : ""}, ${checks.filter((c) => c.bucket === "skipping").length} skipped`, failed.length ? "Course: CI passes, or manual verification is documented in the PR." : "");

  const rubric = [...p.comments, ...p.reviews].filter((c) => c.author.login !== p.author.login && /code review/i.test(c.body || "") && /correctness/i.test(c.body || ""));
  add(a, "Review rubric from a non-author", rubric.length ? "PASS" : "FAIL", rubric.map((c) => `@${c.author.login}`).join(", ") || "none yet", "Ask a teammate to post the rubric on their first review pass.");
  const selfApproved = p.reviews.some((r) => r.author.login === p.author.login && r.state === "APPROVED");
  const selfMerged = p.mergedBy && p.mergedBy.login === p.author.login;
  add(a, "No self-approval or self-merge", selfApproved || selfMerged ? "FAIL" : "PASS", selfMerged ? `merged by the author @${p.mergedBy.login}` : selfApproved ? "approved by its author" : p.mergedBy ? `merged by @${p.mergedBy.login}` : "not merged yet", "A teammate must approve and merge.");
  if (p.state === "MERGED") add(a, "Merged by sprint end", p.mergedAt.slice(0, 10) <= sprintEnd ? "PASS" : "FAIL", p.mergedAt.slice(0, 10));
  else add(a, "Merged by sprint end", "CHECK", `${p.state.toLowerCase()}; due ${sprintEnd}`, "Merge (by a teammate) before the deadline, then delete the branch.");
}

// ---------- Output ----------
const order = { FAIL: 0, CHECK: 1, INFO: 2, PASS: 3 };
const counts = Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(order).map((k) => [k, rows.filter((r) => r.result === k).length]));
const out = [`# Preflight: issue #${issue.number} — ${issue.title}`, "", `${issue.url} · ${issue.state.toLowerCase()} · PRs: ${prs.map((p) => `#${p.number}`).join(", ") || "none"}`, "",
  `**${counts.FAIL} FAIL · ${counts.CHECK} CHECK (needs a human look) · ${counts.PASS} PASS · ${counts.INFO} INFO**`, "",
  "| Area | Check | Result | Evidence | Fix |", "|---|---|---|---|---|",
  ...rows.map((r) => `| ${r.area} | ${esc(r.check)} | ${r.result === "PASS" ? "PASS" : `**${r.result}**`} | ${esc(r.evidence)} | ${r.result === "PASS" ? "" : esc(r.fix)} |`)];
console.log(out.join("\n"));

## User Story
As an event host, I want to configure weekly recurring events to repeat on specific days (e.g., Tuesday and Thursday).

## User Scenario
An event host configures a weekly recurring event, selecting specific days (e.g., Tuesday and Thursday) from a new toggle row. When a booker schedules the event, they only see availability for those selected days. 

## Acceptance Criteria
1. When setting an event to repeat weekly, a new row of buttons (Sunday through Saturday) appears, allowing the host to select specific days.
2. The system requires at least one day to be selected and prevents users from unchecking every day.
3. The selected days are successfully saved to the event's settings so they apply to all future bookings.
4. Automated tests must ensure the calendar correctly generates the schedule based on the chosen days.

## Out of Scope
- Implementing specific end dates ("Ends: Never / On [date]")—the system will continue using a maximum occurrence count.
- Day-of-week selection for monthly or yearly recurrence intervals.
- Updating the `GoogleCalendarService` sync logic to support the new day selection (to be handled in a follow-up issue).

## Open Question
- Does the "maximum of N events" limit refer to individual meetings or total weeks (e.g., does a max of 8 on a Tue/Thu schedule mean 4 weeks or 8 weeks)?

---
name: pr-preflight
description: Grading audit for one issue and its PRs against the current sprint's course requirements (spec, design, PR description, Tech Debt, CI, review rubric, self-merge, AI Assistance comment and links, milestone). Read-only; reports pass/fail with fixes.
argument-hint: "<issue#> [extra pr# ...]"
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Bash(git fetch*) Bash(node .claude/course/scripts/preflight.mjs *) Bash(gh issue view *) Bash(gh pr view *) Bash(gh pr list *) Bash(gh pr checks *) Bash(gh pr diff *)
---

## Rules
!`cat .claude/course/skill-rules.md`

## Current sprint
!`cat .claude/course/current-sprint.md`

## Your task

Arguments given to this skill: "$ARGUMENTS". The first number is the issue; any others are extra PRs that belong to it (e.g. stacked PRs that don't say `Closes #N`). If there is no issue number, ask for one and stop.

Audit the issue against what the course grades this sprint, so the user can fix problems **before** the deadline. This skill only reads. It never edits the issue, PR, or comments, and never posts.

### Step 1 — Run the audit
1. `git fetch origin`. This updates the local copy of the remote so the log-link checks are current; it changes nothing on GitHub.
2. `node .claude/course/scripts/preflight.mjs <issue#> [extra PRs]`

The script checks:
- the milestone and the single owner;
- the spec sections, acceptance criteria and user-story form, plus the original GitHub template (INFO only);
- a teammate's spec-review comment;
- a design decision with at least 2 alternatives;
- your AI Assistance comment, and that every link resolves on GitHub;
- for each linked PR:
  - `Closes #N`, the what/why/how-tested/test-strategy/CI-or-manual parts, and the Tech Debt section;
  - a conventional-commit title, the size limit and test files;
  - CI, the reviewer rubric, no self-approval or self-merge, and merged by the end of the sprint.

### Step 2 — Verify before reporting
The script matches text patterns, so it can be wrong in both directions. For **every FAIL and CHECK**, look at the actual text it refers to before you report it:
- Use `gh issue view <N> --json body,comments` and `gh pr view <PR> --json body,comments,reviews`.
- Mark each one **Confirmed** (you saw the problem) or **False alarm** (it's there under a different wording; say where).
- For CHECK rows, decide which it is:
  - **Spec-review comment:** does the teammate's comment actually review the spec?
  - **CI failures:** are they unrelated to the change?
  - **Size and missing tests:** is there a good reason?

  Say what you found.

If the issue clearly has related PRs the script didn't find, ask whether to rerun with them, for example stacked PRs whose descriptions say "part of #N" instead of `Closes #N`.

### Step 3 — Report
Write `.claude/work/issue-<N>/preflight.md` containing the script's table plus your verification notes. Then, in chat:
1. A one-line verdict: the number of confirmed problems.
2. **Confirmed problems, most points at risk first.** Use the deliverable weights in the sprint config (for example D2 Spec 20 pts and D4 PRs 20 pts before D3 Design 5 pts). For each, give:
   - the fix;
   - the skill that helps (`/plan-spec`, `/plan-design`, `/pr-draft`, `/log-comment`), or the manual step, such as asking a teammate to review or merge;
   - who must do it. Some fixes are a teammate's job, such as the spec review, the rubric, or the approval and merge.
3. Under a short "Not problems" heading: the false alarms and the INFO rows.

Never fix anything yourself in this skill. Edits to issues, PRs and comments are the user's to make on GitHub. Offer to draft the text with the matching skill.
