`/pr-preflight` is built, and git ignores it like the other course skills. It runs in our conversation instead of as a separate agent, as I mentioned before starting; I recorded that change in `skills-proposal.md`.

## How it works

**The script, `.claude/course/scripts/preflight.mjs`,** only reads: it calls `gh … view/list/checks` and `git cat-file`.

| Block | What it does |
|---|---|
| Settings and `gh` wrapper | Reads the repo, your username, the milestone and the sprint end date from `current-sprint.md`. `gh pr checks` reports failure when a check failed, so the wrapper still uses its output in that case. |
| `section()` / `listItems()` | Finds the text under a heading and counts list items, which is how the acceptance criteria and alternatives are counted. |
| Issue checks | Milestone, exactly one owner, the course spec sections, at least 3 acceptance criteria, the "As a / I want / so that" form, and the original GitHub template (INFO only, since that's your preference and isn't graded). It also looks for a teammate's comment that reads like a spec review. |
| Linked PRs | PRs linked to the issue on GitHub, plus PRs whose description says `Closes/Fixes/Resolves #N`, plus any PR numbers you add. |
| Design | Looks for "alternative" in the issue body, issue comments and PR descriptions, then counts the options and whether Decision, Rationale and Consequences all appear. |
| AI comment | Finds your `### AI Assistance` comment on the issue or a PR. For each link it flags relative links and folder links, and checks the file exists on that branch on GitHub. |
| Per-PR checks | `Closes #N`; the what/why/how-tested/test-strategy/CI-or-manual parts; Tech Debt with Introduced and Encountered; a conventional-commit title; size, counting code only; test files; CI, noting that `required` fails on purpose per `agents/rules`; a rubric from someone other than the author; no self-approval or self-merge; merged by the end of the sprint. |
| Output | A table with problems first. Results are **FAIL**, **CHECK** (needs a human look), PASS or INFO. |

**The skill** then has me look at the actual text behind every FAIL and CHECK before reporting it, and mark each as Confirmed or a false alarm. Problems are ranked by how many points each deliverable is worth, and each one names the skill that fixes it. I never edit anything myself.

## Git workflow and final submission checklist

One branch and one PR per issue; everything below must be pushed by Oct 29, 11:59 PM.

**Branch and PR workflow (verbatim)**

```bash
# Sync with main before starting
git checkout main
git pull origin main

# Create a branch for your issue
git checkout -b feat/issue-42-export-pdf   # new feature
git checkout -b fix/issue-17-date-overflow  # bug fix

# After making changes and running tests:
git add <changed files>
git commit -m "feat: add PDF export for reports (#42)"
git push origin feat/issue-42-export-pdf
```

Open the PR from GitHub's "Compare & pull request" banner with `main` as the base. After it is merged:

```bash
git checkout main           # switch back to main
git pull origin main        # pull the merged changes
git branch -d feat/issue-42-export-pdf  # delete local branch (safe: only works if merged)
```

Then click "Delete branch" on the merged PR page.

git tag v<version>-csci435-s2
git push origin v<version>-csci435-s2

````mjs
// Read-only planner for /dev-checks: works out which files changed on this branch, which
// workspace packages own them, and which unit tests relate to them, then prints the commands.
// Runs nothing but read-only git; never edits files.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/checks-plan.mjs [base-ref]   (default base: origin/main)
import { readFileSync, existsSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join, basename, extname } from "node:path";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const base = process.argv[2] ?? "origin/main";
const git = (...args) => execFileSync("git", args, { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();

// Everything that differs from where this branch left main: commits, staged, unstaged, untracked.
const mergeBase = git("merge-base", base, "HEAD");
const tracked = git("diff", "--name-only", mergeBase).split("\n").filter(Boolean);
const untracked = git("ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").split("\n").filter(Boolean);
const changed = [...new Set([...tracked, ...untracked])].filter((f) => existsSync(f));

// Course logs, notes and docs never need code checks.
const isCode = (f) => /\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$/.test(f) && !/^(ai-logs|docs|\.claude|\.specstory)\//.test(f);
const isTest = (f) => /\.(test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/.test(f) && !/\.e2e\./.test(f);
const isE2e = (f) => /\.e2e\.[jt]sx?$/.test(f) || /\/playwright\//.test(f);
const code = changed.filter(isCode);

// The workspace package that owns a file is the nearest package.json above it.
function owningPackage(file) {
  for (let dir = dirname(file); dir && dir !== "."; dir = dirname(dir)) {
    const pj = join(dir, "package.json");
    if (existsSync(pj)) return JSON.parse(readFileSync(pj, "utf8")).name;
  }
  return null;
}
const packages = [...new Set(code.map(owningPackage).filter(Boolean))].sort();

// Related unit tests: changed test files, plus tests named after a changed source file
// in the same folder or a sibling __tests__ folder.
const tests = new Set(code.filter(isTest));
for (const f of code.filter((f) => !isTest(f) && !isE2e(f))) {
  const stem = basename(f, extname(f));
  for (const dir of [dirname(f), join(dirname(f), "__tests__")]) {
    if (!existsSync(dir)) continue;
    for (const t of readdirSync(dir)) {
      if (isTest(t) && t.startsWith(`${stem}.`)) tests.add(join(dir, t).replace(/\\/g, "/"));
    }
  }
}
const e2e = code.filter(isE2e);
const sourcesWithoutTests = code.filter((f) => !isTest(f) && !isE2e(f) && ![...tests].some((t) => basename(t).startsWith(`${basename(f, extname(f))}.`)));

const q = (f) => `"${f}"`;
const out = [`# dev-checks plan`, "", `Branch \`${git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")}\`, compared with \`${base}\` (merge base \`${mergeBase.slice(0, 9)}\`).`, ""];
out.push(`**Changed files (${changed.length}):** ${changed.map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(", ") || "none"}`, "");
out.push(`**Code files to check (${code.length}):** ${code.map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(", ") || "none"}`, "");
out.push(`**Packages:** ${packages.map((p) => `\`${p}\``).join(", ") || "none"}`, "");
out.push(`**Related unit tests (${tests.size}):** ${[...tests].map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(", ") || "none found"}`, "");
if (sourcesWithoutTests.length) out.push(`**Changed source files with no test named after them:** ${sourcesWithoutTests.map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(", ")} — a test may still cover them elsewhere; check before saying they are untested.`, "");
out.push("## Commands", "");
if (code.length) {
  out.push("1. Lint/format, check only (reports, changes nothing):", "```bash", `yarn biome check ${code.map(q).join(" ")}`, "```");
  out.push("2. Type check each affected package (`yarn type-check:ci` is broken on this Windows machine):", "```bash", ...packages.map((p) => `yarn turbo run type-check --filter=${p} --force`), "```");
  if (tests.size) out.push("3. Related unit tests (`NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=\"\"` is required; `.env` sets it for E2E):", "```bash", `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E="" TZ=UTC yarn vitest run ${[...tests].map(q).join(" ")}`, "```");
  else out.push("3. No related unit tests found; run the package's tests or add tests.");
}
if (e2e.length) out.push("", `E2E files changed (${e2e.map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(", ")}): the user runs these against a production build (see setup notes).`);
console.log(out.join("\n"));

````

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Read-only: for each file, ask Biome whether it would change the file's LF version.
# Separates real format/import-order problems from CRLF artifacts of the Windows checkout
# (core.autocrlf=true). Never writes to the files.
# Usage: bash .claude/course/scripts/biome-lf.sh <file> [file ...]
status=0
for f in "$@"; do
  lf=$(tr -d '\r' < "$f")
  fixed=$(printf '%s\n' "$lf" | yarn -s biome check --diagnostic-level=error --stdin-file-path="$f" 2>/dev/null)
  # In stdin mode Biome prints the (possibly fixed) contents; compare them with the input.
  if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$lf")" = "$(printf '%s\n' "$fixed" | sed -n "1,$(printf '%s\n' "$lf" | wc -l)p")" ]; then
    echo "OK (CRLF only): $f"
  else
    echo "NEEDS FORMAT/IMPORT FIX: $f"
    status=1
  fi
done
exit $status

```

```bash
rm .claude/course/scripts/biome-lf.sh && cat > .claude/course/scripts/biome-lf.mjs <<'EOF'
// Read-only: for each file, asks Biome whether it would change the file's LF version.
// Separates real format/import-order problems from CRLF artifacts of the Windows checkout
// (core.autocrlf=true). Never writes to the files.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/biome-lf.mjs <file> [file ...]
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";

let status = 0;
for (const file of process.argv.slice(2)) {
  const lf = readFileSync(file, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
  // In stdin mode Biome prints the contents it would write; unchanged contents mean no real problem.
  const run = spawnSync("yarn", ["-s", "biome", "check", "--diagnostic-level=error", `--stdin-file-path=${file}`], { input: lf, encoding: "utf8", shell: true });
  const ok = run.stdout.startsWith(lf) || run.stdout === lf;
  console.log(`${ok ? "OK (CRLF only)" : "NEEDS FORMAT/IMPORT FIX"}: ${file}`);
  if (!ok) status = 1;
}
process.exit(status);
EOF
```

```bash
// Read-only: runs Biome on each changed file's branch version and its origin/main version,
// both with LF line endings, and reports whether each problem is new or already on main.
// Line endings are normalised because core.autocrlf=true gives the Windows checkout CRLF,

// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/biome-compare.mjs <file> [file ...]
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { spawnSync, execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

function biome(file, contents) {
  // With stdin, --write prints the fixed contents to stdout instead of writing the file.
  const run = spawnSync("yarn", ["biome", "check", "--write", "--diagnostic-level=error", `--stdin-file-path=${file}`], { input: contents, encoding: "utf8", shell: true });
  const needsFix = !run.stdout.startsWith(contents);
  const lintErrors = [...new Set((run.stderr + run.stdout).match(/lint\/[\w/]+/g) || [])];
  return { needsFix, lintErrors };
}
function mainVersion(file) {

  } catch {

  }
}

  const mainText = mainVersion(file);
  const main = mainText === null ? null : biome(file, mainText);
  const describe = (r) => (r.needsFix || r.lintErrors.length ? [r.needsFix ? "format/import order" : "", ...r.lintErrors].filter(Boolean).join(", ") : "clean");
  const newLint = branch.lintErrors.filter((e) => !main?.lintErrors.includes(e));
  const newFix = branch.needsFix && !main?.needsFix;
  const verdict = !branch.needsFix && !branch.lintErrors.length ? "OK" : newFix || newLint.length ? "**NEW on this branch**" : "pre-existing (same on main)";
  if (verdict.includes("NEW")) newProblems++;
  console.log(`| \`${file}\` | ${describe(branch)} | ${main ? describe(main) : "new file"} | ${verdict} |`);
}
process.exit(newProblems ? 1 : 0);
EOF
```

```mjs
// Read-only facts for /pr-draft: what the PR would contain, its size against the team
// limit, how far the branch is behind main, and which local files should stay out of it.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/pr-facts.mjs [base-ref]   (default origin/main; run `git fetch` first)
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const base = process.argv[2] ?? "origin/main";
const git = (...args) => execFileSync("git", args, { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();
const lines = (s) => s.split("\n").filter(Boolean);

const branch = git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD");
const mergeBase = git("merge-base", base, "HEAD");
const [behind, ahead] = git("rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", `${base}...HEAD`).split(/\s+/).map(Number);

// Same rule as AGENTS.md: limits apply to code files only, not docs, logs, lock or generated files.
const isCode = (f) => !/\.(md|mdx|txt|pdf|png|jpe?g|gif|svg|lock)$|(^|\/)(ai-logs|docs)\/|yarn\.lock|\.generated\./.test(f);
const numstat = (range) => lines(git("diff", "--numstat", ...range)).map((l) => {
  const [add, del, path] = l.split("\t");
  return { path, add: Number(add) || 0, del: Number(del) || 0 };
});
const committed = numstat([`${mergeBase}..HEAD`]);
const uncommitted = numstat(["HEAD"]);
const untracked = lines(git("ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard"));
const all = new Map();
for (const f of [...committed, ...uncommitted]) {
  const prev = all.get(f.path) ?? { path: f.path, add: 0, del: 0 };
  all.set(f.path, { path: f.path, add: prev.add + f.add, del: prev.del + f.del });
}
const files = [...all.values()];
const code = files.filter((f) => isCode(f.path));
const codeLines = code.reduce((n, f) => n + f.add + f.del, 0);

// Local files that never belong in a code PR.
const neverCommit = (f) => /^(\.claude|\.specstory)\/|^Issue_.*\.(json|md)$|^Claude-.*\.md$|\.env/.test(f);
const tests = files.filter((f) => /\.(test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/.test(f.path)).map((f) => f.path);

const out = [`# PR facts`, "", `Branch \`${branch}\` vs \`${base}\`: ${ahead} commit(s) ahead, **${behind} behind**.`, ""];
if (branch === "main") out.push("**You are on `main`.** Code PRs come from a `feat/issue-N-…` or `fix/issue-N-…` branch.", "");
out.push(`**Size (code only):** ${codeLines} lines changed in ${code.length} file(s); limit 500 lines / 10 files (AGENTS.md) → ${codeLines > 500 || code.length > 10 ? "**OVER — split it**" : "OK"}.`, "");
out.push("| File | + | − | Code? | State |", "|---|---|---|---|---|");
const committedPaths = new Set(committed.map((f) => f.path));
const uncommittedPaths = new Set(uncommitted.map((f) => f.path));
for (const f of files.sort((a, b) => a.path.localeCompare(b.path))) {
  const state = committedPaths.has(f.path) ? (uncommittedPaths.has(f.path) ? "committed + uncommitted edits" : "committed") : "uncommitted";
  out.push(`| \`${f.path}\` | ${f.add} | ${f.del} | ${isCode(f.path) ? "yes" : "no"} | ${state} |`);
}
for (const f of untracked) out.push(`| \`${f}\` | | | ${isCode(f) ? "yes" : "no"} | untracked${neverCommit(f) ? " — **leave out**" : ""} |`);
out.push("", `**Test files in the change:** ${tests.map((t) => `\`${t}\``).join(", ") || "none"}`);
const leaveOut = [...files.map((f) => f.path), ...untracked].filter(neverCommit);
if (leaveOut.length) out.push("", `**Never commit:** ${leaveOut.map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(", ")}`);
console.log(out.join("\n"));

```

## The three new skills

**`/dev-checks`** runs your local checks and separates new problems from ones already on `main`.
- **`checks-plan.mjs`** works out which files changed against `main`, including commits, uncommitted edits and untracked files. It then finds the package each one belongs to and the tests named after it, and prints the exact commands.
- **`biome-compare.mjs`** runs Biome on your copy of each file and on `main`'s copy, then labels each problem **NEW** or **pre-existing**. It only prints results and never changes your files.
- **Order of checks:** Biome, then the type check per package, then the related unit tests. That follows the repo rule that type errors often cause test failures.
- **Failures elsewhere in the codebase** are marked *Unverified*. You get commands to confirm them on `main` yourself.
- **E2E tests** are only listed for you to run.

**`/pr-draft`** writes the PR description and everything around it.
- **`pr-facts.mjs`** reports how far your branch is ahead of and behind `main`, and the code-only size against the 500-line / 10-file limit. It also lists each file's state and which files to leave out: the `Issue_*` files, `.claude`, and AI logs, which go in their own PR.
- **The description** follows your PR #84 layout: the upstream template's headings, with `Closes #N`, What/Why/Design, Test strategy, CI-or-manual and Commands inside them, then the Tech Debt section word for word.
- **It warns you first** if you're on `main`, behind `main` (it suggests merge rather than rebase), over the size limit (with a stacked-split plan and every command explained), or have no tests.
- **It also gives you** a conventional-commit title, a draft commit message, and a reminder that a teammate has to merge the PR.

**`/dev-uml`** drafts the D6 diagrams.
- **Before drafting,** it confirms the scope with you (classes, the sequence, the annotations) and asks Mermaid or PlantUML.
- **What it writes:**
  - the `.mmd` sources, with existing and new code colour-coded, a legend, design notes and real UML notation;
  - the Q&A file, word for word, with **answers left blank** and optional hint comments to delete;
  - a local `uml-ai-record.md` to help you answer the AI-use question.
- **No renderer is installed.** It offers `npx mermaid-cli`, which downloads about 150 MB, so it asks first, or exporting from mermaid.live yourself. It never sends diagrams to the PlantUML server without your yes.

## What testing found

**Biome isn't reliable on this machine.** Your one changed file, `AvailabilitySettings.tsx`, shows 2 Biome errors. I first blamed Windows line endings, but that test was set up wrong. Comparing against `main` shows the import-order problem **already exists on `main`**, so your change didn't cause it. Running `--write` to clear it would rewrite the whole file. That's why `/dev-checks` compares with `main`, and I've corrected the note in `setup-notes.md`.

**Two smaller fixes along the way:**
- Yarn 4 doesn't accept a `-s` flag.
- When Biome reads from stdin, it only shows its fixes if you add `--write`. Even then it prints them and leaves the file alone; I checked the file's checksum before and after.

**Two things worth knowing about your repo right now:**
- **Your edit sits directly on `main`.** `AvailabilitySettings.tsx` has `availabilityView = "grid", //grid` as an uncommitted change. Your local `main` is also 13 commits behind `origin/main`. Neither was caused by the skills, but `/pr-draft` and `/dev-checks` will point both out.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 00:39:01Z)**_

I didn't give the Tier 2 skills scripts because their main work is judgment: understanding the issue, picking alternatives, tracing bugs. I gave scripts only to tasks with a mechanical answer, like counting criteria, comparing files or checking links. But you're right that concept location has a mechanical first pass, and the template wording is a real reliability gap.

## Why Tier 2 has no scripts, and where that's wrong

In Tier 1 I used scripts where the answer should be the same every run. A script also leaves an auditable record in the log, and it's easy to check against reality. That's how the Biome mistake surfaced: comparing against `main` exposed my wrong line-ending explanation.

For Tier 2 I assumed I'd do the searching myself with `rg` and `ast-grep`. That has three costs:
- **It isn't repeatable.** Two runs of `/plan-estimate` might search different terms and find different files.
- **You can't easily learn the method.** Concept location is a skill the course wants you to practise, and `--hypothesis` is meant to support that.
- **I may skip a layer.** In Cal.diy a concept usually spans several layers, and a guided search covers them all every time.

A first-pass script for `/plan-estimate` would make sense. Given a few terms from the issue, for example `node locate.mjs recurrence "repeat weekly"`, it would search:
1. **File and folder names.**
2. **The UI text:** find matching text in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`, then the translation keys, then the components that use those keys. This is often the fastest route from what the user sees to the code.
3. **The database schema:** models and fields in `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`.
4. **The API:** tRPC routers and API v2 controllers.
5. **Existing tests** that mention the terms.
6. **Documentation:** `agents/knowledge-base.md`, `agents/rules/`, `docs/`.

It would print a candidate table. I would still read each hit and mark it Confirmed or Unverified, because a name match isn't proof.

A second script, `dependents.mjs <file>`, would list who imports a file, for the impact-analysis step. `/pr-review` could reuse both.

## How sure can we be that templates are copied word for word?

**Right now, not fully.** The skills tell me to copy from the reference file, but I'm regenerating the text. I could change a word or a heading without noticing. The only safety net is `/pr-preflight`, which checks headings exist, not exact wording.

**Filling a template with a script removes most of the risk.** The fixed wording would come from the file itself; I would only supply the values for the blanks.

The details matter, though:
1. **Templates are pulled from the reference by a script,** not retyped by me. A script extracts each template block marked *verbatim* into `.claude/course/templates/<name>.md`, so no copy of the wording passes through me. `/sprint-init` would do the same each sprint.
2. **Blanks are named placeholders** such as `{{introduced}}`. Values are passed in a JSON file and replaced with a plain string replace. I'd avoid `printf` because it treats `%` specially, and Python f-strings because they treat `{}` specially, which clashes with code in the values. Shell arguments also break on quotes and newlines, which a JSON file avoids.
3. **Some templates repeat parts.** The rubric table and the AI Assistance table need one row per entry, so the script needs a repeat-this-row placeholder.
4. **Edits after filling can still break the wording,** whether from you or from me. So the stronger guarantee is a separate check, `verify-template.mjs <template> <file>`: every fixed line of the template must appear exactly and in order, while the blanks can hold anything. It works on any draft, and `/pr-preflight` could run it against the text actually posted on GitHub.

With 1, 2 and 4 together, the fixed wording comes from the source file, and any change to it is caught before you post. That's as close to certain as we can get. The values I fill in are still my writing and need your review.

// Shared helpers for the template scripts. Templates are always read straight from the sprint
// reference file named in current-sprint.md, so there is no second copy that could drift.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

const CONFIG = ".claude/course/current-sprint.md";

export function referencePath() {
  const row = readFileSync(CONFIG, "utf8").split("\n").find((l) => l.startsWith("| Reference file"));
  if (!row) throw new Error(`"Reference file" row missing from ${CONFIG}`);
  return row.split("|")[2].trim().replace(/`/g, "");
}

// A template is a "### N. Title (verbatim|suggested…)" heading followed by a ```markdown block.
export function loadTemplates() {
  const text = readFileSync(referencePath(), "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
  const templates = [];
  const heading = /^### (\d+)\. (.+?)$/gm;
  let m;
  while ((m = heading.exec(text))) {
    const fenceStart = text.indexOf("```markdown\n", m.index);
    const nextHeading = text.slice(m.index + m[0].length).search(/^### /m);
    if (fenceStart < 0 || (nextHeading >= 0 && fenceStart > m.index + m[0].length + nextHeading)) continue;
    const bodyStart = fenceStart + "```markdown\n".length;
    const body = text.slice(bodyStart, text.indexOf("\n```", bodyStart) + 1);
    const title = m[2];
    const name = title.split(/ — | \(/)[0].toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-").replace(/^-|-$/g, "");
    templates.push({ number: Number(m[1]), name, title, verbatim: /verbatim/i.test(title), body });
  }
  return templates;
}

export function findTemplate(key) {
  const all = loadTemplates();
  const t = all.find((x) => x.name === key || String(x.number) === String(key));
  if (!t) throw new Error(`No template "${key}". Available: ${all.map((x) => `${x.number}=${x.name}`).join(", ")}`);
  return t;
}

// Per-template adjustments, kept small and explicit:
//  - drop: lines that are only examples (the course's sample rows), never required
//  - optional: lines that are required only when relevant
export const OVERRIDES = {
  "ai-assistance-comment": { drop: [/jsmith/], optional: [/^\*\*Attachments:\*\*/] },
};

// Placeholders: the parts of a template the author fills in. Everything else is fixed text.
//  [ ... ]  (may span lines)   < ... >   ...   @your-github-username   empty table cells
const PLACEHOLDER = /\[[^\]]*\]|<[^>\n]*>|\.\.\.|@your-github-username|(?<=\|)[ \t]+(?=\|)/g;

export function placeholders(body) {
  return [...body.matchAll(PLACEHOLDER)].map((m) => ({ text: m[0], index: m.index }));
}

// Fixed segments: the template text between placeholders, with whitespace collapsed, in order.
// Comparing with collapsed whitespace means re-wrapped lines still count as verbatim.
export function fixedSegments(template) {
  const o = OVERRIDES[template.name] ?? {};
  const lines = template.body.split("\n").filter((l) => !(o.drop ?? []).some((re) => re.test(l)));
  const segments = [];
  let current = [];
  const flush = (optional) => {
    const text = current.join(" ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    if ((text.match(/[A-Za-z0-9]/g) || []).length >= 3) segments.push({ text, optional });
    current = [];
  };
  // Re-join the lines so multi-line [ ... ] placeholders are found, then walk the pieces.
  const body = lines.join("\n");
  let last = 0;
  for (const p of placeholders(body)) {
    pushText(body.slice(last, p.index));
    flush(false);
    last = p.index + p.text.length;
  }
  pushText(body.slice(last));
  flush(false);
  // Mark segments that come from optional lines.
  for (const s of segments) {
    if ((o.optional ?? []).some((re) => re.test(s.text))) s.optional = true;
  }
  return segments;

  function pushText(t) {
    for (const piece of t.split("\n")) {
      // A table row or a blank line ends a segment, so one table cell can't swallow the next row.
      if (piece.trim() === "" || /^\|/.test(piece)) {
        flush(false);
        if (piece.trim()) {
          current.push(piece);
          flush(false);
        }
        continue;
      }
      current.push(piece);
    }
  }
}

export const normalize = (s) => s.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();

// Checks every required fixed segment appears, in order, in the draft.
export function verify(template, draft) {
  const text = normalize(draft);
  const results = [];
  let from = 0;
  for (const seg of fixedSegments(template)) {
    const at = text.indexOf(seg.text, from);
    if (at >= 0) {
      results.push({ ...seg, ok: true });
      from = at + seg.text.length;
    } else {
      results.push({ ...seg, ok: seg.optional, closest: closest(text, seg.text) });
    }
  }
  return results;
}

// For a missing segment, the stretch of the draft that shares the most words with it,
// so the report can show what was changed.
function closest(text, target) {
  const words = target.toLowerCase().split(" ");
  const want = new Set(words);
  const tokens = text.split(" ");
  let best = { score: 0, start: 0 };
  for (let i = 0; i < tokens.length; i++) {
    let score = 0;
    for (let j = i; j < Math.min(tokens.length, i + words.length); j++) if (want.has(tokens[j].toLowerCase())) score++;
    if (score > best.score) best = { score, start: i };
  }
  return best.score ? tokens.slice(best.start, best.start + words.length + 2).join(" ") : null;
}

```mjs
// Fills a course template from the sprint reference with values from a JSON file. The fixed
// wording is copied from the reference file byte for byte; only the blanks are replaced.
// The result is then checked with the same verifier /pr-preflight uses.
//
// 1. List the blanks:  node .claude/course/scripts/template-fill.mjs --slots <template>
// 2. Write values.json:
//      { "slots": { "1": "text for blank 1", "3": "..." },        blanks by number
//        "lines": { "12": ["row 1", "row 2"] } }                   replace whole template line 12
//                                                                  (e.g. example table rows) with these lines
// 3. Fill:             node .claude/course/scripts/template-fill.mjs <template> <values.json> <out.md>
//
// Values come from a JSON file, not command-line arguments, so quotes, $, %, backticks and
// newlines in them are never interpreted by a shell or a format function.
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { findTemplate, slots, verify } from "./template-lib.mjs";

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
if (args[0] === "--slots") {
  const t = findTemplate(args[1]);
  const lineOf = (i) => t.body.slice(0, i).split("\n").length;
  console.log(`Template ${t.number} "${t.name}". Blanks (number, template line, current text):`);
  slots(t).forEach((s, i) => console.log(`  ${String(i + 1).padStart(2)}  line ${String(lineOf(s.index)).padStart(2)}  ${JSON.stringify(s.text)}`));
  console.log("\nTemplate lines (for \"lines\" replacements):");
  t.body.split("\n").forEach((l, i) => l && console.log(`  ${String(i + 1).padStart(2)}  ${l}`));
  process.exit(0);
}

const [key, valuesFile, outFile] = args;
if (!key || !valuesFile || !outFile) {
  console.error("Usage: template-fill.mjs <template> <values.json> <out.md>   |   template-fill.mjs --slots <template>");
  process.exit(1);
}
if (existsSync(outFile) && !args.includes("--overwrite")) {
  console.error(`${outFile} already exists; pass --overwrite to replace it.`);
  process.exit(1);
}

const t = findTemplate(key);
const values = JSON.parse(readFileSync(valuesFile, "utf8"));
const all = slots(t);
const lineStarts = [0];
for (let i = 0; i < t.body.length; i++) if (t.body[i] === "\n") lineStarts.push(i + 1);

// Edits are [start, end, replacement] on the original body, applied from the end backwards
// so earlier offsets stay valid.
const edits = [];
for (const [ln, rows] of Object.entries(values.lines ?? {})) {
  const n = Number(ln);
  if (!lineStarts[n - 1] && n !== 1) throw new Error(`Template has no line ${ln}`);
  const start = lineStarts[n - 1];
  const end = (lineStarts[n] ?? t.body.length + 1) - 1;
  edits.push([start, end, [].concat(rows).join("\n")]);
}
const insideLineEdit = (i) => edits.some(([s, e]) => i >= s && i < e);
const unfilled = [];
all.forEach((s, i) => {
  const v = values.slots?.[String(i + 1)];
  if (insideLineEdit(s.index)) return;
  if (v === undefined) unfilled.push(`${i + 1} ${JSON.stringify(s.text)}`);
  else edits.push([s.index, s.index + s.text.length, String(v)]);
});
for (const k of Object.keys(values.slots ?? {})) if (!all[Number(k) - 1]) throw new Error(`Template has no blank ${k}`);

let out = t.body;
for (const [s, e, r] of edits.sort((a, b) => b[0] - a[0])) out = out.slice(0, s) + r + out.slice(e);
writeFileSync(outFile, out);

const check = verify(t, out).filter((r) => !r.ok);
console.log(`Wrote ${outFile} from template ${t.number} "${t.name}".`);
if (unfilled.length) console.log(`Blanks left as in the template (fill or delete them):\n  ${unfilled.join("\n  ")}`);
if (check.length) {
  console.log(`WARNING: the fixed wording no longer matches the template (a "lines" replacement probably removed fixed text):`);
  for (const r of check) console.log(`  - "${r.text}"`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log("Fixed wording verified against the template.");
```

```mjs
// Read-only first pass of concept location for /plan-estimate (and /pr-review, /plan-design).
// Searches tracked files only (git grep / git ls-files), layer by layer, and prints candidates.
// Every hit is a lead, not a finding: read the code before calling it Confirmed.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/locate.mjs <term> [term ...] [--max <n>]
//   e.g. node .claude/course/scripts/locate.mjs recurring "repeat weekly"
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const maxAt = args.indexOf("--max");
const MAX = maxAt >= 0 ? Number(args.splice(maxAt, 2)[1]) : 15;
const terms = args;
if (!terms.length) {
  console.error('Usage: locate.mjs <term> [term ...] [--max <n>]   e.g. locate.mjs recurring "repeat weekly"');
  process.exit(1);
}

// "repeat weekly" is also searched as repeatWeekly, RepeatWeekly, repeat-weekly, repeat_weekly.
function variants(term) {
  const words = term.toLowerCase().split(/[\s_-]+/).filter(Boolean);
  const camel = words.map((w, i) => (i ? w[0].toUpperCase() + w.slice(1) : w)).join("");
  return [...new Set([term, words.join(" "), camel, camel[0].toUpperCase() + camel.slice(1), words.join("-"), words.join("_")])];
}
const allVariants = terms.flatMap(variants);
const escape = (s) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
const anyTerm = new RegExp(allVariants.map(escape).join("|"), "i");

// git grep exits 1 when nothing matches; that is not an error here.
function gitGrep(pathspecs, extra = []) {
  try {
    return execFileSync("git", ["grep", "-n", "-I", "-i", ...extra, ...allVariants.flatMap((v) => ["-e", v]), "--", ...pathspecs], { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 })
      .split("\n").filter(Boolean).map((l) => {
        const m = l.match(/^(.+?):(\d+):(.*)$/);
        return m ? { file: m[1], line: Number(m[2]), text: m[3].trim() } : null;
      }).filter(Boolean);
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.status === 1) return [];
    throw e;
  }
}
const byFile = (hits) => {
  const map = new Map();
  for (const h of hits) (map.get(h.file) ?? map.set(h.file, []).get(h.file)).push(h);
  return [...map.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1].length - a[1].length);
};
const snippet = (t) => (t.length > 110 ? `${t.slice(0, 107)}…` : t).replace(/\|/g, "\\|");
const out = [`# locate: ${terms.map((t) => `"${t}"`).join(", ")}`, "", `Variants searched: ${allVariants.map((v) => `\`${v}\``).join(", ")}. Tracked files only. Hits are leads; read the code before calling one Confirmed.`];
const section = (title, rows, header = "| File | Hits | First hit |\n|---|---|---|") => {
  out.push("", `## ${title}`, "");
  if (!rows.length) return out.push("None found.");
  out.push(header, ...rows.slice(0, MAX));
  if (rows.length > MAX) out.push(`| … ${rows.length - MAX} more (use --max) | | |`);
};
const fileRows = (hits) => byFile(hits).map(([f, hs]) => `| \`${f}:${hs[0].line}\` | ${hs.length} | ${snippet(hs[0].text)} |`);

const CODE = ["*.ts", "*.tsx", "*.js", "*.jsx", ":!*.test.*", ":!*.spec.*", ":!*.e2e.*", ":!**/locales/**", ":!*.generated.*", ":!docs/**", ":!ai-logs/**"];

// 1. File and folder names
const files = execFileSync("git", ["ls-files"], { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 }).split("\n").filter((f) => anyTerm.test(f) && !/^(ai-logs|docs)\//.test(f));
section("1. File and folder names", files.map((f) => `| \`${f}\` | | |`), "| Path | | |\n|---|---|---|");

// 2. UI text: English strings → translation keys → code that uses those keys
const COMMON = "packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json";
const strings = JSON.parse(readFileSync(COMMON, "utf8"));
const keys = Object.entries(strings).filter(([k, v]) => anyTerm.test(k) || anyTerm.test(String(v)));
const keyRows = [];
for (const [k, v] of keys.slice(0, MAX)) {
  let uses = [];
  try {
    uses = execFileSync("git", ["grep", "-n", "-F", "-e", `"${k}"`, "-e", `'${k}'`, "--", "*.ts", "*.tsx", ":!**/locales/**"], { encoding: "utf8" }).split("\n").filter(Boolean);
  } catch {}
  keyRows.push(`| \`${k}\` | "${snippet(String(v))}" | ${uses.length ? uses.slice(0, 3).map((u) => `\`${u.split(":").slice(0, 2).join(":")}\``).join(", ") + (uses.length > 3 ? ` +${uses.length - 3}` : "") : "no direct use found (key may be built dynamically)"} |`);
}
section(`2. UI text (${COMMON})`, keyRows, "| Key | English text | Used at |\n|---|---|---|");
if (keys.length > MAX) out.push(`(${keys.length} matching keys in total)`);

// 3. Database schema: models and fields
const SCHEMA = "packages/prisma/schema.prisma";
const schemaLines = readFileSync(SCHEMA, "utf8").split(/\r?\n/);
let model = null;
const schemaRows = [];
schemaLines.forEach((l, i) => {
  const m = l.match(/^(model|enum|type)\s+(\w+)/);
  if (m) model = m[2];
  if (anyTerm.test(l)) schemaRows.push(`| \`${SCHEMA}:${i + 1}\` | ${model ?? ""} | ${snippet(l.trim())} |`);
});
section("3. Database schema (Prisma)", schemaRows, "| Location | Model/enum | Line |\n|---|---|---|");

// 4. API layer: tRPC routers and API v2
section("4. API (tRPC routers, API v2)", fileRows(gitGrep(["packages/trpc/server/routers/**", "apps/api/v2/src/**", ":!*.spec.*", ":!*.test.*"])));

// 5. Other code, most hits first
const apiOrSchema = /^(packages\/trpc\/server\/routers|apps\/api\/v2\/src)\//;
section("5. Other code (most hits first)", fileRows(gitGrep(CODE).filter((h) => !apiOrSchema.test(h.file))));

// 6. Tests
```

```mjs
// Read-only impact helper: lists the tracked files that import a given file, resolving
// relative paths, workspace package names (@calcom/...) and apps/web's tsconfig aliases.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/dependents.mjs <file> [--depth 2]
import { readFileSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join, normalize, extname } from "node:path";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const depthAt = args.indexOf("--depth");
const DEPTH = depthAt >= 0 ? Number(args.splice(depthAt, 2)[1]) : 1;
const target = args[0];
if (!target || !existsSync(target)) {
  console.error("Usage: dependents.mjs <existing file> [--depth n]");
  process.exit(1);
}
const posix = (p) => normalize(p).replace(/\\/g, "/");
const run = (...a) => execFileSync("git", a, { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });

// Workspace package name -> folder, from every tracked package.json.
const packages = new Map();
for (const pj of run("ls-files", "*package.json").split(/\r?\n/).filter((f) => f && !f.includes("node_modules"))) {
  try {
    const name = JSON.parse(readFileSync(pj, "utf8")).name;
    if (name && !packages.has(name)) packages.set(name, posix(dirname(pj)));
  } catch {}
}
// apps/web tsconfig "paths" aliases (e.g. ~/* -> modules/*).
const WEB_ALIASES = { "~/": "apps/web/modules/", "@components/": "apps/web/components/", "@lib/": "apps/web/lib/", "@server/": "apps/web/server/", "@pages/": "apps/web/pages/" };

const stripExt = (p) => p.replace(/\.(d\.)?[cm]?[jt]sx?$/, "").replace(/\/index$/, "");
function resolve(spec, importer) {
  if (spec.startsWith(".")) return stripExt(posix(join(dirname(importer), spec)));
  for (const [alias, dir] of Object.entries(WEB_ALIASES)) if (importer.startsWith("apps/web/") && spec.startsWith(alias)) return stripExt(dir + spec.slice(alias.length));
  const parts = spec.split("/");
  const name = spec.startsWith("@") ? parts.slice(0, 2).join("/") : parts[0];
  const dir = packages.get(name);
  if (!dir) return null;
  const rest = parts.slice(spec.startsWith("@") ? 2 : 1).join("/");
  return stripExt(rest ? `${dir}/${rest}` : `${dir}/index`);
}

// Files whose import specifiers end in the target's file name, then keep only true matches.
function importersOf(file) {
  const stem = stripExt(posix(file)).split("/").pop();
  const want = stripExt(posix(file));
  let lines = [];
  try {
    lines = run("grep", "-n", "-E", `(from|import|require)[ (]*["'][^"']*${stem.replace(/[.[\]()]/g, "\\$&")}["']`, "--", "*.ts", "*.tsx", "*.js", "*.jsx", "*.mjs").split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean);
  } catch (e) {
    if (e.status !== 1) throw e;
  }
  const hits = [];
  for (const l of lines) {
    const m = l.match(/^(.+?):(\d+):([\s\S]*)$/);
    if (!m) continue;
    for (const s of m[3].matchAll(/["']([^"']+)["']/g)) {
      const r = resolve(s[1], m[1]);
      if (r && (r === want || r === `${want}/index` || `${r}/index` === want)) hits.push({ file: m[1], line: Number(m[2]), spec: s[1] });
    }
  }
  return hits;
}

const out = [`# Dependents of \`${posix(target)}\``, ""];
let frontier = [posix(target)];
const seen = new Set(frontier);
for (let level = 1; level <= DEPTH && frontier.length; level++) {
  const next = [];
  const rows = [];
  for (const f of frontier) {
    for (const h of importersOf(f)) {
      const kind = /\.(test|spec)\.|e2e/.test(h.file) ? "test" : "code";
      rows.push(`| \`${h.file}:${h.line}\` | ${kind} | \`${h.spec}\` |${DEPTH > 1 ? ` via \`${f}\` |` : ""}`);
      if (!seen.has(h.file)) {
        seen.add(h.file);
        next.push(h.file);
      }
    }
  }
  out.push(`## Level ${level}${level === 1 ? " (direct importers)" : ""}: ${rows.length}`, "");
  if (rows.length) out.push(`| Importer | Kind | Import |${DEPTH > 1 ? " Through |" : ""}`, `|---|---|---|${DEPTH > 1 ? "---|" : ""}`, ...rows, "");
  frontier = next;
}
out.push("Not detected: dynamic paths built at runtime, re-exports through barrel files (index.ts) beyond one hop, and generated app-store maps. Search for the exported names too before saying nothing else uses it.");
```

The template scripts and the concept-location scripts are built and wired into the skills. All the helper scripts are listed in `skills-catalog.md`, and you can run any of them yourself in Git Bash.

## The template scripts

All three read the templates straight from the sprint reference file (`sprint2-reference.md`) every time, so there's no second copy to drift. Next sprint, pointing the settings at the new reference is enough.

- **`template-verify.mjs <template> <file>`** checks that every fixed part of a template appears exactly and in order. The blanks can hold anything, and line wrapping doesn't matter.
  - Headings, list items and labels are checked separately, so your answers can sit between the questions.
  - Some templates have special cases: the course's example rows in the AI Assistance comment are ignored; the role ("Implementation / Code review / …") counts as a choice you make; the Attachments line is optional; and the check-in only checks the question wording, since the reference says its layout is only suggested.
- **`template-fill.mjs`** lists a template's numbered blanks (`--slots`). It then fills them from a JSON file and copies every fixed character from the reference.
  - It can replace whole lines, for example to swap the course's example rows for real ones.
  - It refuses to overwrite an existing file, and it runs the check before finishing.
  - Values go through JSON, so `$`, `%`, backticks, quotes and line breaks come through unchanged. I tested exactly that.
- **`/pr-preflight` now checks the exact wording** of the spec, the Tech Debt section, your AI Assistance comment and the reviewer's rubric, as posted on GitHub.
- **Shared rule 4 now says never retype a template.** `/plan-spec`, `/log-comment`, `/pr-draft`, `/pr-review` and `/dev-uml` each build theirs with the fill script.

## What testing on real text found

- **It catches one-word changes.** Swapping "one thing" for "something", or removing "unnecessary", was detected, and it showed the closest matching text.
- **Real problems on #63:** the user story has no "so that" clause, and the heading reads `## Open Question`. Your #69 AI comment, Julissa's rubric on PR #84 and your check-in all pass.
- **A bug the tests caught and I fixed:** the Q&A questions were first treated as one block, which would have failed once you added answers between them.

**What this does and doesn't guarantee:** the fixed wording comes from the source file, and any change to it is caught before posting. What goes in the blanks is still my writing, so it still needs your review.

## The concept-location scripts

- **`locate.mjs <terms…>`** searches in layers. It also tries naming variants of each term, such as `repeatWeekly` and `repeat-weekly`. The layers are:
  - file names;
  - **UI text → translation keys → the code that uses them**;
  - the Prisma schema;
  - tRPC and API v2;
  - other code, most hits first;
  - tests;
  - docs and `agents/` rules.

  On "recurring", it ranks `RecurringEventController.tsx` first among other code. That's the recurrence UI #63 will change. It also points to `EventType.recurringEvent` in the schema and `recurring-event.test.ts`.
- **`dependents.mjs <file> [--depth n]`** lists who imports a file. It understands relative paths, `@calcom/*` package names and `apps/web`'s `~/` shortcut. Two levels up from the controller, it finds both the web and platform wrappers.
- **Wired into** `/plan-estimate` (it runs these first, then reads the code before marking anything Confirmed), `/plan-design`, `/pr-review` and `/dev-uml`.

**Two bugs found and fixed along the way:**
- Windows line endings stopped `git grep`'s output from being read, so 4 of the 7 sections came back empty at first.
- API v2's `*.e2e-spec.ts` test files were being counted as API code.

`rg` and `ast-grep` aren't installed, so these scripts use `git grep`. I removed `rg` from the skills' pre-approved tools.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 00:54:15Z)**_

## What that line meant

The user-story template's fixed wording is `As a [type of user], I want [goal] so that [benefit].` The fill script only replaces the bracketed blanks and keeps "As a" exactly as written. So filling "event host" produced **"As a event host"**, which is ungrammatical.

The fix is a one-letter edit after filling, from "As a" to "As an". I added a note to `/plan-spec` saying this is allowed. That's safe because the checker looks for the fixed text **"## User Story As a"** somewhere in the draft, and "## User Story As an event host" contains it.

Then I reran each script once to confirm the edits hadn't broken anything: `preflight.mjs 69`, `log-scan`, `log-find`, `checks-plan` and `pr-facts`, and checked that the skills are still excluded from git.

**I should have pointed out a side effect:** "As an" passes only because the check looks for the fixed text anywhere, even in the middle of a longer word. That same looseness means **"As administrator"** would also pass, because it starts with "As a". The check stops at the end of each fixed part and doesn't require a word break after it. It's a small gap, but it is one. I can tighten it so a fixed part must end at a word boundary, with "a" → "an" allowed explicitly.

## Fix 1: `git grep` output was being thrown away

**Cause.** `git config core.autocrlf` is `true`, so the files on your disk end their lines with Windows line endings (`\r\n`). When `git grep` prints a matching line, the `\r` is still part of the text, followed by git's own `\n`. In `locate.mjs` I then:
- split the output on `\n` only, so every line kept a trailing `\r`;
- parsed each line with `/^(.+?):(\d+):(.*)$/`. In JavaScript `.` does not match `\r`, and `$` (without the `m` flag) needs the end of the string, so the match failed. Every line was quietly dropped, and sections 4–7 printed "None found."

**Change, in `gitGrep()` in `locate.mjs`:**
```js
.split(/\r?\n/)                                  // was .split("\n")
const m = l.match(/^(.+?):(\d+):([\s\S]*)$/);    // was (.*)$
```
Splitting on `\r?\n` removes the trailing `\r`. `[\s\S]*` matches any character, as a backup.

**Could it cause regressions?** Unlikely:
- **Sections 1–3 don't use this function.** File names come from `git ls-files`, and the translation file and Prisma schema are read directly. That's why those three sections worked from the start.
- **Splitting on `\r?\n` changes one rare case:** a line containing a lone `\r` in the middle would be split in two. That's very rare in this repo.
- **The `\r` bug could exist elsewhere,** anywhere a script parses `git grep` lines with `.`:
  - `dependents.mjs` was written after I found the bug and uses the fixed pattern.
  - `preflight.mjs` already splits on `\r?\n`.
  - `log-find.mjs` counts matches across the whole text, not by line.
  - `checks-plan.mjs` and `pr-facts.mjs` only parse git's own output (file names and counts), which never contains `\r`.

  So I believe none are affected, but I haven't checked each one directly.

## Fix 2: API v2's end-to-end test files appeared as API code

**Cause.** API v2 names its end-to-end tests `*.e2e-spec.ts`, for example `recurring-bookings.e2e-spec.ts`. Section 4 excluded `*.spec.*`, which needs the text `.spec.`. These names contain `-spec.` instead, so they slipped through and topped the API list.

**Change, made with a one-line `sed` edit to `locate.mjs`:**
- **Section 4 (API):** added the exclusion `":!*e2e-spec*"`.
- **Section 6 (Tests):** added `"*e2e-spec*"` to the included patterns, so those tests still show up where they belong.

**Could it cause regressions?**
- **`sed` can fail silently.** If its pattern doesn't match, it changes nothing and reports success. I checked that `e2e-spec` appears twice, once per edit, and reran section 4. That's reasonable evidence, but checking the file itself is better.
- **The pattern is broad.** Git's `*` also matches `/`, so `*e2e-spec*` excludes any path containing "e2e-spec" anywhere, including a hypothetical folder of that name. That's acceptable here.
- **Section 5 ("Other code") doesn't exclude `*e2e-spec*` itself.** It's safe today only because section 5 already removes everything under `apps/api/v2/src/`, where all of these files live. An `e2e-spec` file elsewhere would show up as code.

```mjs
// Read-only: compares the course templates in two sprint reference files, so /sprint-init can
// show exactly what changed between sprints (added, removed, reworded templates).
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/template-diff.mjs <old-reference.md> <new-reference.md>
import { loadTemplates } from "./template-lib.mjs";

const [oldRef, newRef] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!oldRef || !newRef) {
  console.error("Usage: template-diff.mjs <old-reference.md> <new-reference.md>");
  process.exit(1);
}
const load = (path) => {
  process.env.COURSE_REFERENCE = path;
  return new Map(loadTemplates().map((t) => [t.name, t]));
};
const before = load(oldRef);
const after = load(newRef);

// Line diff via longest common subsequence; templates are short, so this is cheap.
function lineDiff(a, b) {
  const x = a.split("\n"), y = b.split("\n");
  const L = Array.from({ length: x.length + 1 }, () => Array(y.length + 1).fill(0));
  for (let i = x.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) for (let j = y.length - 1; j >= 0; j--) L[i][j] = x[i] === y[j] ? L[i + 1][j + 1] + 1 : Math.max(L[i + 1][j], L[i][j + 1]);
  const out = [];
  let i = 0, j = 0;
  while (i < x.length || j < y.length) {
    if (i < x.length && j < y.length && x[i] === y[j]) { i++; j++; }
    else if (j < y.length && (i === x.length || L[i][j + 1] >= L[i + 1][j])) out.push(`    + ${y[j++]}`);
    else out.push(`    - ${x[i++]}`);
  }
  return out;
}

const lines = [`# Template changes: ${oldRef} → ${newRef}`, ""];
for (const [name, t] of after) {
  const old = before.get(name);
  if (!old) lines.push(`- **NEW** ${t.number}. ${name} (${t.verbatim ? "verbatim" : "suggested"})`);
  else if (old.body !== t.body || old.verbatim !== t.verbatim) {
    lines.push(`- **CHANGED** ${t.number}. ${name}${old.verbatim !== t.verbatim ? ` (now ${t.verbatim ? "verbatim" : "suggested"})` : ""}`, ...lineDiff(old.body, t.body));
  } else lines.push(`- unchanged: ${name}`);
}
for (const [name] of before) if (!after.has(name)) lines.push(`- **REMOVED** ${name}`);
console.log(lines.join("\n"));

```

```mjs
// Read-only backlog audit for /sprint-backlog: the current milestone's issues, the previous
// milestone's unfinished issues (carryovers), and open issues with no milestone.
// Only runs `gh issue list`; never edits issues, labels or milestones.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/backlog.mjs
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { findTemplate, verify } from "./template-lib.mjs";

const config = readFileSync(".claude/course/current-sprint.md", "utf8");
const configValue = (key) => {
  const row = config.split("\n").find((l) => l.startsWith(`| ${key} |`));
  if (!row) throw new Error(`"${key}" row missing from current-sprint.md`);
  return row.split("|")[2].trim().replace(/`/g, "");
};
const repo = configValue("GitHub repo").split(" ")[0];
const milestone = configValue("Milestone");
const previous = configValue("Previous milestone");

const FIELDS = "number,title,state,assignees,labels,body,milestone,url";
const list = (...filters) => JSON.parse(execFileSync("gh", ["issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--limit", "300", "--json", FIELDS, ...filters], { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 }));

const current = list("--state", "all", "--milestone", milestone);
const carry = list("--state", "open", "--milestone", previous);
const unplanned = list("--state", "open", "--search", "no:milestone");

const feature = findTemplate("feature-issue");
const bug = findTemplate("bug-report");
const labelsOf = (i) => i.labels.map((l) => l.name);
// Team convention seen on the issues: effort:low / effort:medium / effort:high, plus "scope: xl".
const effort = (i) => labelsOf(i).find((l) => /^effort:/i.test(l)) ?? null;

function audit(i) {
  const isBug = labelsOf(i).some((l) => /bug/i.test(l)) || /observed behavio/i.test(i.body || "");
  const missing = verify(isBug ? bug : feature, i.body || "").filter((r) => !r.ok).map((r) => r.text);
  const problems = [];
  if (missing.length) problems.push(`spec: ${missing.length === (isBug ? 4 : 7) ? "no course template" : `missing/changed ${missing.map((m) => `"${m}"`).join(", ")}`}`);
  if (!effort(i)) problems.push("no effort label (estimate)");
  if (i.assignees.length !== 1) problems.push(`${i.assignees.length} owners (need exactly 1)`);
  if (labelsOf(i).some((l) => /scope: ?xl/i.test(l)) || /effort:high/i.test(effort(i) ?? "")) problems.push("large: consider sub-issues");
  return { isBug, problems };
}
const owners = (i) => i.assignees.map((a) => `@${a.login}`).join(", ") || "—";
const esc = (s) => String(s).replace(/\|/g, "\\|");
const row = (i) => {
  const a = audit(i);
  return `| [#${i.number}](${i.url}) | ${esc(i.title)} | ${i.state.toLowerCase()} | ${owners(i)} | ${effort(i) ?? "—"} | ${a.isBug ? "bug" : "feature"} | ${a.problems.length ? a.problems.map(esc).join("; ") : "OK"} |`;
};
const header = "| Issue | Title | State | Owner | Estimate | Type | Problems |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|";

const out = [`# Backlog audit: ${milestone}`, ""];
out.push(`## ${milestone} (${current.length} issues)`, "", header, ...current.map(row), "");

// Scope minimum (course): 2 medium issues per CSCI 435 member; 2 medium + 1 small per CSCI 535 member.
const perMember = new Map();
for (const i of current) for (const a of i.assignees) {
  const m = perMember.get(a.login) ?? { low: 0, medium: 0, high: 0, none: 0 };
  const e = (effort(i) ?? "").replace(/^effort:/i, "").toLowerCase();
  m[e in m ? e : "none"]++;
  perMember.set(a.login, m);
}
out.push("## Scope per member", "", "Course minimum: 2 medium issues per CSCI 435 member; 2 medium + 1 small per CSCI 535 member (or equivalent points). Which course each member is in isn't recorded here.", "",
  "| Member | low | medium | high | no estimate |", "|---|---|---|---|---|",
  ...[...perMember].sort().map(([m, c]) => `| @${m} | ${c.low} | ${c.medium} | ${c.high} | ${c.none} |`), "");

out.push(`## Carryovers: still open in ${previous} (${carry.length})`, "", "Each must be moved into this sprint, or get a comment saying why not (closed, invalidated by later changes, or no longer relevant).", "");
if (carry.length) out.push(header, ...carry.map(row), "");
else out.push("None.", "");

out.push(`## Open issues with no milestone (${unplanned.length})`, "");
if (unplanned.length) out.push(header, ...unplanned.map(row));
else out.push("None.");
console.log(out.join("\n"));
```

```mjs
// Read-only: checks a sprint config has every row the course scripts read, that the files it
// names exist, and that its reference file parses into templates. Used by /sprint-init before
// a new config replaces the active one.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/config-check.mjs [config path]   (default: current-sprint.md)
import { readFileSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const path = process.argv[2] ?? ".claude/course/current-sprint.md";
const text = readFileSync(path, "utf8");
const value = (key) => text.split("\n").find((l) => l.startsWith(`| ${key} |`))?.split("|")[2]?.trim().replace(/`/g, "");

// Every row some script parses (log-scan, log-find, preflight, backlog, template-lib, …).
const REQUIRED = ["Sprint number", "Dates", "Time zone", "Reference file (templates, rubric, checklist)", "GitHub repo", "GitHub user", "Milestone", "Previous milestone", "AI log folder", "Docs folder", "Check-in", "Report", "Release tag"];
const problems = [];
for (const k of REQUIRED) if (!value(k)) problems.push(`missing row "${k}"`);
if (value("Dates") && !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} to \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value("Dates"))) problems.push(`"Dates" must look like "YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD", got "${value("Dates")}"`);
if (value("Time zone")) {
  try { new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en", { timeZone: value("Time zone") }); } catch { problems.push(`unknown time zone "${value("Time zone")}"`); }
}
const ref = value("Reference file (templates, rubric, checklist)");
if (ref && !existsSync(ref)) problems.push(`reference file not found: ${ref}`);
if (ref && existsSync(ref)) {
  const list = execFileSync("node", [".claude/course/scripts/template-verify.mjs", "--list"], { encoding: "utf8", env: { ...process.env, COURSE_REFERENCE: ref } });
  const count = list.split("\n").filter((l) => /^\s+\d+\s/.test(l)).length;
  if (!count) problems.push(`no templates parsed from ${ref} (each needs a "### N. Title (verbatim|suggested…)" heading followed by a \`\`\`markdown block)`);
  else console.log(`Reference ${ref}: ${count} templates parsed.`);
}
if (!/^\| ID \| Deliverable/m.test(text)) problems.push(`no deliverables table ("| ID | Deliverable | …")`);

console.log(problems.length ? `Config ${path}: ${problems.length} problem(s)\n  - ${problems.join("\n  - ")}` : `Config ${path}: OK`);
process.exit(problems.length ? 1 : 0);

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 01:30:28Z)**_

A skill runs in a fork when its `SKILL.md` frontmatter says `context: fork`. When you type its command, Claude Code doesn't load the skill's instructions into our conversation. It starts a separate agent instead: that agent gets the skill's text as its task, does the work with its own tools, and only its final message comes back to the main chat. The optional `agent:` field picks which kind of agent runs it; `general-purpose` is the standard one.

## A minimal test you can run

**1. Create the file** `agents/skills/dev-fork-test/SKILL.md`. The name starts with `dev-`, so your exclude rule already keeps it out of git.

```markdown
---
name: dev-fork-test
description: Test skill - checks that a forked skill run is captured by SpecStory.
disable-model-invocation: true
context: fork
agent: general-purpose
allowed-tools: Bash(ls *) Bash(git rev-parse *)
---

You are running as a forked skill. Do exactly this:
1. Run `ls` in the repository root.
2. Run `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`.
3. Reply with one line: "FORK TEST OK", the branch name, and the number of entries `ls` printed.
```

**2. Run it.** In a Claude Code session in the repo, type `/dev-fork-test`. If it doesn't show up in the `/` menu, restart Claude Code; new skill folders are sometimes only picked up at startup.

**3. What you should see in the chat:** a "running" indicator, then only the final message ("FORK TEST OK …"). The individual `ls` and `git` calls shouldn't appear in the main conversation.

**4. Then check the SpecStory log.** Run `specstory sync` if needed, then open the newest file in `.specstory/history/`. Look for:
- the forked run's turns, probably labelled `Agent - sidechain` like in your earlier test, starting with the skill's text ("You are running as a forked skill…");
- the `ls` and `git rev-parse` calls with their output;
- the final "FORK TEST OK" message in the main conversation.

**How to read the result:**
- If all three are there, a forked `/sprint-report` would be fully logged.
- If only the final message is there, forked skills lose their working steps in the log. That would fail the course's "full prompt and response history" rule, and the report should stay in the main chat.

**5. Delete the test skill afterwards:** `rm -r agents/skills/dev-fork-test`. I can delete it for you if you prefer.

Would you rather I create the test file, so you only need to run `/dev-fork-test`?

## The unexpected "User" entries

SpecStory labels each message by its **role**, not by who wrote it. Claude Code sends some of its own messages with the "user" role, so they appear as "User" even though you didn't type them:

| Line | Content | Who actually wrote it |
|---|---|---|
| 243 | `/dev-fork-test` | You. This one is correct. |
| 249 | `<local-command-caveat>…` | Claude Code. When you type a slash command, it adds a note explaining that the command came from you directly. |
| 321 | `<task-notification>…` | Claude Code. It tells the main conversation that the forked agent finished, and includes the result. |

The order quirk you noticed (the skill text at line 232 before your command at 243) has the same cause. Both messages have the same timestamp, `01:36:31Z`, and SpecStory lists the side conversation first. Nothing is missing or out of place in substance, and it's what you'd expect from how the transcript is recorded.

**Does it matter for grading?** The log is complete and unedited, which is what the course checks. A grader might wonder why "User" sent XML. If you want, the "What AI helped with" cell of your AI Assistance comment can say: *"User" entries containing `<local-command-caveat>` or `<task-notification>` are messages Claude Code adds automatically.* That explains the log without editing it, which stays forbidden.

**Two more things the log shows:**
1. **A fork costs a lot to start.** The notification reports `subagent_tokens: 74575` for one `ls`. Each fork starts a fresh agent with its own setup, so a fork only pays off when its work would otherwise put much more than that into our conversation.
2. **It ran in the background, and the main agent hedged.** You got a completion notice afterwards, and then the main agent wrote that the result "**most likely means**…". It can't see the fork's work, only the final message. For a report you'll hand to your team, that's a real loss: I couldn't check the tables against the data behind them, or answer "where did this number come from?" without rerunning.

## Effect on the other skills

**Interactive skills can't be forked.** These stop and wait for you partway through:
- `/log-sync` (name approval)
- `/plan-*` (choices)
- `/dev-implement` (one step at a time)
- `/pr-review` and `/pr-address` (decisions)
- `/sprint-init` (template confirmation)

A fork returns one final message, so they have to stay in our conversation. The test doesn't change that.

**Non-interactive skills now could be forked, but there's little reason to.** These are `/pr-preflight`, `/sprint-backlog`, `/sprint-report` and `/dev-checks`.
- **The scripts already shrink their output.** The preflight table is about 1,000 tokens and the backlog audit about 3,000, compared with the 75,000 a fork costs to start.
- **In our conversation, I can check the script's FAIL rows against the real text,** which `/pr-preflight` requires, and answer your follow-ups directly.

## How much does cluttering the main conversation matter?

Moderately. It matters in one situation and hardly at all in the others.

- **Where it matters: long sessions on one issue,** for example `/dev-implement` step after step with `/dev-checks` in between. Raw output adds up fast. A type check or test run can print thousands of lines, and a full `gh` JSON dump with comments can be 20–50 KB. When the conversation fills up, it gets summarized. That happened once in this very session, and detail is lost each time.
- **Where it doesn't:** short skills like `/log-comment` and `/pr-preflight` add 1–5 KB, which is negligible.
- **The weaker effect is distraction:** lots of irrelevant output can blur focus a little. That's hard to measure, and small compared with summarization.
- **The fix is shorter output, not forks.** The scripts already do this. One gap is `/dev-checks`: the type check and unit tests print raw output. I could have it keep only the error lines and a summary count. You keep the transparency, with most of the clutter removed.

## Recommendation for `/sprint-report`

Build it **as a script in our conversation**, like `/pr-preflight`:
- the tables are small;
- I can check them against GitHub before you share them with the team;
- you can rerun the script yourself.

Forking would hide the gathering but cost about 75,000 tokens and prevent me from checking the numbers. If you'd still prefer the fork for this one, it's a one-line change.

**Two follow-ups:**
- Delete the test skill: `rm -r agents/skills/dev-fork-test`.
- Should I build `/sprint-report` as a script in our conversation, and make `/dev-checks` keep only error lines and summary counts?

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```mjs
// Read-only data gathering for /sprint-report (whole team). Only runs `gh issue/pr list|view`,
// `gh api` GETs and read-only git; never edits anything. Run `git fetch origin` first: committed
// logs, diagrams and check-ins are read from origin/main, since teammates' files exist only there.
// Usage: node .claude/course/scripts/report-data.mjs
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";

const config = readFileSync(".claude/course/current-sprint.md", "utf8");
const configValue = (key) => {
  const row = config.split("\n").find((l) => l.startsWith(`| ${key} |`));
  if (!row) throw new Error(`"${key}" row missing from current-sprint.md`);
  return row.split("|")[2].trim().replace(/`/g, "");
};
const repo = configValue("GitHub repo").split(" ")[0];
const milestone = configValue("Milestone");
const previous = configValue("Previous milestone");
const [sprintStart] = configValue("Dates").split(" to ");
const docs = configValue("Docs folder").replace(/\/$/, "");
const logRoot = configValue("AI log folder").replace(/\/$/, "").split("/").slice(0, -1).join("/");
const tag = configValue("Release tag").split(" ")[0];

const sh = (cmd, args) => execFileSync(cmd, args, { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 });
const gh = (...args) => JSON.parse(sh("gh", [...args, "--repo", repo]));
const esc = (s) => String(s ?? "").replace(/\|/g, "\\|").replace(/\r?\n/g, " ");

const issues = gh("issue", "list", "--state", "all", "--milestone", milestone, "--limit", "300", "--json", "number,title,state,assignees,labels,url,createdAt,closedByPullRequestsReferences");
const carry = gh("issue", "list", "--state", "open", "--milestone", previous, "--limit", "300", "--json", "number,title,assignees,url");

// PRs for each issue: GitHub's own link, plus "Closes/Fixes/Resolves #N" in a PR body.
const prCache = new Map();
const prView = (n) => {
  if (!prCache.has(n)) prCache.set(n, gh("pr", "view", String(n), "--json", "number,title,url,state,author,mergedBy,reviews,comments"));
  return prCache.get(n);
};
const recentPrs = gh("pr", "list", "--state", "all", "--limit", "300", "--search", `created:>=${sprintStart}`, "--json", "number,body");
function prsFor(issue) {
  const nums = new Set(issue.closedByPullRequestsReferences.map((p) => p.number));
  const re = new RegExp(`(close[sd]?|fix(e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?)\\s+#${issue.number}\\b`, "i");
  for (const p of recentPrs) if (re.test(p.body || "")) nums.add(p.number);
  return [...nums].sort((a, b) => a - b).map(prView);
}
// Reviewers: anyone other than the author who reviewed or posted the course rubric.
const reviewers = (pr) => [...new Set([
  ...pr.reviews.map((r) => r.author.login),
  ...pr.comments.filter((c) => /code review/i.test(c.body) && /correctness/i.test(c.body)).map((c) => c.author.login),
].filter((l) => l !== pr.author.login))];

const owner = (i) => i.assignees.map((a) => `@${a.login}`).join(", ") || "—";
const effort = (i) => i.labels.map((l) => l.name).find((l) => /^effort:/i.test(l))?.replace(/^effort:/i, "") ?? "—";
const scope = (i) => i.labels.map((l) => l.name).find((l) => /^scope:/i.test(l))?.replace(/^scope:\s*/i, "") ?? "—";

const out = [`# Sprint report data: ${milestone}`, "", `Read-only snapshot. Narrative sections are for the team. Points = the team's \`effort:\` label (no numeric points are recorded on the issues).`, ""];

// Sprint backlog table (template columns: Issue | Owner | Points | Scope | Status)
const status = (i, prs) => {
  if (i.state === "CLOSED") return prs.some((p) => p.state === "MERGED") ? "Done (merged)" : "Closed";
  if (prs.some((p) => p.state === "OPEN")) return "In review";
  if (prs.some((p) => p.state === "MERGED")) return "Merged, issue still open";
  return "Not started / in progress";
};
const withPrs = issues.map((i) => ({ i, prs: prsFor(i) })).sort((a, b) => a.i.number - b.i.number);
out.push("## Sprint backlog table", "", "| Issue | Owner | Points | Scope | Status |", "|---|---|---|---|---|",
  ...withPrs.map(({ i, prs }) => `| [#${i.number}](${i.url}) ${esc(i.title)} | ${owner(i)} | ${effort(i)} | ${scope(i)} | ${status(i, prs)} |`), "");

// Completed issues table (Issue | Owner | PR link | PR author | Reviewer(s) | Status | Description of changes)
const rows = [];
for (const { i, prs } of withPrs) for (const p of prs) {
  const selfMerged = p.mergedBy && p.mergedBy.login === p.author.login ? " ⚠ self-merged" : "";
  rows.push(`| #${i.number} | ${owner(i)} | [#${p.number}](${p.url}) | @${p.author.login} | ${reviewers(p).map((r) => `@${r}`).join(", ") || "**none**"} | ${p.state.toLowerCase()}${selfMerged} | ${esc(p.title)} |`);
}
out.push("## Completed issues table (all PRs linked to milestone issues)", "", "The description column holds the PR title as a starting point for the team.", "",
  "| Issue | Owner | PR link | PR author | Reviewer(s) | Status | Description of changes |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|", ...(rows.length ? rows : ["| (no PRs yet) | | | | | | |"]), "");

// Carryovers: previous milestone's open issues, and milestone issues created before this sprint began.
const older = issues.filter((i) => i.createdAt.slice(0, 10) < sprintStart);
out.push("## Carryover facts", "", `Still open in ${previous} (not moved): ${carry.map((i) => `[#${i.number}](${i.url}) ${esc(i.title)} (${owner(i)})`).join("; ") || "none"}.`, "",
  `In ${milestone} but created before ${sprintStart} (likely carried over or pulled from the backlog; confirm): ${older.map((i) => `#${i.number}`).join(", ") || "none"}.`, "");

// Committed course files on origin/main.
let committed = [];
try {
  committed = sh("git", ["ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", "origin/main", "--", `${logRoot}/`, `${docs}/`]).split(/\r?\n/).filter((f) => f && !f.endsWith(".gitkeep"));
} catch {}
const members = [...new Set([...issues.flatMap((i) => i.assignees.map((a) => a.login)), ...committed.filter((f) => f.startsWith(`${logRoot}/`)).map((f) => f.split("/")[2])])].sort();

const logRow = (m) => {
  const logs = committed.filter((f) => f.startsWith(`${logRoot}/${m}/`) && /\.(md|txt|json)$/.test(f) && f.split("/").length === 4);
  const tools = [...new Set(logs.map((f) => (f.split("/").pop().match(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}_([^_]+)_/) || [])[1]).filter(Boolean))];
  return `| @${m} | ${tools.join(", ") || "—"} | ${logs.length} | \`${logRoot}/${m}/\` | |`;
};
out.push("## AI tool usage table (committed logs on origin/main)", "", "| Member | Tools used | Sessions logged | Log folder | What worked / what you'd change |", "|---|---|---|---|---|", ...members.map(logRow), "",
  "Logs that exist only locally or on unmerged branches are not counted.", "");

const filesFor = (dir) => members.map((m) => {
  const files = committed.filter((f) => f.startsWith(`${docs}/${dir}/`) && f.split("/").pop().includes(m));
  return `- @${m}: ${files.length ? files.map((f) => `[${f.split("/").pop()}](https://github.com/${repo}/blob/main/${f})`).join(", ") : "**none on main**"}`;
});
out.push("## UML diagrams (D6) on main", "", ...filesFor("diagrams"), "", "## Mid-sprint check-ins (D7) on main", "", ...filesFor("checkin"), "");

// Release
let tagExists = false;
try {
  tagExists = sh("git", ["ls-remote", "--tags", "origin", `refs/tags/${tag}`]).trim().length > 0;
} catch {}
let release = null;
try {
  release = JSON.parse(sh("gh", ["api", `repos/${repo}/releases/tags/${tag}`]));
} catch {}
out.push("## Release", "", `Tag \`${tag}\`: ${tagExists ? "exists" : "**not created yet**"}. GitHub release: ${release ? `[${release.name || tag}](${release.html_url})` : "**not created yet**"}.`);

console.log(out.join("\n"));

```

```mjs
// Runs one of two fixed checks and prints only the error lines and summary counts, so the
// conversation isn't filled with thousands of lines. The full output is saved to a log file
// so any error can still be looked at in context. Edits nothing else.
// Usage:
//   node .claude/course/scripts/run-check.mjs typecheck <package>        e.g. @calcom/features
//   node .claude/course/scripts/run-check.mjs vitest <test file> [...]
// Only these two commands can run, so pre-approving this script is safe.
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

const [kind, ...targets] = process.argv.slice(2);
const MAX_LINES = 40;
let args;
let env = { ...process.env };
if (kind === "typecheck" && targets.length === 1 && /^@?[\w./-]+$/.test(targets[0])) {
  // yarn type-check:ci is broken on this Windows machine (spawn tsc ENOENT); this is the working form.
  args = ["turbo", "run", "type-check", `--filter=${targets[0]}`, "--force"];
} else if (kind === "vitest" && targets.length && targets.every((t) => /^[\w./@()[\] -]+$/.test(t))) {
  // .env sets NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E=1 for E2E, which makes some unit tests fail by design.
  env = { ...env, NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E: "", TZ: "UTC" };
  args = ["vitest", "run", ...targets];
} else {
  console.error("Usage: run-check.mjs typecheck <package>  |  run-check.mjs vitest <test file> [...]");
  process.exit(2);
}

const started = Date.now();
// shell is needed on Windows to find yarn.cmd; arguments were validated above.
const run = spawnSync("yarn", args.map((a) => (/\s/.test(a) ? `"${a}"` : a)), { env, encoding: "utf8", shell: true, maxBuffer: 512 * 1024 * 1024 });
const full = `${run.stdout ?? ""}\n${run.stderr ?? ""}`;
// Strip terminal colour codes so the patterns below match.
const plain = full.replace(/\u001b\[[0-9;]*m/g, "");
mkdirSync(".claude/work/checks", { recursive: true });
const logFile = `.claude/work/checks/${kind}-${new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, "-")}.log`;
writeFileSync(logFile, plain);

const lines = plain.split(/\r?\n/);
const unique = (xs) => [...new Set(xs.map((l) => l.trim()))];
let errors = [];
let summary = [];
if (kind === "typecheck") {
  // tsc errors look like: path/file.ts(12,5): error TS2322: Type 'x' is not assignable ...
  errors = unique(lines.filter((l) => /error TS\d+:/.test(l)).map((l) => l.replace(/^\S+:type-check:\s*/, "")));
  summary = [`${errors.length} type error(s)`, ...unique(lines.filter((l) => /Tasks:|Failed:|ERR_PNPM|command .* exited/.test(l)))];
} else {
  errors = unique(lines.filter((l) => /^\s*(FAIL|×|✗)\s|AssertionError|Error:|^\s*❯ .*:\d+:\d+/.test(l)));
  summary = unique(lines.filter((l) => /^\s*(Test Files|Tests|Duration)\s/.test(l)));
}

console.log(`${kind} ${targets.join(" ")}: exit ${run.status} in ${Math.round((Date.now() - started) / 1000)}s`);
console.log(summary.join("\n") || "(no summary line found — see the full log)");
if (errors.length) {
  console.log(`\nError lines (${errors.length}${errors.length > MAX_LINES ? `, first ${MAX_LINES}` : ""}):`);
  console.log(errors.slice(0, MAX_LINES).join("\n"));
}
console.log(`\nFull output: ${logFile}  (search it for context: grep -n -A5 "<error text>" ${logFile})`);
process.exit(run.status ?? 1);

```

## Naming: type a prefix to see a group

Skills in `.claude/skills/` can't be put in folders or categories, so related skills share a name prefix. Typing the prefix in the `/` menu shows just that group.

| Type | Group | Skills |
|---|---|---|
| `/find` | Help | `/find` |
| `/log-` | AI logs | `/log-sync`, `/log-comment` |
| `/plan-` | Before code | `/plan-estimate`, `/plan-spec`, `/plan-design` |
| `/dev-` | Writing and understanding code | `/dev-implement`, `/dev-checks`, `/dev-explain`, `/dev-uml` |
| `/pr-` | Pull requests | `/pr-draft`, `/pr-preflight`, `/pr-review`, `/pr-address` |
| `/sprint-` | Sprint setup and housekeeping | `/sprint-init`, `/sprint-backlog`, `/sprint-checkin`, `/sprint-report`, `/sprint-release` |

Renamed from the course prompt: `/estimate` → `/plan-estimate`, `/spec` → `/plan-spec`, `/design` → `/plan-design`, `/implement` → `/dev-implement`, `/checks` → `/dev-checks`, `/explain` → `/dev-explain`, `/uml` → `/dev-uml`, `/preflight` → `/pr-preflight`, `/review-pr` → `/pr-review`, `/address-review` → `/pr-address`, `/backlog` → `/sprint-backlog`, `/checkin` → `/sprint-checkin`, `/release-notes` → `/sprint-release`.

## Rules every skill follows

1. **No git or GitHub writes, ever. You do these by hand.** Skills never commit, push, create or switch branches, stash, merge, rebase, reset, tag, open PRs, post or edit issue/PR comments, review/approve/merge PRs, or change labels, milestones or releases. Instead they give you:
   - draft markdown: PR descriptions, issue bodies, comments, review rubrics, release notes;
   - draft commit messages;
   - the exact commands to run yourself, each with a one-line note on what it does.

   This is also **enforced** by 116 deny rules in `.claude/settings.local.json` (Bash and PowerShell), so these commands fail if anything tries to run them. You still run them in your own terminal. Because `git branch` is blocked, skills read the branch with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`; tags are read with `git ls-remote --tags origin`.
2. **Read-only git and `gh` are allowed** to gather facts: `git status/diff/log/show/fetch`, `gh issue view/list`, `gh pr view/list/diff/checks`, and `gh api` reads.
3. **Local files are allowed:** drafts and notes under `.claude/work/`, copies of logs into `ai-logs/…`, diagram and check-in files under `docs/…`. These only reach GitHub when you commit and push them.
4. **Templates:** fill the repo's original GitHub template first, then add every course-required field. Course templates marked *verbatim* keep their exact wording.
5. **Never edit AI log contents.** Logs are only copied and renamed.
6. **Review scores stay blank** for you to fill in; skills write only the Notes.
7. **Story points are suggestions** for planning poker.
8. **Every code claim cites `file:line`** and is marked Confirmed or Unverified. Every rule says where it comes from: course, team, or `AGENTS.md`.
9. **Commands use Git Bash syntax** and the verified commands in `setup-notes.md`. E2E tests and the dev server are always yours to run.
10. **Your questions are answered in the main conversation**, never handed to background agents.

It proposes slugs for your approval and creates attachment folders.
